He retired?''"
"''Quite suddenly. He tried to rascal Black Sun for more credits on a delivery for which there was an agreed-upon contract. That was… unwise.|Guri, giving Boushh's outfit to Leia Organa|[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]}} '''Boushh''' was a successful [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Ubese/Legends|Ubese]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] active around the time of the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Known for his melee skills and penchant for [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]], Boushh was considered cool-headed in a profession often filled with trigger-happy [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], and operated as a freelancer traveling from [[Star system/Legends|system]] to system looking for work. He wore a suit of customized Ubese armor—layers of brown survival material and an optically enhanced helmet which both provided him with protection and obscured his identity. Although he made sure to never officially join the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]] but unofficially he still worked for them and also worked with Cradossk, Boushh worked for [[Crimson Nova]], a sect of the Guild dedicated to hunting fugitive [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. During the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], he helped hunt [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kai Justiss]] alongside bounty hunters [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[Breela]]. After that, Boushh began to work mainly for [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], the largest criminal syndicate in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], he was sent to hunt down [[Kodo Finn|Kodo]] and [[Aleema Finn]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], but was intercepted by Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]]. Lo'gaan and Boushh fought, but ultimately allied together when hordes of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] raided the building. Lo'gaan escaped and Boushh was apprehended, but he was later released. Many years later, around [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Boushh captured a [[Unidentified Nimbanel|Nimbanel]] for Black Sun, but in doing so spent a considerable amount of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. He bartered with Xizor for a 50 percent greater payment; this was a mistake, as Xizor, feeling Boushh was becoming a hindrance, had his [[Human replica droid]], [[Guri]], kill the Ubese. Boushh's trademark armor was later used by [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] on missions to infiltrate Coruscant and [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. ==Biography== ===Boushh the bounty hunter=== [[File:Boushh_SWE.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Boushh masked]] Boushh was an [[Ubese/Legends|Ubese]] from [[Uba IV/Legends|Uba IV]]''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' who joined the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]] profession early in his life, proving a keen combatant and expert hunter. Although he was slight of build, Boushh wore a suit of "armor," which consisted of layers upon layers of brown survival clothing, and an optically enhanced helmet; this helped mold his reputation as a formidable and dangerous hunter. He acquired a horde of facial scars from his adventures,''[[Evasive Action: Prey]]'' though because he hardly ever took off his mask in public, few ever saw them. Boushh trusted no one, and often kept tabs on his employers, looking for information he could use against them should they attempt to betray him. He made few alliances during his time as a bounty hunter; he roamed the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], working for various different employers, rarely staying with one for more than a few months. He did, however, work alongside several other hunters on occasion, such as the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Snoova]], and [[Beylyssa]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] female. Beylyssa and Boushh both shared a love of explosives, but their partnership ended violently—neither of them was badly injured, though. Rumors abounded that Boushh sent much of his profits on to other struggling Ubese bounty hunters. It was surmised by many of his fellow bounty hunters that he was part of a network of elite Ubese mercenary units. However, these rumors were never proved and their accuracy was doubted by many. Boushh also worked as part of [[Crimson Nova]]—a subset of [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]] dedicated to hunting down [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] survivors of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]—for a time, and hunted [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kai Justiss]] on [[Garqi/Legends|Garqi]] alongside fellow hunters [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[Breela]] at some point. Boushh's work with the group was limited, though, and he refused to properly join the Guild. ===Working for Xizor=== {{Quote|They belonged to Boushh, an Ubese bounty hunter. Boushh was quite good at the trade. He did a lot of contract work for Black Sun. He… retired recently.|Guri|}} [[File:DrakeSurrounded.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Boushh and Lo'gaan fight off the stormtroopers]] Boushh occasionally worked for [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], one of the largest criminal syndicates in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], though he was not formally tied to the organization. In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], he was hired by [[Kreet'ah]], a subordinate of the high-ranking [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]] known as [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], to kill two [[Omwati/Legends|Omwati]], [[Kodo Finn|Kodo]] and [[Aleema Finn]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. The two Finns had seemingly defeated a trio of Xizor's agents, and he wished them dealt with quietly and efficiently. Boushh infiltrated the Omwatis' abode, destroying a security guard and using a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] to blast away the outer wall. He was met by [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]], a fugitive Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] and a friend of the Finns. The two faced off for a time while another Jedi, [[Zonder/Legends|Zonder]], fled with Kodo and Aleema Finn. Lo'gaan demanded to know why Black Sun wanted to kill the Finns, though Boushh did not answer him. Eventually, their fight was interrupted—to the duo's surprise and fear—by a group of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. With a common enemy, Boushh and Lo'gaan began to work together against the stormtroopers, fighting back-to-back. Eventually, however, Boushh's twin [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] were carried through the air by [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] by Imperial [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] [[Antinnis Tremayne]], who had just arrived. Lo'gaan was able to flee, though Boushh was left defenseless against over a dozen stormtroopers, Tremayne, and his fellow Inquisitor [[Lanu Pasiq]]. Tremayne believed that Boushh was in fact Lo'gaan's associate and fellow Jedi, [[Ekria/Legends|Ekria]], in disguise, though he was disappointed to learn what was truly under the mask. Boushh was allowed to leave, and he returned to inform Xizor personally of his failure to kill the Finns. Some time after Boushh returned to Xizor's headquarters, Lo'gaan, Zonder, Ekria, and the Finns arrived to plead with Xizor for their lives. Xizor agreed, for a price, and the two Omwati were allowed to flee to the Outer Rim. ===Other hunts=== {{Quote|In certain operations, I've found it useful to leverage the relatives of the target.|Boushh|}} Some time later, Boushh was hired to protect [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]] [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] [[Narloch]], who had a hefty bounty on his head for theft and fraud, from a group of bounty hunters. Boushh guarded Narloch while he gambled in a [[Casino/Legends|casino]] on [[The Wheel/Legends|the Wheel]], where they were attacked by the bounty hunters. They fled to [[Dalos IV]], though they were pursued; Boushh enlisted the help of several other [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] in order to protect Narloch, laying traps and explosives for his enemies. The pursuers managed to make their way to Dalos IV, where Boushh engaged them in a firefight in the hopes of allowing Narloch to escape. Instead, Boushh eventually fled, and Narloch was captured.[[No Disintegrations (West End Games)|''No Disintegrations'']][[No Disintegrations (West End Games)|''No Disintegrations'']] is a roleplaying game adventure, so the exact nature of the events are vague. Boushh is supposed to be used as an antagonist by gamemasters at various points in the game, though because he needed to survive for the events of the ''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]'', ''No Disintegrations'' states that if he is captured or killed, it is revealed that it is an impostor, and not the real Boushh. At some point during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Boushh was hired by [[Administrator/Legends|Administrator]] [[Lenc]] to capture [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]]-allied arms dealer [[Praaelon Di]], after Di sold arms to both sides of a rebellion on Lenc's mining colony on [[Weldii III]]. Boushh researched Di before making a move, and learned that the gunrunner had a number of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] and [[LM-432 crab droid/Legends|LM-432 crab droids]] at his disposal; thus, Boushh hired a number of other bounty hunters to assist him in the hunt. Boushh assembled the team with their abilities in mind, and the end result was that he had a group capable of countering Di's powerful droids. The bounty hunters clashed with Di aboard his ship, the ''[[Tri-Sun]]'', with Di coming out on top.{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/unfinished2|text=Unfinished Business, Part 2: Well-Armed and Dangerous|int=Unfinished Business (scenario)}} Boushh then traveled to [[Mine Shaft 342]], Weldii III, where Lenc was overseeing repairs to his mine. Di, with more forces, including Rebel allies, arrived to kill Lenc; Boushh hoped to execute part of the bounty on the arms dealer. However, Praaelon Di was ultimately successful in his efforts, and Boushh did not capture him.{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/unfinished3|text=Unfinished Business, Part 3: Shafted!|int=Unfinished Business (scenario)}} [[File:Boushh-BetweenTheShadows.png|thumb|left|200px|Boushh wielding a force pike]] Sometime after the [[battle of Talus]] Boushh was tracking [[Corellian Security Force]] operative [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] from the [[Emperor's Most Wanted]], a list of high-paid bounties on important Alliance leaders. He was assisted by another bounty hunter, both agreed that using a direct approach in apprehending Horn would be difficult, Horn was difficult to ambush and even more difficult to deceive. Once the two agreed that Boushh would collect the bounty, he offered to capture Corran's father, [[Hal Horn]], and lure Horn into a trap. The bounty hunters captured the elder Horn and moved him to a secure location, which was soon ambushed by Corran and several other CorSec operatives. However, Boushh's perimeter security alarm gave the bounty hunters the critical seconds necessary to withstand the initial assault, and the battle soon turned into a standoff. The bounty hunters offered to let the elder Horn go if Corran would turn himself over to them. Refusing to allow harm to come to his father, Corran agreed to the ultimatum, allowing Boushh to cuff and capture himself.{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Dark Side scenario campaign}} ===Demise=== {{Quote|This bounty hunter is my kind of scum… fearless and inventive.|translated=1|Jabba the Hutt, to Organa, in Boushh's armor|{{Film|VI}}}} [[File:Boushh-The_Dark_Times.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Boushh in the time of the Empire]] Boushh continued to work as a freelancer for several years, though by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], he frequently worked for Black Sun, contacted by agents such as [[Chorh-dha]], [[Vimriss]] and other underlings of the [[Vigo/Legends|vigo]] [[Green]], who had criminal interests in that region of space. Per his usual practice, Boushh tried to spy on those agents and probe on their contacts, superiors, and the wider context of their interests, something that was undesireable for the secretive organization.{{WEGCite|story=Bounty's Due|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}} He blackmailed a vigo during this time, which earned him Xizor's ire.[[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']] In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Chorh-dha hired him to capture a [[Unidentified Nimbanel|Nimbanel]] enemy of Black Sun; he succeeded, but to his usual practice, Boushh contacted Black Sun claiming that the hunt ultimately cost him greatly, for he had to use much equipment and technology to capture his quarry; he requested that he be paid 50 percent extra, to which Xizor agreed. Boushh was staying with the Nimbanel in an old [[Cargo container/Legends|cargo container]] serving as a hovel in the muddy streets of [[Gelgelar/Legends|Gelgelar]] waiting for Chorh-dha. Xizor's [[Human replica droid]], [[Guri]], showed up in the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]]'s place and presented him with a metal case supposedly filled with [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. Ever paranoid, Boushh frisked Guri, finding no weapons, though he refused to open the case; he wanted her to open it, so that he could keep his blaster trained on her permanently. Guri obliged, and Boushh began to search through the credit chips, but he was momentarily incapacitated when a hidden [[Dinko (creature)|dinko]] bit him. Guri took this opportunity to kick Boushh in the face, snapping his neck. Boushh had crossed the line with Black Sun, with both his demands for extra payment and his blackmailing of a vigo. Guri picked up Boushh's body, and the Nimbanel captive, back to Xizor. Few knew of his death, though, which would later be used to others' advantage. [[File:Leia_boush2.jpg|thumb|left|200px| Leia Organa disguised as the bounty hunter Boushh.]] Some time later, Guri gave [[Boushh's armor]] to a leading member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], on [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]], so that she could infiltrate Coruscant to meet with [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]]. The suit fit Organa perfectly, and she and her friend [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]—disguised as Snoova, Boushh's old partner—used it to get onto Coruscant without arousing suspicion. Organa kept the armor for use on later missions; in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], she once again disguised herself as Boushh and brought Chewbacca to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'']] During her time disguised as Boushh, she also participated in [[Jabba's demolition games]], riding a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]].''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]'' Organa could speak [[Ubese (language)/Legends|Ubese]], and because the mask concealed her true appearance, none suspected her deception. After she was captured, however, the armor was discarded by Jabba's minions. Despite this, few knew of Organa's ruse, and many suspected that Boushh was not dead, but merely retired. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Chorh-dha thought it would be better to send me. Someone you might trust more.''"
[Laughs] "''Yo czhal.|Guri and Boushh|}} [[File:Boushh.png|thumb|right|200px|Boushh in his signature outfit, without helmet]] Boushh was paranoid and cautious to a fault, and always planned for and expected the worst. He trusted no one, expecting to be backstabbed, cheated, taken advantage of, and lied to at every turn. Boushh allied with no organization, moved on to a new employer every few months; he spent great deals of time searching for information both on his prey as well as his employers, anticipating counter-moves. As for his employers, he hoped to find incriminating items; should someone attempt to deny him his due payment, he would blackmail and threaten them until they paid up. This led partially to his downfall; one of the reasons Xizor had him killed was that the Ubese hunter was blackmailing a Black Sun vigo. Boushh cared more about his own life than money, and he had no qualms about turning down a bounty offer which would put him in any considerable danger, even for immense sums of money.''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]'' When hired by Narloch, Boushh left the Herglic gambler for dead when he fled Dalos IV, demonstrating that he cared more for his own skin than fulfilling his mission. Boushh was also notorious for often demanding extra credits after successfully capturing a bounty; he claimed that this was because he had used resources, such as high quality equipment, in tracking them down, though this was often exaggerated. Like most members of his [[Species/Legends|species]], Boushh had a fascination with technology of all sorts. He was known to use a wide array of small, easily concealable gadgets while pursuing quarry, and had a love of all things explosive. He used explosives to make an impression, and played to his reputation for appearing somewhat suicidal, hoping that his targets would give themselves up in the erroneous knowledge that Boushh would blow himself up in order to take others down with him. However, he was also talented at close-quarters combat, and often used small blades during his work. Boushh was known to be a fearless and inventive bounty hunter,{{CCG|set=Enhanced Jabba's Palace|cardname=Boushh}} cool and calculating in a profession of trigger-happy freelancers. ==Equipment== [[File:Boushh_BotF_by_Bradbury.png|thumb|left|210px|Boushh with a blaster rifle]] Boushh wore a suit of customized "[[Ubese raider armor|armor]]," incorporating the traditional Ubese [[Ogygian cloak/Legends|Ogygian cloak]]. He wore many layers of rough survival clothing, light brown in color, with spiked, metal armor on his shoulders, neck, and wrists. [[Shata leather pants/Legends|Shata leather pants]] covered his legs, with traditional cream-colored Ubese boots. Boushh wore several bandoleers, packed tight with small [[ammo pouch]]es that hold explosives—projectile detonators, [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash]] and [[Stun grenade/Legends|stun grenades]], [[Computer surge exploder plug]]s, intricate [[Timer bomb|detonation timers]] and [[Plasma-burn tape]]s, and [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]]—around his chest, and an [[Ubese clan belt-clasp/Legends|Ubese clan belt-clasp]] around his waist.''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' Boushh's helmet allowed him to breathe [[Atmosphere/Legends|Type I atmospheres]]; without it, such atmospheres would damage his lungs. The helmet also contained an [[Audio sensor/Legends|audio pickup]] and [[Broadband antenna/Legends|broadband antenna]],''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]'' a speech scrambler, an optically enhanced vision scanner, and a flash guard visor, which nullified the effect of any [[Stun grenade/Legends|stun grenades]]. Boushh always carried numerous weapons with him: a [[Force pike/Legends|force pike]], a [[Lance/Legends|lance-blade]], a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]], and a pair of melee swords. He was also known to utilize an [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaff]].{{HasbroCite|set=Saga Legends|pack=Princess Leia (Boushh Disguise)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TACSLleiaboushh.asp}}{{SW|url=news/exclusive-star-wars-collectibles-at-san-diego-comic-con|text=Exclusive ''Star Wars'' Collectibles at San Diego Comic-Con}} ==Behind the scenes== Boushh was created for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] in [[1983]]. He first "appeared" in [[James Kahn]]'s [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novel adaptation]] of the film; it is not revealed until after Boushh's first scene in ''Return of the Jedi'' that he is in fact Leia Organa in disguise. Boushh's costume appeared again in the ''Return of the Jedi'' film, though, unlike in the novel, his name was never given. He was voiced by [[Pat Welsh]] in ''Return of the Jedi''. Boushh has been used infrequently for a movie character, only making a handful of other appearances. Boushh was not referenced again until [[1996]], when [[Steve Perry]] used the character for his novel ''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'' to explain how Leia got his armor. The ''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]'' expanded his backstory. Several reasons are given for Boushh's death; ''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'' simply says that he "made the mistake of withholding credits on a job for the syndicate".''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'' The concurrent ''Sourcebook'' (1996) says that he demanded a higher payment, while the much later [[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']] ([[2008]]) says that he blackmailed a vigo. Leia Organa, wearing Boushh's armor, is one of the playable characters in the [[2000]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''. However, unlike the majority of the characters developed for the game, a winning and losing cutscene for Leia were not added for the character. [[Paul Ens]]'s ''[[Evasive Action: Prey]]''—which contains the first image of an unmasked Boushh—is the only narrative [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] source the character has appeared in alive. {{Quote|We have been called criminals, but we are not. We are rebels. Fighting for the people. Fighting for you.|Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Call to Action">{{Rebels|Call to Action}}</ref>}}
'''Ezra Bridger''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]], a [[Spectres|freedom fighter]], and a revolutionary leader in the [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|early rebellion]] against the [[Galactic Empire]]. He was [[Reproduction|born]] on [[Empire Day]] in [[19 BBY]] to [[Ephraim Bridger|Ephraim]] and [[Mira Bridger]]. His parents' public criticism of the Empire led to their [[Prisoner|imprisonment]], leaving Bridger an orphan on the [[planet]] [[Lothal]] as a [[Youngling|child]]. He joined the rebel crew of the ''[[Ghost]]'' in [[5 BBY]] and was [[Jedi training|trained]] in the ways of [[the Force]] by [[Kanan Jarrus]]. With a particular [[Taming beasts|connection to nature and other living beings]], Bridger's [[Force power|abilities]] grew quickly, and a [[Ezra's broadcast|message of hope]] he broadcast in the [[Lothal sector]] inspired a number of rebel cells to begin working together to fight the Empire.

In [[4 BBY]], Bridger learned that his [[parent]]s were [[Death|killed]] while attempting to [[Revolt in an Imperial prison|escape]] from [[prison]]. The young Jedi, already having to struggle with the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]], became more conflicted, [[Mission to Malachor|coming to a head]] on the ancient [[Sith]] world of [[Malachor]] where he recovered a [[Sith holocron]] in the hopes of destroying the Sith. He also encountered the former [[Sith Lord]] [[Maul]], who hoped to make Bridger his apprentice—particularly once Bridger used the dark side to open the [[holocron]]. This briefly strained his apprenticeship with Jarrus, who was blinded by Maul on Malachor, but the two repaired their relationship and continued to progress as Jedi.

With his powers growing stronger, especially his natural skill at communicating with other living beings, Bridger took on more leadership roles in the rebellion, including [[Mission to Agamar (2 BBY)|helping]] [[Captain]] [[Rex|CT-7567]] "Rex" and a surviving [[battalion]] of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist Alliance]] [[battle droid]]s make peace and bring a sense of closure to the unresolved [[Clone Wars]]. Bridger also came into [[Lothal campaign|conflict]] with [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], helped fellow crewmate [[Sabine Wren]] in her quest to reunite the [[Mandalorian]] people, and sought to find [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], whom Bridger believed was key to destroying the Sith.

In [[1 BBY]], Bridger managed to free his people from the Empire's control during the [[Liberation of Lothal]] with the help of the [[Purrgil]]. Towards the end of the battle, he and Thrawn were taken into [[hyperspace]] by the purrgil. This opening allowed the [[Lothal resistance group]] on the ground to free the planet by destroying the [[Imperial Complex (Lothal)|Imperial dome]]. After the [[Battle of Jakku|fall]] of the Empire, Wren and [[Ahsoka Tano]] set off on a [[Quest to find Ezra Bridger|journey]] to find Bridger and bring him home.

After almost a decade of being stranded on the planet [[Peridea]] in another galaxy, Ezra reunited with Sabine and Ahsoka as they came to Peridea alongside a [[Morgan Elsbeth's forces|force]] that were looking for Thrawn. After Thrawn successfully escaped Peridea on his [[Star Destroyer]] the ''[[Chimaera]]'', Ezra escaped too by hitching a ride on it, albeit at the cost of leaving Sabine and Ahsoka behind.

==Biography==
===Childhood===
====Child under the Empire====
{{Quote|I've been on my own since I was seven, okay? If I'd let myself believe my folks were alive, if I let myself believe they'd come back and save me, I'd never have learned how to survive.|Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Gathering Forces">{{Rebels|Gathering Forces}}</ref>}}
[[File:Bridger_family.png|thumb|left|180px|A young Ezra with his parents]]
Ezra Bridger was [[Reproduction|born]] in 3258 [[Lothal Calendar|LY]],<ref name="SWR:TVG" /> on the [[Empire Day|day]] of the [[Proclamation of the New Order|inception]] of the [[Galactic Empire]],<ref name="Meet Ezra">{{SWYouTube|lw-YfJetY18|Meet Ezra, the Street-Smart Hero | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-meet-ezra-the-street-smart-hero}}</ref><ref name="Empire Day" /> and grew up on the [[planet]] [[Lothal]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. Hoping to make the galaxy a better place for him, his [[parent]]s [[Mira Bridger|Mira]] and [[Ephraim Bridger]] set up public broadcasting transmissions to speak out against the Empire's harsh rule<ref name="SWR:TVG" /> in [[14 BBY]]<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> The Bridgers' anti-Imperial activities began years earlier, around [[18 BBY]]<ref name="Timeline">In ''[[Adventures in Wild Space: The Steal]]'', Ezra Bridger is an infant. Since Ezra was born on the first [[Empire Day]] (which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' cites as [[19 BBY]]), the ''[[Star Wars: Adventures in Wild Space]]'' series (the books of which take place in close proximity to each other) must be set around [[18 BBY]].</ref> when Ezra was only an infant and his [[parent]]s gave shelter to [[Lina Graf|Lina]] and [[Milo Graf]], a pair of [[Youngling|children]] whose own [[Rhyssa Graf|mother]] and [[Auric Graf|father]] were abducted by the Empire. While the Graf children were in the [[Bridger family]] home, the infant Ezra's giggles drew the attention of Milo, who presented him with his finger to hold and commented that the baby was cute. According to Mira, at that age Ezra was cute when he was not screaming, which he was prone to doing as a baby.<ref name="Adventures in Wild Space: The Steal">''[[Adventures in Wild Space: The Steal]]''</ref>

Over the course of his early childhood, Ezra came to know multiple acquaintances of his parents, including the [[Rodian]] [[Tseebo]]<ref name="Empire Day" /> and Lothal [[Governor]] [[Ryder Azadi]].<ref name="Legacy">{{Rebels|Legacy (episode)}}</ref> At the same time, his parents continued their broadcasts encouraging resistance against the Empire, however this would eventually cost them their own lives. By [[12 BBY]], his parents were found and taken away by the Empire,<ref name="SWR:TVG" /> leaving Ezra to live largely on his own for the next eight years and find work as a [[con artist]] and thief, stealing technology and reselling it on the black market, while unknowingly using [[the Force]] to occasionally get himself out of tough situations.<ref name="Meet Ezra" /><ref name="Property">{{Rebels|Property of Ezra Bridger}}</ref> Eventually, he would come to live in the abandoned [[LothalNet comm tower E-272]], where he would keep a collection of stormtrooper helmets.<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Spark of Rebellion">{{Rebels|Spark of Rebellion}}</ref><ref name="Ezra's Gamble">''[[Ezra's Gamble]]''</ref> Bridger scraped by best he could, such as by engaging in theft when needed.<ref name="Born Rebel">{{InsiderCite|227|Born to Rebel}}</ref> 

Bridger would later be apprenticed to a [[Xexto]] named [[Ferpil Wallaway]], who was the owner of a [[Wallaway's Pawn Shop|pawn shop]] in Lothal as well as a skilled pickpocket who had various underworld connections. The Xexto taught the boy everything he knew, and they would try to pick each other clean for fun. The boy worked for him, doing jobs like scamming wealthy-looking tourists and trick them and selling them stuff. Bridger would also befriend [[Moreena Krai]], a girl of the same age as him, who knew of his under-handed skills. Although he was unaware of his [[Force-sensitive|Force-sensitivity]],<ref name="Ezra's Gamble" /> he shared a natural bond with nature and thus was able to easily connect with other living-beings, particularly animals.<ref name="The Call Rebels Recon">{{RebelsRecon|cto9_9qNHZ0|#2.14: Inside "The Call" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-the-call}}</ref>

====Gladiator night====
{{Quote|I hate to say so, Mr. Bossk, but I have a bad feeling about this.|Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Ezra's Gamble" />}}
[[File:Ezra_and_Bossk.jpg|thumb|300px|right|Ezra briefly was hired as a guide by Bossk.]]
One day at [[Capital City]]'s [[Capital City spaceport|spaceport]], Bridger was selling tickets for a [[Gladiator Night]] between a [[Houk]] and [[Feeorin]] when Krai told him her family and her were leaving for [[Alderaan]] to live with [[Moreena Krai's grandmother|her grandmother]] due to the Empire, and bade farewell to the boy. Later that day, Bridger caught sight of the ''[[Hound's Tooth]]'' and met [[Trandoshan]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]], who hired him as a guide to [[Ake's Tavern]]. As they reached their destination, Bossk sent Bridger instead to lure his prey, [[Gronson Takkaro|Gronson "Shifty" Takkaro]], out; soon enough, however, a confrontation between Bossk and the [[assassin]]s [[Angrigo]] and the [[Unidentified Kratchell twin (blaster pistols)|Kratchell]] [[Unidentified Kratchell twin (disruptor rifle)|twins]] ensued, in which Bridger [[stun]]ned Takkaro, and Bossk killed the assassins, only for Imperial authorities to surround them. Aware of a likely set-up by [[Lieutenant]] [[Herdringer]], Bossk was forced to leave Takkaro and follow Bridger, and the two escaped from the Imperials on a [[speeder bike]]. During their escape, however, Bossk was injured and convinced Bridger to help him by offering the boy all the content of his strongbox onboard the ''Tooth''.<ref name="Ezra's Gamble" />

In the course of an hour, Bridger took the Trandoshan to his tower and tended to his wounds, before the bounty hunter woke up, "disguised" himself as a blind Trandoshan and almost immediately prompted Bridger into leading him to a posting agency at the [[spaceport]], where he accessed the [[Imperial Enforcement DataCore]] to check records on Herdringer. However, they discovered Herdringer had been dead for months, and Bossk surmised that his replacement, [[Jenkes]], had been the one to set him up, now also aware that he and Takkaro had worked together in [[Nyriaan gladiator arena|gladiator arena]] in [[Nyriaan]] years before. Their search, though, attracted Jenkes' attention, who sent troopers to attack them, but Bridger and Bossk managed to slip away again, and they went to Wallaway's pawn shop, where they saw from afar as Jenkes shot Wallaway and took his money.<ref name="Ezra's Gamble" />

Once Jenkes left the shop, Bridger and Bossk entered the place, only for Wallaway to die on Bridger's arms. Convinced by Bossk, he accompanied the Trandoshan to [[Monad Outpost]] during Gladiator Night, where they faced Jenkes. During the confrontation, Bridger used his stolen Imperial comlink to alert Jenkes' superiors, while Bossk told everyone on the arena of Jenkes' actions. Bridger, then, proceeded to stun the Imperial before he could flee the arena, just before Imperial forces arrived and swarmed the arena. The next morning, as promised, Bossk gave Bridger the contents of his strongbox, which turned out to be just seventy-five credits, and the Trandoshan bade him farewell.<ref name="Ezra's Gamble" />

On his way home, Bridger was walking through the fields around his tower when a [[Ghost|freighter]] shot down a TIE fighter, which crashed not far from him. As Ezra rushed to the wreck and encountered [[Baron of the Empire|Baron]] [[Valen Rudor]],<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Ezra's Gamble" /> who thought himself to be better than the boy<ref name="Ezra Pilot">''[[Ezra and the Pilot]]''</ref> and rebuked Bridger for touching the starfighter<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Ezra's Gamble" /> instead of thanking the boy for his help.<ref name="Ezra Pilot" /> After successfully opening the top of the cockpit, Bridger hopped inside and managed to trick the unlucky pilot into thinking he was helping get his armor unstuck when, in fact, he was actually stealing bits of equipment<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Ezra's Gamble" /> to sell on the black market<ref name="Born Rebel" /> and teach Rudor a lesson for his rudeness.<ref name="Ezra Pilot" /> After grabbing Rudor's [[helmet]] for his collection<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Ezra's Gamble" /> and to sell the tech within,<ref name="Born Rebel" /> Bridger quickly left the wreckage, while revealing his thievish intentions.<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Ezra's Gamble" />

Rudor, not meaning to be outsmarted by the child, attempted to kill him with his fighter's lasers, but the boy's latent Force-sensitivity alerted him to a laser blast from the vengeful pilot. While the pilot was bewildered at how Bridger managed to survive the shot, the boy knocked him out with his [[energy slingshot]], and strutted away with his prize<ref name="Property" /><ref name="Ezra's Gamble" /> despite it being too large to wear, which did not bother him.<ref name="Ezra Pilot" /> Among the contents taken from the fighter, Ezra found a confidential memo mentioning and displaying the images of a [[Kanan Jarrus|human leader]] and a [[Hera Syndulla|Twi'lek pilot]] of a Rebel fighter ship.<ref name="Rebel Journal">''[[Rebel Journal by Ezra Bridger]]''</ref>

===Joining the Spectres===
====Early encounters with the Spectres====
{{Quote|Who ''is'' that kid?|Kanan Jarrus, on Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Spark of Rebellion" />}}
In 3272 LY,<ref name="SWR:TVG" /> after a [[Star Destroyer]] flew over in Lothal's Capital City, Bridger went to the city and prevented a merchant from being imprisoned by Imperials, just before witnessing Kanan Jarrus and his team executing a [[Mission in Capital City|heist]], and intervening to steal one of the crate-carrying [[614-AvA speeder bike|speeder bikes]] they were after. As he fled with the stolen goods, he met [[Sabine Wren]], who proceeded to recover one of the crates.<ref name="Spark of Rebellion" />

[[File:Ghost_Hovers_Over_Ezra.png|thumb|left|220px|Jarrus offering Bridger an escape route]]
Chased through the streets and a roadway out of the city, Bridger had to board the ''Ghost'' as a [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighter]] closed-in on him. As the boy unknowingly used the Force to leap into the hovering ship with his crate, Jarrus was made aware of his Force-sensitivity. Inside the [[Starship|ship]], he met [[Garazeb Orrelios|Garazeb "Zeb" Orrelios]] and Hera Syndulla. Forced to remain with them for a while longer, Bridger was taken to [[Lothal re-settlement camp 43|Tarkintown]], where he helped deliver the stolen crates. Later, he returned to the ''Ghost'' and entered Kanan's quarters where he stole the former [[Jedi]]'s [[Kanan Jarrus' lightsaber|lightsaber]] and [[Kanan Jarrus' holocron|holocron]]. Bridger returned the [[lightsaber]], but kept the [[holocron]] to himself, thinking Jarrus hadn't noticed.<ref name="Spark of Rebellion" />

During the team's [[Mission to free Wookiee prisoners|operation]] to free [[Wookiee]]s, he stayed behind with Syndulla but was convinced to board a [[Gozanti-class cruiser|''Gozanti''-class cruiser]] to alert Kanan, Sabine, Zeb, and [[C1-10P|Chopper]] of an incoming Star Destroyer. However, he was captured by [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus|Kallus]] and abandoned by Orrelios. In his cell, he was able to open Jarrus' holocron and see [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'s message, before escaping from his prison and learning of the Wookiees' location.<ref name="Spark of Rebellion" />

[[File:Ezra_saving_Kitwarr.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Ezra in an attempt to save Kitwarr's life from a stormtrooper]]
Once the ''Ghost'' returned, he boarded the ship along with everyone and revealed what he had learned, prompting the rebels to go to the [[Spice mines of Kessel|spice mines]] of [[Kessel]]. There, while the others kept the [[stormtrooper]]s busy, he freed the Wookiees and watched as Jarrus publicly revealed himself to be a Jedi. He rescued [[Kitwarr]], only to be saved from Kallus by Jarrus' sudden appearance on the ''Ghost''.<ref name="Spark of Rebellion" />

After sending the Wookiees on their way, Ezra stole Kanan's lightsaber once again, but returned the holocron before departing to his tower. Shortly after entering his room, Jarrus gave him two choices—to keep the lightsaber and remain on Lothal, or return to the ship and become his Padawan and a member of the ''Ghost''{{'s}} crew. After taking some time to think about the offer, Ezra returned the lightsaber to Kanan, and became his apprentice.<ref name="Spark of Rebellion" />

====Mission to steal Imperial weapons====
His training, however, only began after a [[mission to steal Imperial weapons]] on the nearby planet of [[Garel]], involving the droids [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]]. During the mission, Bridger—along with Jarrus, Orrelios, Wren, and Chopper—boarded the same [[Star Commuter 2000|star commuter shuttle]] where [[Amda Wabo]] and [[Minister]] [[Maketh Tua]] negotiated their agreement while on their way to Garel. Once there, Bridger infiltrated Bay Seven to open the door to the rest of the team, who managed to steal the [[T-7 ion disruptor rifle]]s, and returned to Lothal. There, Syndulla told the boy of [[Siege of Lasan|Lasan's fall]]. During the unsuccessful transaction with [[Cikatro Vizago]] due to Kallus' arrival, Ezra saved Zeb after his duel with the [[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] Agent. His use of the Force prompted Jarrus to begin his training the following day.<ref name="Droids in Distress">{{Rebels|Droids in Distress}}</ref>

====The meiloorun hunt====
[[File:Grafitti_zeb_and_ezra_room.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Sabine Wren's depiction of Chopper's prank]]
Some time later, Bridger accidentally angered Orrelios due to Chopper's actions and ended up making a mess in the cargo hold. Exasperated, Syndulla sent them both to town for a supply run, with a list that included the rare [[meiloorun fruit]]. The boy and the [[Lasat]] went to [[Kothal]], where they resolved to steal the fruit from an Imperial convoy. However, Bridger and Orrelios were forced to split up, with the Lasat stealing a TIE fighter to escape and save Bridger. Once aboard, the two contacted Syndulla and Jarrus, who ordered them to destroy the fighter and proceed to a rendezvous point.

Before doing so, Bridger asked Orrelios to check out a rising column of smoke on the horizon, which they discovered to be [[Morad Sumar]]'s freshly-destroyed farm. The pair decided to help the farmers, who were being held as [[prisoner]]s aboard an [[K79-S80 Imperial Troop Transport|Imperial Troop Transport]]. After a [[Attack on Imperial Troop Transports|small confrontation]], the pair managed to save Sumar and two other prisoners from [[Yogar Lyste]], and retrieve a meiloorun fruit. Afterwards, they hid the stolen TIE fighter,<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy">{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}}</ref> but claimed to have destroyed it, to Jarrus and Syndulla's approval. Back aboard the ''Ghost'', Wren showed them her new work of art, depicting Chopper's prank.<ref name="Fighter Flight">{{Rebels|Fighter Flight}}</ref>

====Mission to Osisis Station====
[[File:Osisis_Station.png|thumb|right|270px|Osisis Station]]
During a mission to the backwater [[Osisis Station]], the crew of the ''Ghost'' sought repair parts from the station's owner, [[Galus Vez]]. When Vez challenged Hera Syndulla to a race through the treacherous [[Fool's Run]] with the ''Ghost'' as the stakes, Bridger and Kanan Jarrus watched the competition unfold from the station.<ref name="Ring Race">{{RebelsMagCite|1|Ring Race}}</ref>

As Vez utilized false decoy asteroids to damage the ''Ghost'' and regain the lead, Bridger and Jarrus decided to intervene. Using the Force, they manipulated the surrounding asteroids to obstruct Vez's path, causing his ship, the ''[[Splendour]]'', to suffer heavy damage and allowing Syndulla to win the race.<ref name="Ring Race" />

Following the race, a disgruntled Vez accused the crew of cheating and launched an attack. Bridger and Jarrus used their Force abilities to stun Vez's henchmen, successfully ending the confrontation. The crew ultimately secured the necessary parts, leaving the station while Vez remained unaware that Sabine Wren had tagged the location with her starbird graffiti.<ref name="Ring Race" />

====Stygeon Prime====
{{Quote|I don't want to dump you. Look, I just wanted you to have the best teacher.''"<br />"''Well, I don't want the best teacher! I want you.|Kanan and Ezra|<ref name="Rise of the Old Masters">{{Rebels|Rise of the Old Masters}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ezra_Trains_on_Ghost.png|thumb|right|220px|Ezra training on the top of the ''Ghost'']]
After struggling with his Jedi training under a master full of self-doubt, Bridger saw one of [[Senator]] [[Gall Trayvis]]'s [[HoloNet|broadcasts]] for the first time, and was upset to hear that Jarrus wanted the imprisoned Jedi Master [[Luminara Unduli]] to teach Bridger and willing to free the [[Mirialan]] from the [[Spire (Stygeon Prime)|Spire]] on [[Stygeon Prime]]. Nevertheless, the boy took part of the operation and accompanied Jarrus to Unduli's cell, only to discover that she had been dead for years and was being used by [[the Grand Inquisitor]] as bait to lure any surviving Jedi to their end. Bridger tried to help Jarrus on his duel against the [[Pau'an]], who tried to lure the boy to the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]]. After a difficult escape and their return to Lothal, Jarrus promised him he would no longer try to teach Bridger, but to do with newfound resolve.<ref name="Rise of the Old Masters" />

====Ion storm skirmish====
Bridger trained in the Force with Jarrus aboard the ''Ghost'', focusing on telekenisis. Bridger was impatient, to which Jarrus gently chastised him that patience is one of the greatest skill a Jedi has. The next day, the ''Ghost'' [[Skirmish near an ion storm|battled]] an Imperial transport and two TIE fighters in space near an ion storm while Jarrus and Orrelios were away on another mission. Outgunned by the cruiser and the TIE fighters, Bridger suggested hiding in the nearby ion storm to escape the Imperials. Chased into the storm by the Imperials, the transport and TIE fighters were disabled by lightning from the storm. However, so was the ''Ghost''. The crew set about repairing the disabled freighter and while fixing part of the power grid, Bridger becomes frustrated with the lack of success he is having. After requesting help from Chopper, Bridger tells Syndulla he feels useless as that he does not feel he is succeeding in his Jedi training. This leads to a discussion with Syndulla on his need for things to happen quickly and offers the same advice as Jarrus, that patience is required and rushing leads to mistakes. She requests that he work on a damaged console next.<ref name=":0">{{RebelsMagCite|2|Learning Patience}}</ref> 

While trying to fix it, Syndulla returns to inform him that the Imperials have succeeded in re-activating their ship. With time running out as the Imperials close on the disabled freighter, Syndulla demands everyone work faster. Bridger uses the Force to reassemble his console which allows the work Sabine Wren was doing to be completed, reactivating the ship's targeting computer. With the Imperial ship's shields still down, Wren uses the laser cannons on the ''Ghost'' to severely damage the Imperial cruiser, causing it to explode. The ''Ghost'' then reunites with Jarrus and Orrelios.<ref name=":0" />

====The Imperial Academy====
Sometime later, Jarrus sent Bridger on a [[Mission to destroy a kyber crystal|mission]] to steal a decoder containing the location of a [[kyber crystal]] at [[Academy for Young Imperials|Lothal's Imperial Academy]]. Bridger was also supported by Chopper, Wren, and Orrelios. Chopper infiltrated the Academy disguised as an Imperial [[astromech droid]] while Wren and Orrelios waited outside the Academy in a [[landspeeder]] to pick Bridger up. Meanwhile, Jarrus and Syndulla waited in space on the ''Ghost'' to launch their strike on the Imperial convoy carrying the kyber crystal.<ref name="Breaking Ranks" />

For this mission, Bridger posed as "Dev Morgan," a transfer [[cadet]] from the [[Pretor Flats Academy]] on the far side of Lothal. Upon arriving, Morgan was assigned to [[Unit Aurek]], a four-member unit in Squad [[LRC-077|LRC077]]. While Morgan quickly befriended [[Jai Kell]], he was disliked by [[Nazhros Oleg]] and [[Zare Leonis]]. The latter disliked Morgan's braggadocio and carefree attitude and suspected that he was a spy or part of the plot that ensnared his sister [[Dhara Leonis]]. Unknown to Bridger, Leonis was a rebel sympathizer who had infiltrated the Academy to find his sister.<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks">''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]''</ref> Bridger's arrival coincided with Squad LRC077 participating in a series of assessments run by [[Commandant]] [[Cumberlayne Aresko]] and [[Taskmaster]] [[Myles Grint]]. Due to his Force powers, Bridger was able to win five consecutive assessments over a period of two days. This caught the attention of not only the Imperial authorities at the Academy but Leonis himself, who noted that Morgan always seemed to be "in the right place at the right time." During the sixth exercise, Morgan and the other cadets had to leap onto floating [[repulsorlift]] platforms in order to climb out of the Well. After struggling with Oleg, Bridger was the first to reach the top, followed by Kell and Leonis respectively. As a reward, the three Cadets were assigned to work as aides at the [[Imperial Complex (Lothal)|Imperial Complex]] on Lothal.<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks" />

While working in the Imperial Complex, Bridger infiltrated Agent Kallus' office and stole the decoder. Before he could leave, he was intercepted by Leonis, who shoved Bridger back into the room. To Bridger's surprise, Leonis helped him by revealing that the device had a built-in sensor which would cause the facility to go into lockdown if it was illegally taken out of the room. Later that night, Leonis asked Morgan why he needed the decoder. While not revealing his true identity, Bridger revealed that his friends needed it to stop an Imperial shipment. When Bridger asked Leonis how he knew about the sensors, Leonis told him about his missing older sister Dhara. While the Empire claimed that she had run away, he believed that the Empire was not telling the truth.<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks" />

During their meeting, the two boys reached an agreement that Leonis would help Morgan to steal the decoder from Kallus' office. After Morgan and his rebel associates had finished using the decoder, they would provide it to Leonis' girlfriend [[Merei Spanjaf]], a hacker who was trying to access classified Imperial files about Dhara. In order to work in the Imperial Complex, both boys resolved to win the next assessment in the Well. This time, the assessment involved the Cadets using [[E-11 medium blaster rifle|E-11 rifles]] to shoot targets in order to activate the panels necessary to climb out. During the exercise, Bridger was forced to shove Kell in the back in order to maintain his place. While Morgan's actions earned the praise of Commandant Aresko, Kell was bitter that his friend had sabotaged him.<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks" />

With Spanjaf's help, Morgan and Leonis managed to forge a fake requisition order for [[podracer]] parts. While Leonis distracted Kallus with the fake order, Morgan crept into the ISB agent's room through the ceiling and used the Force to levitate the decoder. However, Morgan also discovered that Commandant Aresko had taken an interest in himself and Kell, who met the [[Grand Inquisitor]]'s "[[Force-sensitive|special criteria]]." The Inquisitor responded that he would visit the Academy the following day to assess the two Cadets and take them into custody. When pressed by Leonis, Morgan admitted that he was Force-sensitive. Both resolved to prevent Kell from meeting the same fate as Dhara.<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks" />

Morgan managed to pass the stolen decoder to Chopper and also recorded a message for Wren and Orrelios. In that message, he told his fellow rebels that he had to stay in the Academy to protect Kell from being kidnapped by the Inquisitor. He also told Chopper, Wren, and Orrelios to attack the Academy in the morning in order to create a diversion for them to escape.<ref name="Breaking Ranks" /> That night, Morgan and Leonis woke up Kell and convinced him to escape with them. While Kell was initially distrustful, Leonis managed to reason with him by telling him about his sister. The three Cadets then resolved to escape the Academy by winning the next training exercise in the Well so that they could ride on the [[All Terrain Defense Pod|AT-DP walker]].<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks" />

The following day, their plan encountered an unexpected setback when Morgan was knocked down by a blast fired by Oleg. Thus, Kell, Leonis, and Oleg were designated as the winners and allowed to ride on the AT-DP walker. Despite this problem, Morgan told his fellow Cadets to stick to the plan. As part of the escape plan, Chopper planted a detonator on a nearby AT-DP walker, causing it to crash to the ground. This gave the signal for Kell to stun the walker's [[Imperial combat driver]] and Oleg with his blaster. The hijacked AT-DP walker then exchanged fire with an Imperial Troop Transport. During the chaos, Bridger used his Force abilities to climb onto the walker under the ruse of fighting the hijackers.<ref name="Rebel in the Ranks" />

With much difficulty, the AT-DP walker managed to exit the Academy's gates. There, Bridger and Kell were picked up by the other rebels. However, Leonis opted to stay behind in order to find out about his sister and told him they would stay in touch. After Syndulla and Jarrus' return to Lothal, the rebels agreed to help Kell and his [[Jai Kell's mother|mother]] hide from the Empire. Following the rebel attack on the Academy, the Inquisitor quickly realized upon examining a picture of "Dev Morgan" that he had encountered Bridger and his Master before.<ref name="Breaking Ranks" />

====Disaster at Fort Anaxes====
Later on, Bridger accompanied Syndulla and Wren aboard the ''[[Phantom]]'' for an assault on an Imperial convoy, but the damage done to the shuttle had to be repaired. Assigned along with Orrelios and Chopper to repair it, they never finished due to another of their scuffles, thus leaving Wren and Syndulla temporarily trapped on their mission to [[Fort Anaxes]]. After rescuing them, the boy and the Lasat apologized.<ref name="Out of Darkness">{{Rebels|Out of Darkness}}</ref>

====Supply run to Kaller====
The Spectres were tasked by Fulcrum to aid the people of Tarkintown and recover supplies from the planet [[Kaller]].<ref name="Kanan 1">[[Kanan 1|''Kanan'' 1]]</ref> Arriving at a set of coordinates, they found crates of supplies that had been looted. They were promptly surrounded by forces led by [[Gamut Key]], who searched their ship and determined that they were not smugglers. Thinking of ways to recover the supplies, Bridger suggested searching the nearest large city, explaining that the thief might try to get lost in a crowd. Thus, the Spectres traveled [[Plateau City]]. There, they split off into three pairs, with Bridger joining Syndulla.<ref name="Kanan 6">[[Kanan 6|''Kanan'' 6]]</ref> After some time searching, the Spectres attempted to reach Jarrus, but when he didn't answer, they went towards him and found him bleeding with a stab wound in his back. Bridger and the others waited as Jarrus was healed in bacta.<ref name="Kanan 7">[[Kanan 7|''Kanan'' 7]]</ref> As a medical droid gave them an assessment of his condition, Imperial forces heralded them from outside and ordered them to surrender.<ref name="Kanan 8">[[Kanan 8|''Kanan'' 8]]</ref> Realizing they were outnumbered,<ref name="Kanan 9">[[Kanan 9|''Kanan'' 9]]</ref> they fought off stormtroopers as they entered,<ref name="Kanan 10">[[Kanan 10|''Kanan'' 10]]</ref> but were ultimately captured. However, before they could be moved, Jarrus awoke from bacta treatment and ran through their captors, freeing them single-handedly.<ref name="Kanan 11">[[Kanan 11|''Kanan'' 11]]</ref> Their mission was then completed by recovering the supplies. However, while the rest of the crew returned to Lothal to deliver the supplies, Bridger stayed with Jarrus on Kaller for one more adventure.<ref name="Kanan 12">[[Kanan 12|''Kanan'' 12]]</ref>

Bridger accompanied Jarrus to visit Kanan's friend [[Morfizo]], who had sent a coded message asking for their help. Following the signal, they met with [[Morfizia]] and her children and learned that Morfizo had been captured by the Empire and brought to [[Lahn]]. Jarrus showed Bridger his secret starship, the ''[[Escape]]'', which Morfizo had been keeping safe for him should he ever return for it, and traveled to Lahn, landing at the [[Illmek Island Spaceport]]. There Bridger tried to trick a pair of stormtrooper guards into leaving their post so Jarrus could infiltrate the building where Morfizo was being held. However, Bridger ended up having to fight the troopers once they tried to detain him as Jarrus snuck inside. When the two troopers cornered Bridger, he was saved by [[Janus Kasmir]], a [[Kalleran]] scoundrel who Bridger was unaware was a former associate of Jarrus. Bridger thanked him before taking off, meeting Jarrus and Morfizo back at the ship. Once the trio returned to Kaller, Morfizo and his family were set up with new identities.<ref name="Kanan 12" />

====Empire Day====
On Bridger's fifteenth birthday, Jarrus began training Bridger to use the Force to influence animals, but he struggles. They soon went to [[Old Jho's Pit Stop]] to learn of the Empire's search for an old friend of Bridger's parents, the Rodian Tseebo. Wanting to be alone for a while, Bridger returned to his tower, finding an old [[keycard]] to his residence and discovered where Tseebo is. Bridger meet up with Jarrus, Wren, and Orrelios after they ruined the Imperial parade by detonating a bomb in the recently-unveiled [[TIE/ad v1]].<ref name="Empire Day" />

During their escape, Orrelios departed for the [[Old Market (Lothal)|Old Market]] as Bridger guided Jarrus and Wren into his old residence, where they found Tseebo and the boy told them of his past. HEading to where he found Tseebo, Bridger found an hold [[Hologram disc|holodisk]] in his parent's [[holotransmitter]], where he soon experiences a flashback of Tseebo and his parents. Considering the valuable information the Rodian possessed, the three rebels decided to smuggle him out of Capital City in a stolen Imperial Troop Transport, and later aboard the ''Ghost''.<ref name="Empire Day" /> Despite being pursued by both Kallus and the Inquisitor, the ship managed to jump into hyperspace after Tseebo transmitted the [[hyperspace]] coordinates to the ''Ghost''{{'s}} hyperdrive. Later, when the crew were discussing what to do with Tseebo, Bridger expressed hostility and indifference since Tseebo had not helped his parents when the Empire came after them.<ref name="Gathering Forces" />

Bridger briefly recounted how he had been living on the streets of Lothal for the past eight years until he encountered the crew of the ''Ghost''. Jarrus warned his apprentice that he could not move forward if he was unable to let go of his past. In the middle of the meeting, Tseebo detected the presence of a [[XX-23 S-thread tracker|tracking beacon]], which Chopper quickly deduced was located on the ''Phantom''{{'s}} hull. Sensing that the Inquisitor was pursuing them, Jarrus decided that he and Bridger would depart on the ''Phantom'' in order to lure the Imperials away from the ''Ghost''. Prior to departing, Bridger was still unable to forgive Tseebo.<ref name="Gathering Forces" />

After exiting hyperspace, Bridger and Jarrus took the shuttle to [[PM-1203]], the asteroid which hosted the former Republic base Fort Anaxes. Earlier, Syndulla and Wren had been stranded on Fort Anaxes and accosted by the local [[fyrnock]]s after the ''Phantom'' experienced a fuel leak. Once in there, Jarrus prompted Bridger to let go of his fear, so that he could connect with the fyrnocks. After accepting his fear and forgiving Tseebo, Bridger learned how to influence the creatures. When the Inquisitor and his stormtroopers arrived on the asteroid, Bridger unleashed the fyrnocks on them. As Jarrus dueled the darksider, Bridger commanded the fyrnocks to attack the remaining stormtroopers.<ref name="Gathering Forces" />

[[File:Gathering_Forces_thumb.png|thumb|right|250px|Ezra briefly gives into the dark side of the Force.]]
However, as the Pau'an managed to knock out Jarrus and cornered Bridger, the boy tapped into the dark side and controlled an enormous fyrnock that attacked the Inquisitor. However, this momentarily knocked Bridger out, forcing his master to carry him to the ''Phantom''. On their return to the ''Ghost'', Jarrus explained to him what happened and apologized for not teaching him what he needed to know. Then, Bridger spent some time alone until Wren gave him a birthday gift—a disk containing a picture of Bridger and his parents together—, and proceeded to stare at the picture for a while. Unknown to Bridger, Syndulla had a brief conversation with Tseebo prior to him departing into hiding with the mysterious rebel leader known as [[Ahsoka Tano|Fulcrum]]. He revealed the true fate of Bridger's parents and Syndulla promised to tell Bridger the truth when he was ready.<ref name="Gathering Forces" />

====Rescuing Sabine Wren====
During a mission to swipe the Lothal Imperial Academy's new recruits, Wren [[Mission to Oon|let herself be captured]] and taken to the [[Zygerrian]] [[Slavery|slaver]] [[MaDall]], prompting Bridger and the rest of the team to look for clues of her whereabouts. When Bridger found one of her [[graffiti]] stencils leading them to the planet [[Oon]], Bridger and the rest of the Spectres followed the clue and, upon their encounter, Jarrus chastised Wren for not warning them beforehand. Not wanting to bring themselves to her level, they let MaDall go free and returned, with Wren, to the ''Ghost''.<ref name="Return of the Slavers">{{RebelsMagCite|5|Return of the Slavers}}</ref>

====Dealing with bounty hunters====
When Bridger left to practice his Jedi training alone on Lothal he was watched by the bounty hunters [[Fissol]] and [[Gowski]], who had been informed of a Jedi on Lothal and sought to capture him for credits. The two bounty hunters captured Bridger after a small chase through the cavern. Jarrus felt something was amiss and rode his personal [[Joben T-85 speeder bike]] to their encounter. To rescue his Padawan, Jarrus defeated the two bounty hunters and freed Bridger, and at the prospect of letting Gowski and Fissol with the knowledge of their existence, Jarrus did a mind trick on them so that they thought there were no Jedi on Lothal and duo left Lothal.<ref name="Eyes on the Prize">{{RebelsMagCite|6|Eyes on the Prize}}</ref>

===Impersonation===
Bridger had a vision of someone killing Orrelios with his lightsaber while asleep aboard the ''Ghost''. Concerned about the dream, he sought Jarrus' guidance the next day, claiming it was the third time he had seen the vision. However, Orrelios had departed aboard the ''Phantom'', but had just returned bringing urgent news of a large bounty placed on their heads by the Empire. Suddenly, the [[dejarik]] table suffers a malfunction and needs to be repaired. Chopper was sent to get some of the supplies to repair the table while Orrelios made for his cabin. However, as Chopper rolled into one of the compartments, he comes across something he shouldn't have seen and was shot. Wren found the disabled droid and brought him back to the main room where the assembled Spectres inspect him. The Spectres, suspecting each other, begin to throw accusations around, but Bridger remembered his visions, and climbed into the ''Phantom'' to discover another Orrelios unconscious in the pilot's chair. Bridger informed the rest of the crew that there was an [[Clawdite|imposter]] aboard the ship and as the crew prepared to face the imposter Orrelios, they instead saw a second Wren. A chase begins and eventually the imposter [[Changeling|shapeshifts]] first into Bridger and then after encountering the real Orrelios, back into Orrelios, leading to a hand-to-hand fight. The real Bridger comes upon them with his lightsaber ignited and is forced to choose the real one to stop. Bridger stuns one, which is revealed to be the Clawdite imposter. Jarrus suggests dropping the bounty hunter off at the next world.<ref name="Ezra's Vision">{{RebelsMagCite|8|Ezra's Vision}}</ref>

====Jedi Trials====
{{Quote|I am ready. Wait. Ready for what?''"<br />"''For a test, a real challenge one that could determine if you're meant to be a Jedi or not.|Bridger and Kanan Jarrus|<ref name="Path of the Jedi">{{Rebels|Path of the Jedi}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ezra_guided_by_Yoda.png|thumb|left|250px|Yoda appears to Bridger as a guiding light]]
Sometime after his dangerous connection with the Dark Side on Fort Anaxes, Bridger missed training to show Wren the TIE fighter he had stolen during an earlier adventure with Orrelios.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" /> Kanan then decided to put his apprentice through a challenge to determine if he was worthy of being a Jedi. To do so, he instructed Bridger to locate a [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]], which to their surprise was on Lothal. Once inside the temple, Bridger continued alone and was faced with several illusions.<ref name="Path of the Jedi" />

Firstly, he saw the Inquisitor striking Jarrus down. Secondly, he heard the rest of the crew speaking about Bridger as if they had little faith in him, only for them to be killed by the Inquisitor. Thirdly, Ezra was forced to confront the Inquisitor alone. However, the boy managed to see through the illusions and overcome his fear. After passing through his trials, Ezra heard the voice of the Jedi Master [[Yoda]]. The Jedi Master guided him through the ancient temple and asked him a series of questions. When asked why he wanted to become a Jedi, Bridger admitted that he desired revenge against the Empire. When corrected by Yoda, Ezra expressed his desire to protect others. Pleased by Ezra's answers, Yoda gifted him a kyber crystal and wished Ezra well in his Jedi path.<ref name="Path of the Jedi" />

[[File:EzraRunWithSaber-Fathead.png|thumb|180px|right|Ezra built his first lightsaber with parts donated by the ''Ghost'' crew.]]
Returning to the entryway and meeting up with Jarrus, his master explained that the small crystal he had received could be used to build a lightsaber. Over the course of several weeks, Bridger built a [[Ezra Bridger's first lightsaber|lightsaber]] with the help of the crew. Jarrus gave him spare lightsaber parts that he had found over the previous fifteen years, Wren donated modulation circuits and an energy gate, Chopper donated a power cell and Syndulla likewise provided additional technology based on Bridger's specifications.<ref name="SWR:TVG" /> With all of the rebels assembled, the boy presented the finished weapon to Jarrus, who thought the design fit his apprentice. When he returned it, Bridger ignited the lightsaber for the first time.<ref name="Path of the Jedi" />

====Dealing with Calrissian====
After Orrelios and Jarrus lost Chopper in a game of [[sabacc]] to [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], they reluctantly struck a deal to help him [[Smuggler|smuggle]] goods to Lothal. During their job run for Calrissian, Bridger quickly took a dislike for Calrissian after the "galactic entrepreneur" flirted with the young [[Mandalorian]]. After the smuggler received a [[puffer pig]] from [[Azmorigan]] and Syndulla returned to the ''Ghost'', Bridger and Orrelios scared the pig, causing the creature to inflate. This left Hera and the rest of the crew trapped outside the bridge. In the meantime, Kanan was forced to take the helm of the ''Ghost''.<ref name="Idiot's Array">{{Rebels|Idiot's Array (episode)}}</ref>

To make matters worse, Bridger climbed over the puffer pig, causing the animal to inflate even more and accidentally pushing Orrelios to deactivate the ''Ghost''{{'s}} signature mask. The ''Ghost'' was then pursued by several TIE fighters but Kanan managed to lose them following a brief dogfight. Upon landing at [[Lando Calrissian's farm]], the rebels were immediately accosted by Azmorigan and his henchmen, who had come for retribution against Calrissian. However, the rebels fought them off and drove them away. During the fight, Ezra used his lightsaber to fire shots at Azmorigan's henchmen. After saving Lando, the crew departed on the ''Ghost'' with Chopper stealing Calrissian's [[fuel]] canisters as compensation for their risky job.<ref name="Idiot's Array" />

====The false rebel====
[[File:Rebels_protect_Trayvis.png|thumb|left|250px|Bridger and Jarrus attempting to protect Trayvis from Imperial forces]]
After a training session on deflecting blasters, Bridger experienced a [[Force vision|vision]] that involved Gall Trayvis. Later, he and his comrades saw Trayvis' broadcast inviting the rebels to meet him at the [[Lothal City Capitol Building]] in Lothal's Capital City. Despite his eagerness, Jarrus' suspicions made Bridger verify some intel with his old friend Zare Leonis, who then informed him that he was being transferred to [[Arkanis Academy|Officer's Academy]] in [[Arkanis]]. Feeling guilty, Bridger then revealed "Morgan" was an alias, but as stormtroopers interrupted their meeting, he was unable to tell Leonis his real name.<ref name="Vision of Hope">{{Rebels|Vision of Hope}}</ref>

Later, Bridger rejoined the rest of the team and met Trayvis at the Senate Building, only to be cornered by Agent Kallus and Minister Maketh Tua. Escaping through the sewers, the rebels split into two groups. Jarrus along with Wren and Orrelios departed in one direction. Meanwhile, Bridger, Syndulla, and Trayvis reached a dead end, blocked by a fan. At this opportune moment, the Senator revealed his true colors as an Imperial agent. Syndulla, however, knocked him out just as they were rejoined by Wren, Orrelios, and Jarrus. They then linked up with Chopper and fled aboard the ''Ghost''. After escaping, Bridger was very disappointed for interpreting his vision incorrectly, which Jarrus said was because of his emotions, but Syndulla encouraged the boy to have hope.<ref name="Vision of Hope" />

====Rescuing a Senator====
Syndulla tracked a distress call from a shuttle and rescued the [[Senator]] from [[Thrad]], [[Nadea Tural]]. They take her aboard the ''Ghost'' where Bridger and Jarrus objected to her presence, especially after what happened with Trayvis. Once awake, Tural confronted the crew of the ''Ghost,'' believing them to be insurgents and criminals. Jarrus and Syndulla refuted those claims, explaining how the rebels support the less fortunate and those that are suffering because of the Empire. However, the Imperials were also tracking the distress call and capture and boarded the ''Ghost.'' Bridger, who attempted to fight the Imperials with his lightsaber, was shot in the arm and was captured along with the rest of the crew and taken aboard the Imperial cruiser. As the Imperials prepared to execute the crew Tural intervened, demanding they get a fair trial, which is ignored by the Imperial officer. Tural then threw herself at one of the stormtroopers, preventing them from firing, allowing Jarrus to Force push the remaining Imperials. The crew of the ''Ghost'' escaped with Tural and jumped to hyperspace. They dropped Tural off on [[Camson]] where she revealed that she had a change of heart concerning the rebels.<ref name="Senate Perspective">{{RebelsMagCite|9|Senate Perspective}}</ref>

====Confronting Tarkin====
{{Quote|Stand up together. Because that's when we're strongest—as one.|Ezra Bridger|<ref name="Call to Action" />}}
After a [[raid near Jalath]], the turncoat Senator Trayvis gave a public broadcast on HoloNet reaffirming his loyalty to the Empire and condemning the Spectres. In response, Jarrus decided to hijack the [[Imperial Communications Center]] near [[Jalath]] to broadcast their own counter-propaganda. Bridger participated in this mission and accompanied Jarrus, Wren, Orrelios, and Chopper on their mission to infiltrate the tower. Despite destroying a [[dwarf probe droid]], [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] was alerted to their presence and ordered the Inquisitor and Agent Kallus to launch their trap. Tarkin had arrived on Lothal to implement a permanent solution to the Lothal rebel presence.<ref name="Call to Action" />

Despite Bridger's concerns, he took part in the mission to secure the tower. Chopper uploaded a data spike which allowed the rebels to control the tower. When the rebels were cornered by Imperial forces, Jarrus ordered Bridger and the other rebels to escape up the lift to the top of the tower while he confronted the Imperials alone. After destroying an Imperial [[LAAT/le patrol gunship|patrol transport]], Bridger and his companions reluctantly escaped with Syndulla aboard the ''Phantom''; leaving Jarrus behind. Following Jarrus' capture, Bridger [[Ezra's broadcast|spoke]] to the people of Lothal at sunrise, encouraging them to stand up against the Empire. He finished his message just as Tarkin ordered his patrol transports to destroy the tower.<ref name="Call to Action" />

Determined to [[Action at Mustafar|rescue Jarrus]], Bridger disobeyed Syndulla's orders to stop searching for the former Jedi and enlisted Chopper, Wren, and Orrelios' help to escape on the ''Phantom''. While Chopper kept Hera preoccupied, Bridger along with Wren and Orrelios met up with the [[Devaronian]] [[crime lord]] Vizago. After revealing to his Force powers to Vizago, the crime lord revealed that the Imperials were using [[courier droid]]s to transport classified information in the light of the comm tower's destruction. With Syndulla's approval, he conceived a plan and they sent a disguised Chopper to retrieve Jarrus' location, only to learn at the droid's return that Jarrus was being held aboard Tarkin's Star Destroyer ''[[Sovereign]]'', which was due to travel to the [[Mustafar system]].<ref name="Rebel Resolve">{{Rebels|Rebel Resolve}}</ref>

To approach the ''Sovereign'', the rebels stole an [[Evac One|Imperial transport ship]] and used their stolen TIE fighter to infiltrate the Star Destroyer. Once inside, Bridger separated from the others and rescued Jarrus from his cell, helping him walk to the [[reactor]] core where they were confronted by the Grand Inquisitor. Though he tried to assist Jarrus in his duel with the Pau'an, Bridger was quickly overpowered by the darksider and fell onto another platform—his apparent death prompting Jarrus to lose his fear and fight with renewed resolve.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" />

After receiving a message from Syndulla, Bridger reunited with his master, who had just defeated the Inquisitor once and for all. The two, then, told Syndulla to part with Orrelios and Wren while they took [[The Inquisitor's TIE Advanced|the Inquisitor's TIE]] to join them. However, the rebels could escape only when Chopper and a fleet of [[blockade runner]]s jumped from hyperspace and attacked the pursuing TIE fighters. Afterwards, the rebels docked with the ''Ghost'' and escaped the Mustafar system, Syndulla revealed that their cell was part of a wider rebel network. They were also greeted by a hologram of Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] and [[Fulcrum]], who revealed herself as the Jedi Padawan Ahsoka Tano. She then informed them that Bridger's message had given people hope and that a new chapter in the boy's life was about to begin.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" />

===The rebellion===
====Raid on Area Null====
[[File:RescueofDharaLeonis.png|thumb|right|220px|Bridger and his fellow Spectres storming Area Null]]
Following Kanan's rescue, Ezra Bridger and two of his fellow rebels Zeb and Sabine participated in a [[Rescue of Dhara Leonis|mission]] to rescue Zare Leonis, a cadet at the Lothal Imperial Academy that Ezra had befriended during a mission to steal a [[decoder]] from Agent Kallus. Earlier, Ezra's companions had picked up several fugitives including Zare's girlfriend Spanjaf, a slicer who had managed to hack into the Imperial data network on Lothal. Merei also discovered that Zare had been exposed as a traitor while training at the Arkanis Academy and was scheduled to be tried before a military tribunal. Merei convinced Ezra and her companions to help her.<ref name="Secret Academy">''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]''</ref>

Together with Merei and her mother [[Jessa Spanjaf]], Ezra, Zeb, and Sabine traveled to the planet Arkanis on the ''Ghost'', which they had borrowed from Hera without seeking her permission. After learning that Zare was being held at a secret Imperial facility known as [[Area Null]], Ezra and his companions landed the ''Ghost'' on the facility's rooftop. Making their way downstairs, they encountered Zare and another prisoner named [[Beck Ollet]], who had already succeeded in freeing themselves and had planned to free Zare's sister, Dhara, who had been forcibly inducted into [[Project Harvester]]. While Ezra guarded the rooftop, his companions rescued Dhara and locked Imperial reinforcements out of the facility. After achieving their objectives, they returned to Garel and reunited Zare and Dhara with their parents, who had also fled into hiding.<ref name="Secret Academy" />

====Rescuing a defector====
[[File:Kanan_and_Hera_rebellion_talk.png|thumb|left|250px|Ezra watches as Kanan and Hera discuss their differences]]
Following the rescue of Kanan, Ezra learned that his rebel cell was part of a larger rebellion against the Galactic Empire. Ezra and the other crew of the ''Ghost'' joined the [[Phoenix Cell]] fleet and took part in a [[Mission to steal Imperial shield generators|mission to steal]] [[Deflector shield generator|shield generators]] from the Empire to help defend the fleet. The rebels ambushed a group of Imperial [[freighter]]s and stole several fuel supplies from one of the vessels. After the ''Ghost'' secured the cargo, the rebels fled into hyperspace after the arrival of several Imperial [[Arquitens-class light cruiser|light cruisers]]. In response to the increased rebel activity around the Lothal system, the Emperor dispatched his [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], to stamp out this threat.<ref name="Siege of Lothal">{{Rebels|The Siege of Lothal}}</ref>

Later, Ezra was present on the bridge of the rebel command ship ''[[Phoenix Home]]'' when the Phoenix rebel leadership received a holographic transmission from the disillusioned Imperial Minister Tua, who wanted to defect from the Empire. In exchange for asking the rebels for help, she offered to reveal vital Imperial information—including the names of rebel sympathizers on Lothal and nearby star systems, as well as intelligence regarding the Empire's true mission on Lothal. During the ensuing discussion, Ezra successfully convinced his rebel comrades that they had an obligation to help her. In the end, Kanan, Hera, Ahsoka, and the Phoenix cell leader Commander [[Jun Sato|Sato]] approved the mission. Ezra was also aware of a disagreement between Hera and Kanan. While Hera supported the rebellion, Kanan was reluctant to involve the crew of the ''Ghost'' in a military operation and wanted them to return to their previous mission of robbing from the Empire and giving to the needy.<ref name="Siege of Lothal" />

As part of their mission, the crew of the ''Ghost'' infiltrated Lothal on a Star Commuter 2000 shuttle. While passing through the Imperial security cordon around Lothal, Ezra noted the increased presence of Imperial Star Destroyers above Capital City. While Zeb and Chopper stayed behind to man the shuttle, Ezra and the other rebels headed to their pre-arranged rendezvous point to pick up Minister Tua. The Imperial Minister had arranged for them to meet at a landing bay where an Imperial shuttle was waiting to take her for a private audience with Grand Moff Tarkin. Ezra, Sabine, and Hera hid among the rooftops while Kanan infiltrated the facility disguised as a [[Stormtrooper Commander]]. Unknown to the rebels, however, Agent Kallus had set a trap for them and arranged for Minister Tua to be killed in a shuttle explosion. The rebels were blamed for the bombing and were forced to flee.<ref name="Siege of Lothal" />

Ezra and his fellow rebels attempted to escape on their Star Commuter shuttle, but it was shot down by an AT-DP walker. In response, Darth Vader ordered the Imperial forces on Lothal to place the planet on lockdown and to hunt down the rebel cell. The Spectres sought shelter in Ezra's former family home but Imperial stormtroopers quickly caught up with them and the rebels barely managed to escape with their lives. During the ensuing flight, Ezra's former home was destroyed by an Imperial [[thermal detonator]]. With Imperial forces spread out throughout Lothal, the rebels decided to infiltrate the Imperial headquarters in Capital City and escape offworld. While Ezra and Kanan posed as an [[Imperial cadet]] and stormtrooper, the other rebels hid in crates. Their ruse worked and they managed to infiltrate the Imperial headquarters.<ref name="Siege of Lothal" />

====Escaping Darth Vader====
[[File:Kanan_and_Ezra_face_Darth_Vader.png|thumb|right|250px|Ezra and Kanan confront Vader on Lothal]]
The rebels managed to steal several shield generators and began loading them onto an Imperial shuttle. However, they were then cornered by Darth Vader who was accompanied by several stormtroopers. Ezra and his Master sensed the strong presence of the Dark Side around their new adversary. They attempted to engage the [[Sith Lord]] in lightsaber combat but found themselves outmatched by Vader, who even used the Force to summon Ezra's lightsaber towards the Padawan's neck. Only the timely intervention of Kanan saved Ezra's life. After a protracted skirmish, Ezra and his fellow rebels managed to escape the Imperial headquarters in their stolen shuttle.
