In response to Wartol's leak, she instructed Auxi to contact HoloNet News to give her statement. Admiral Ackbar also agreed to send a [[probe droid]] and a scout ship to the Jakku system to gather intelligence on the Imperial presence. Leia urged her advisers to remain vigilant for traitors in their midst.<ref name="Empire's End" />

====The derailed resolution====
{{Quote|It's just—it must be hard, being you. Under siege from every direction.''"<br />"''Yes. It is hard. But we persevere. Like the Rebel Alliance before us, like the New Republic now. We persevere.|Tracene and Mon Mothma|<ref name="Empire's End" />}}
Later, Chancellor Mothma met with the HoloNet News journalist [[Tracene Kane]] and the [[Sullustan]] cam-operator [[Birt]] to deliver her statement to the press. In her speech, Mothma reiterated that she had become aware of reports that the Empire had retreated to Jakku. She reassured the public that the military had sent a scout ship and a probe droid to confirm this information. While acknowledging rumors that the Imperial remnants had relocated to Jakku, she announced that she had convened an emergency session of the Senate in order to mobilize the armed services. After giving her press statement, Mon chatted with Tracene. When Tracene expressed sympathy for her predicament, Mon responded that the New Republic would persevere like the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="Empire's End" />

That night, Chancellor Mothma gave a speech to the Galactic Senate urging them to authorize military intervention on Jakku. She presented data from the probe droids and the scout ship ''[[Oculus]]'' as evidence that the bulk of Imperial forces had relocated to Jakku. Following the speech, Mothma retreated to her office to recuperate. While chatting with Auxi, Admiral Ackbar entered the office to inform her that the vote had failed. Unknown to Mothma and her advisers, the [[Black Sun]] and [[Red Key Raiders|Red Key]] crime syndicates were plotting to prolong the fighting. They had coerced or bribed five senators into voting against Mothma's motion. At the request of Princess Leia, Sinjir contracted the services of his [[slicer]] friend [[Conder Kyl]]. Conder found Wartol's listening device in T-2LC. After learning about the listening device, Chancellor Mothma decided to pay Senator Wartol a visit.<ref name="Empire's End" />

====Meeting a political rival====
{{Quote|You did do it. You sabotaged the vote.''"<br />"''I admit to nothing. I will not give life to your conspiratorial fancies.|Mon Mothma confronting Senator Wartol|<ref name="Empire's End" />}}
Making use of Chancellor Mothma visited Senator Wartol's [[Ganoidian tri-deck cruiser]] just as he was preparing to depart for Nakadia. When Wartol's Orishen guards tried to block her, Mothma warned them that turning her away with the threat of violence would not look good for the Senator. Chancellor Mothma managed to convince Senator Wartol to allow her to join him on his trip to Nakadia under the pretext of meeting with him. While the two shared a meal of roasted [[Nektod]]s, Wartol asked about the purpose behind her visit since they were political opponents. Mothma replied they both had shared interests and wanted what was best for the galaxy.<ref name="Empire's End" />

In private, Chancellor Mothma asked Wartol about her failed resolution to attack the Empire's fleet on Jakku, which had failed by five votes. Wartol tried to deny his involvement but Chancellor Mothma pointed out that the five dissenting senators Ashmin Ek, [[Rethalow]], [[Dor Wieedo]], [[Grelka Sorka]], and [[Nim Tar]] had voted with him in the past and worked with him in various councils and caucuses. While Wartol had voted in favor of military intervention, Mothma observed that the five senators had taken their cues from him in the past.<ref name="Empire's End" />

As the conversation dragged on, Mothma theorized that Wartol had convinced the five other senators to oppose the resolution while voting for it. When Mothma accused Wartol of sacrificing his principles, the Orishen responded that his people knew the meaning of sacrificing their world so that the Empire would not subjugate them. Despite Wartol's rhetoric about sacrifice, Mothma pointed out that he was sacrificing the New Republic's war efforts so that he could conquer the New Republic. She added that by manipulating the five senators, Wartol was sacrificing the safety of the galaxy.<ref name="Empire's End" />

When Wartol accused her of being a weak and indulgent leader, Mothma insinuated that he had sabotaged the vote. Wartol reiterated his denial and accused her of indulging in conspiracy theories. In response, Mothma presented the listening device that Conder had extracted from T-2LC. When Wartol denied planting the bug, Mothma countered that he knew that the Empire was on Jakku and that he had ordered the guards to stop Sinjir and Temmin from leaving on the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. When Wartol reiterated his denial, Mothma vowed to fight him at the next election.<ref name="Empire's End" />

====Intrigue on Nakadia====
{{Quote|Those who vote no: Recognize that you are marked. You will be marked as cowards at best and traitors at worst.|An excerpt from Chancellor Mothma's speech urging the Galactic Senate to send military forces to Jakku|<ref name="Empire's End" />}}
Wartol retorted that her re-vote was scheduled to take place on Nakadia in less than twelve hours and that she had little time to scramble the votes that she needed. However, Mothma then revealed a card up her sleeve; she had smuggled in a small [[pta fruit]]. Since Nakadia was an agrarian world, it was classified as a [[Class A protected planet]] by the New Republic. Senator Wartol's yacht was prevented from landing by the Nakadian authorities since the pta fruit was considered a biosecurity hazard. Thus, Mothma succeeded in delaying the re-vote.<ref name="Empire's End" />

This gave her allies Han Solo, Sinjir, Temmin, Conder Kyl, and the former New Republic soldier [[Jom Barell]] enough time to track down the five senators. Despite Conder being kidnapped by the Red Key syndicate, Jom managed to capture Rethalow. Rethalow revealed that the Black Sun and Red Key syndicates had coerced and bribed the senators into opposing Mothma's resolution. Sinjir and his team managed to defeat the criminal syndicate's plot by rescuing Conder and Senator [[Nim Tar's child]]. Posing as the Chancellor's adviser, Sinjir managed to convince the five senators to change their votes by offering to pardon them.<ref name="Empire's End" />

Meanwhile, Chancellor Mothma and Senator Wartol finally cleared the Nakadian customs and addressed the press. To delay the proceedings, Mothma feigned a limp as they entered the [[Quarrow Senate house]]. During the session, Mothma gave a short but angry speech urging the senators to vote for intervention on Jakku. She urged them not to hesitate in ending the Empire. While Mothma feared that she sounded like Palpatine, Auxi reassured her that it was a great speech. Mothma was relieved when Auxi later informed her that her vote had passed.<ref name="Empire's End" />

====A new adviser====
{{Quote|Yes, your reputation in that regard precedes you, Sinjir. But another reputation is beginning to form and grow: You are even more incisive with your tongue than you are with your violence. You can be alarmingly convincing, as evidenced by what you said to Senator Rethalow. And further how you manipulated those senators into giving me their vote. I need someone like that. Auxi is a most excellent adviser in matters political, but I need a cynic. Someone who distrusts the system—who maybe even despises it. And I also need someone who can play the game and get me what I want. That someone is you.|Chancellor Mothma recruits Sinjir as her new adviser|<ref name="Empire's End" />}}
Following the Galactic Senate's decision to send military forces to Jakku, Chancellor Mothma returned to Chandrila. After learning of Sinjir's exploits, she secured a meeting with the former Imperial [[loyalty officer]]–turned New Republic operative. When Sinjir asked to go to Jakku, Mothma countered that he was not a soldier and that his talents were better applied elsewhere. Mothma offered to hire Sinjir as her new adviser to complement Auxi. She pointed out that she needed a cynic who distrusted the system. After some discussion, Sinjir accepted her job offer.<ref name="Empire's End" />

Chancellor Mothma then sent Sinjir on his first assignment to deliver a small basket of pta fruits to her political rival Senator Wartol. Sinjir and his partner Conder visited the Orishen senator and caught him red-handed trying to trigger a remote-controlled bomb. While they failed to stop Wartol from [[Assassination attempt on Mon Mothma|detonating]] the bomb, the two managed to overpower the rogue Senator, who readily admitted to plotting to kill the Chancellor. The bomb destroyed Chancellor Mothma's office on Chandrila. While her adviser Auxi was killed, Mothma survived because she was outside the building.<ref name="Empire's End" />

Despite the loss of her friend Auxi, Mothma refused to allow grief to cloud her judgment. With the [[Battle of Jakku]] ending in the New Republic's favor, Chancellor Mothma received word that Grand Vizier Mas Amedda had escaped Imperial captivity and was suing for peace. Chancellor Mothma accepted Amedda's offer and enlisted the help of her advisers Sinjir, Sondiv Sella, and Princess Leia. She arranged for the Imperial surrender to take place on Chandrila in the crystal cliffs north of Hanna City under an ancient [[tintolive tree]].<ref name="Empire's End" />

====Galactic Concordance====
{{Quote|Hope through agitation. The light glows stronger when we struggle.|Mon Mothma, following the signing of the Galactic Concordance|<ref name="Empire's End" />}}
During the meeting, Mas Amedda signed both the [[Galactic Concordance|Imperial Instruments of Surrender]] and the [[Galactic Concordance]]. Per the terms of the Instrument of Surrender, the Empire and the various splinter factions were ordered to cease fighting. Mon Mothma also issued a further declaration designating all surviving Imperial military officers as war criminals. Non-combatant functionaries within the Empire were given conditional pardons provided they complied with the articles of the Galactic Concordance. Grand Vizier Amedda was pardoned and tasked with leading the [[Coruscant's provisional government]]. Following the surrender ceremony, Mothma gave Sinjir a bottle of expensive [[lachrymead]] [[wine]] to thank him for his services to the New Republic.<ref name="Empire's End" />

The Galactic Concordance formally ended hostilities between the New Republic and the defeated Galactic Empire.<ref name="TFA VD">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The treaty forced the Empire to remain inside predetermined territories within the [[Core Worlds]] and the Inner Rim. Mothma urged the Republic to remain vigilant in the event that the conflict returned, and temporarily kept the New Republic Starfleet on wartime funding and alert status.<ref name="Lost Stars" /> Once it became clear that the war was over, the Galactic Senate fulfilled Mothma's goal and passed the [[Military Disarmament Act]]. However, the remnants of the Empire disappeared into the [[Unknown Regions]].<ref name="TFA VD" /> Some time during her tenure, Mothma further reformed the Senate by establishing that member worlds would act as the Senate's capital on a rotating basis.<ref name="Hosnian Prime Databank">{{Databank|hosnian-prime|Hosnian Prime}}</ref> Rotating the capital, and in particular keeping it off of Coruscant, did much to convince member worlds that the New Republic would be different from its predecessor governments.<ref name="TFA VD" />

====Meetings with Syndulla====
{{Quote|We have to prepare for the worst and hope for the best.|Hera Syndulla, to Mon Mothma|<ref name="Part Seven">{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}}</ref>}}
[[File:TheSenateSquad.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Chancellor Mothma with members of the New Republic Senate]]
In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{AhsokaDate|1}}</ref> during which time Coruscant was serving as capital of the New Republic<ref name="Insider 228">{{InsiderCite|228|Making History: Five Years of The Mandalorian|Making History: Five Years of ''The Mandalorian''}}</ref> after Chandrila had taken the flag for a time,<ref name="Chapter 12: The Siege">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}}</ref> Chancellor Mothma and four members of the New Republic Senate, including [[Hamato Xiono]], held a meeting over hologram with General Syndulla.<ref name="Part Three">{{Ahsoka|Part Three: Time to Fly}}</ref> Syndulla, who had just been attacked by Imperial loyalists at [[Santhe Shipyards]] on [[Corellia]] while investigating the work of<ref name="Part Two">{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}}</ref> the recently-[[Attack on the Vesper|escaped]]<ref name="Part One">{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}}</ref> Imperial industrialist [[Morgan Elsbeth]],<ref name="Part Two" /> proclaimed that the New Republic had to prepare for the worst and expressed concern over the potential return of Grand Admiral Thrawn, a project that the loyalists at the shipyard had been contributing to.<ref name="Part Three" />

===Retirement===
Sometime later, Mothma became ill and stepped down as Chancellor. However, her successors lacked Mothma's charisma, and failed to create that same political consensus as she did. In her absence, the New Republic fell into chaos and the Galactic Senate became divided into two factions: the [[Populists]], who believed that individual member planets should retain their full sovereignty, and the [[Centrists]], who favored a stronger galactic government and a larger military by [[28 ABY]]. Mothma showed her personal support for Organa after it was publicly revealed that she was the daughter of Darth Vader. Her message to Organa indicated that she had suspected the truth for some time before the announcement.<ref name="Bloodline">[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']]</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|The likes of Mon Mothma are, of course, legendary for their leadership of the Rebel Alliance and then the New Republic. There is a reason why her life and career are considered key parts of school education.|Beaumont Kin, ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|<ref name="RiseFall" />}}
In several ways, Mon Mothma's actions contributed to the New Republic's eventual undoing. Her drive for ensuring peace and demilitarization eventually left the New Republic in a weakened state of unpreparedness that lacked the strength to combat the rise of the First Order.<ref name="TSWB">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> The New Republic she quickly built fractured without her strong presence, and in no small part was caused by the influence of the draconian [[First Order]]'s growing strength that was not revealed for [[Standard decade|decades]].<ref name="HC 40" /> Nevertheless, decentralized defense forces, [[fringer]]s who had taken for granted the New Republic's limited enforcement of interstellar law, and ordinary citizens of the galaxy alike united against the oppression of the First Order. They formed a [[Citizens' Fleet]] that joined the Resistance at the [[Battle of Exegol]], finally liberating the galaxy from the Sith and inspiring a galaxy-wide [[uprising against the First Order]].<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

Due to her importance to the rise of the rebellion and era of the New Republic, Mothma was mentioned throughout ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', a historical text published by the [[historian]] and [[Resistance trooper]] [[Beaumont Kin]] in the hopes of leading the galaxy away from Imperial ideology once and for all. In the text, Kin reflected on Mothma's governmental decisions after the Galactic Civil War and wrote that the outcome of those choices could not be discussed without also touching on the rationale for each decision. Kin pondered in the text if Mothma had been scarred by the recent conflict, while also musing he may himself be scarred by war. He found he could not bring himself to overly critique Mothma's choices, reflecting that she had wanted to believe the bloodshed was worth its outcome and making note of all the limits that had existed on the establishment of her new government.<ref name="RiseFall" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|War is not a state of being. It is meant to be a temporary chaos between periods of peace. Some want it to be the course of things: a default fact of existence. But I will not let that be so.|Mon Mothma, shortly after the death of Emperor Palpatine|<ref name="Aftermath" />}}
[[File:MonMothma2.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Mon Mothma, during her time as a member of the Galactic Senate, wore an elegant robe of [[fleuréline weave]], a [[shraa silk]] mantle, and a [[hanna pendant]], and sported a simple Chandrilan hairstyle.<ref name="Character Encyclopedia" />]]
Mon Mothma was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] with [[Color|auburn]] [[hair]], pale blue-green [[eye]]s, and light skin.<ref name="RotJ paperback novel" /> Her opposition to authoritarianism that led Mothma to help form the Rebel Alliance. She pursued peace during the Clone Wars, but she was willing to fight to restore democracy to the galaxy.<ref name="Mon Mothma Bio Gallery" /> Her ideals led her to become the first chancellor of the New Republic, where she pushed to avoid the mistakes that the Galactic Republic had made during the Clone Wars. Though strong executive powers were granted to her, she wanted nothing of the sort and believed them to be destructive to the democratic process.<ref name="Aftermath" /> During her time as a Republic senator, Mothma held pacifist beliefs which occasionally led to conflict with Amidala,<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /> though the two never truly fought and they remained close allies.<ref name="Queen's Hope" /> In fact, Amidala was able to mend the divide between Mothma and Bail Organa, helping the two friends to work better together. After detonating the assassin Soujen Vak-Nhalis's self-destruction mechanism to prevent his attack on the Imperial capital, Mothma was caught in the blast and, after surgery, lost her stomach, instead receiving a cybernetic replacement that took training to use. Her heart had also been hit by debris and retained microscopic pieces of metal. However, knowing that her body was not entirely her own felt true, as such was how she felt after her interrogation during the earliest days of the Empire.<ref name="MOF" />

Mothma recognized that her instincts for purity, pacifism, and justice were tainted in the wake of Soujen's death and the failure of the Imperial Rebirth Act; while at the time she had told herself she could not justify murder as a political weapon, only to kill Soujen to prevent such from happening, she was left with the memory that she had ended his life and then found herself trending down the path of rebellion to unseat Palpatine anyway.<ref name="MOF" /> Mothma was a courageous and outspoken Senator in the Imperial Senate who criticized the Empire's increasingly authoritarian and repressive policies. The final straw that broke the [[bantha]]'s back came when Mothma denounced the Emperor in a live [[HoloNet]] speech for his role in the Ghorman Massacre. Despite becoming a fugitive, Mothma refused to hide herself but was determined to take dangerous risks in order to fulfill her goal of creating the Rebel Alliance. As a leader, Mothma preferred to lead by example in order to gain the respect of her underlings. Mothma also took the time to build friendships with other rebel fighters, like Hera Syndulla and Garazeb Orrelios.<ref name="Secret Cargo" /> After the Imperial Senate was dissolved and Bail Organa was killed on Alderaan, Mothma invested herself fully into the Rebellion. As its leader, she made difficult decisions, a number of which would continue to haunt her. Despite this, she remained strong due to the individuals she worked with in Alliance High Command.<ref name="HC 20">{{HelmetCollectionCite|20|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref>

Mothma's devotion to her ideals did prove difficult at times. After the Empire's massacre on Kashyyyk, she thought diplomacy was dead and considered becoming a fighter pilot in the war against the Empire, but she learned that she provided more value to the Rebellion as its leader than as a soldier.<ref name="Beware the Power" /> When she learned of the existence of the second Death Star, she immediately believed that they could defeat it and resolved to get to work.<ref name="SW 2020 28" /> Later, when she learned that the Emperor intended to destroy Chandrila with the Death Star II as a means of silencing her, Mon Mothma struggled with the fear that her actions would endanger her people. However, she refused to allow herself to be ruled by fear and regarded giving into her fear as tantamount to surrendering to the Empire.<ref name="Moving Target" /> Mothma viewed many of the simplistic Chandrilan customs favored by her daughter Leida as being outdated in modern times.<ref name="Leida Databank" /> Mothma's arranged marriage to Perrin was an unhappy one, which made the sight of her daughter going down a similar path upsetting to her.<ref name="Space Moms" /> Mothma saw Leia Organa in a way akin to a younger sister, almost as a daughter.<ref name="The Princess and the Scoundrel" />

[[File:MonMothmaspeaks-ROTJ.png|thumb|right|300px|Mon Mothma in the later years of the Galactic Civil War]]
Despite her position as Chancellor of the New Republic, Mothma was wary of abusing her powers due to Palpatine's legacy. She was prepared to reduce the powers of her own office and the New Republic military once the threat of the Empire had been ended.<ref name="Aftermath" /> As the head of government, Mothma developed a sense of pragmatism since she had to manage a state that was also embroiled in a galactic war. Mothma was aware of the strains on the New Republic's resources and was reluctant to deploy military forces to Kashyyyk. Mothma's pragmatism contrasted with the idealism of Princess Leia, who was unwilling to let obstacles block her goal to liberate the Wookiee species. Believing that the Empire was facing defeat, Mothma agreed to peace talks with Rae Sloane. As a politician, Mothma sought to capitalize on the liberation of the Ashmead's Lock prisoners as an opportunity to win more worlds to the New Republic.<ref name="Life Debt" />

As Chancellor, Mon Mothma was skillful and savvy but strove to keep in touch with her constituents. Despite her powers and privileges, Mothma saw herself as serving the galaxy. She consciously struggled not to become an autocratic dictator like the late Palpatine. Mothma walked a fine balance between keeping the New Republic strong without turning it into a force for oppression. While Chancellor Mothma was sympathetic to the plight of Temmin and Sinjir who had loved ones and friends on Jakku, she was still determined to abide by the rules and norms of the New Republic. As a politician, Mothma preferred to use the system to achieve her goals.<ref name="Empire's End" />

Despite facing low approval ratings (39%) and having to contend with the hawkish Senator Tolwar Wartol, Mothma resolved to continue leading the New Republic. Mothma used her friendly connections and political savvy to outwit Wartol's plot to discredit her leadership. Chancellor Mothma was also a good talent spotter. She recruited the former Imperial loyalty officer Sinjir as one of her new advisers. She admired Sinjir's ingenious plan to convince five dissident senators to change their votes in favor of her resolution to intervene on Jakku. Though Mothma grieved the death of her friend Auxi during Senator Wartol's failed assassination attempt on her life, she remained resolute and led the New Republic's peace negotiations with Grand Vizier Mas Amedda. While presiding over the Empire's surrender, Mothma took care to co-opt non-combatant Imperial functionaries in order to ensure a smooth political transition.<ref name="Empire's End" />

==Skills and abilities==
In addition to being a keen diplomat, Mon Mothma trained as a fighter pilot, although she never actually saw battle.<ref name="Beware the Power" /> Mon Mothma was also a skilled speaker who appealed to her listener's hopes, dreams, and values. While Mothma was a politician, she also knew how to detach two docked starships.<ref name="Secret Cargo" /> As a politician, Chancellor Mothma was able to switch from formal talk to plain speaking based on the situation. Despite being wounded in her left arm, Mothma insisted on keeping her arm and took exercises to strengthen it.<ref name="Empire's End" />

==Equipment==
Mothma wore a white Chandrilan [[Clothing|tunic]] and mantle while serving in the Republic Senate.<ref name="VE">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Development and portrayal===
{{Quote|Certainly people are always very envious of me. When I join a new theater company, the other actors look down the program, see my ''Return of the Jedi'' credit and say, 'Oh, you were part of ''Star Wars''.' I smile and say, 'Yes, but only for twenty-six and a half seconds.'|Caroline Blakiston|<ref name="Galaxy Magazine 12">[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 12|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 12]]</ref>}}
[[File:Manybothansdied.png|thumb|left|300px|Since her brief appearance in ''Return of the Jedi'', Mon Mothma has become a vital figure in ''Star Wars'' storytelling.]]
Mon Mothma was first introduced in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], directed by [[Richard Marquand]] from a script by [[George Lucas]] and [[Lawrence Kasdan]]. She was portrayed by [[Caroline Blakiston]],<ref name="Episode VI" /> who was cast while working in [[Wikipedia:Manchester|Manchester]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]] on a television series. Blakiston met with costume designers in a Manchester hotel room to fit her for a costume and discuss what kind of hairstyle her character would sport, but it was ultimately decided she would use her own red hair.<ref name="Blakiston interview">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/05/caroline-blakiston-interview-mon-mothma.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Caroline Blakiston interview|Mon Mothma|Star Wars}}</ref> Blakiston was provided with an initial script for her brief part in the film, but, upon arriving on set, she learned that her lines had been changed and she would have to learn an entirely new monologue. This proved somewhat stressful, particularly as a result of the dialogue containing ''[[Star Wars]]'' terminology like the word "Bothan."<ref name="Blakiston interview" /><ref name="Knightley">{{InsiderCite|75|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of Star Wars)|Appearing Knightley (and the Women of ''Star Wars'')}}</ref> While in production, Blakiston came up with her own idea for the character's backstory, hoping to find inspiration in the ''Star Wars'' [[Star Wars saga|saga's]] classical underpinnings. She felt that the name "Mon Mothma" bore a similarity to the words "Moon Mother," and as a result she saw her character as someone who would be cool and collected.<ref name="Knightley" /> Blakiston had to re-record her dialogue after it was discovered that pigeons roosting in the set were audible in the original recordings.<ref name="Old Databank" />

A younger version of Mon Mothma appeared in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], written and directed by George Lucas. [[Genevieve O'Reilly]] was chosen to portray the role due to her resemblance to Blakiston,<ref name="Old Databank">{{DB|character|monmothma|Mothma, Mon}}</ref> and she filmed a few scenes for the film that were meant to set up the eventual formation of the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="DVD">{{Film|III}} [[Star Wars home video releases#Star_Wars_Episode_III:_Revenge_of_the_Sith|DVD]]</ref> Before filming, O'Reilly studied Blakiston's performance, hoping to capture the character's voice and mannerisms.<ref name="Old Databank" /> The scenes in which O'Reilly had a speaking role were cut and later included on the film's [[Star Wars home video releases#Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith|DVD release]]<ref name="DVD" /> though O'Reilly did appear in one scene in the final film in a non-speaking role.<ref name="Episode III" /> Blakiston hoped to have a part in the film, asking Lucas if she could appear as her character's grandmother, but she never received a response from the director.<ref name="Blakiston interview" />

The character later appeared in an expanded role in the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. In the three episodes in which the character had a speaking role, she was voiced by actress [[Kath Soucie]].<ref name="Senate Murders" /><ref name="Heroes on Both Sides" /><ref name="Pursuit of Peace" /> Her role as leader of the Rebel Alliance and New Republic has also been expanded upon in several [[canon]]ical ''Star Wars'' tales.<ref name="Star Wars 4" /><ref name="Moving Target" /><ref name="Aftermath" /> O'Reilly would voice Mothma in the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' animated television series.<ref name="Secret Cargo" /> Mothma has also proven to be a consistent character in the works of author [[Alexander Freed]], who has described her as a character who makes every story better.<ref name="Freed Mothma">{{Bluesky|alexandermfreed.bsky.social|post/3lhcyf4n5wk2m|[[Alexander Freed]]|date=2025-02-03|quote=Well, okay. But from a quality perspective that's practically cheating! It's like saying, "if you cook all these dishes with enough butter and salt, they'll all turn out delicious!" Mon Mothma just elevates everything.}} {{C|In response to: "the recurrence of mon mothma makes it a lineup of banger after banger. can never go wrong with mon mothma"}}</ref>

===''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story''===
{{Quote|Rogue One was a really exciting piece to be a part of. It felt like a genuinely creative project. My memories of it were that it was shot almost like an indie film at times. It was very exciting, and it felt like a hotbed of creativity.|Genevieve O'Reilly|<ref name="ProductionBrief">{{ProductionBrief/Andor1}}</ref>}}
O'Reilly returned to the role for the film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="EW Rogue One">{{WebCite|url=http://ew.com/gallery/rogue-one-star-wars-story/2552023_gallery-rogue-one-star-wars-story/1|text='Rogue One: A Star Wars Story': 20 clues and revelations|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2016-04-07|archivedate=20171224163304}}</ref> According to [[Alexander Freed]], the author of the [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]], he would have loved to write more about Mon Mothma in the novel. He later had the opportunity to do so in the story "[[Contingency Plan]]" of the [[2017]] anthology ''[[From a Certain Point of View]]''.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|AlexanderMFreed|status/964335431394279424|[[Alexander Freed]]|quote=There are always ideas that don't make it into a final draft--I'd have loved to do more with Mon Mothma, for example (though I got an opportunity later with From a Certain Point of View). Never considered an Indiana Jones novel, though you never know!}}</ref>

===''Andor'' television series===
{{Quote|She's very enigmatic in all the previous incarnations. People don't have any idea how complicated and difficult Mon Mothma's life has been — her character in many ways has the hardest road of our whole show, what she goes through and the pressure on her. She's this woman who's trapped in a box with everybody watching her, and she has this incredibly potent secret life where she's put herself at great risk by supporting the rebellion. There's no freedom from anxiety in this woman's life, and yet she has to not only endure, but she also has to thrive.|Tony Gilroy|<ref name="ProductionBrief" />}}
O'Reilly reprised her role as Mothma in the ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' television series.<ref name="Aldhani" /> Writer and executive producer [[Tony Gilroy]] was interested in exploring the mystique surrounding Mothma and presenting her in a surprising light.<ref name="ProductionBrief" /> He also wanted to explore the orthodoxy and constructs Mothma would have to live with due to becoming a senator and getting married at the age of 16.<ref name="Marriage">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/andor-mon-mothma-genevieve-oreilly-episode-4-interview|text=Genevieve O'Reilly reacts to Mon Mothma's crappy marriage on Andor|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2022-09-29|archivedate=20220929171606}}</ref> Gilroy called her the "figurehead of liberal democracy that will fail"<ref name="Mothma">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/09/mon-mothma-andor-star-wars|text=Who Is Mon Mothma? Star Wars Fans Are About To Be Shocked|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-09-27|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/NZSCB}}</ref> and compared her to [[Wikipedia:Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|US House Speaker]] [[Wikipedia:Nancy Pelosi|Nancy Pelosi]].<ref name="Pelosi">{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/andor-syril-karn-mon-mothma-1234764813|text=Tony Gilroy Unpacks 'Andor' Ep. 4: Mon Mothma Is 'a Nancy Pelosi Character'|author=Proma Khosla|date=2022-09-28|work=[[Wikipedia:IndieWire|''IndieWire'']]|archivedate=20230507110140}}</ref> [[Chuck Wendig]], author of the 2015–2017 [[Star Wars: The Aftermath Trilogy|''The Aftermath Trilogy'']], had previously described her as a "fairly centrist leader" who proved the difficulty of good governance.<ref name="Wendig Empire's End">{{SW|url=news/chuck-wendig-interview-aftermath-empires-end|text=Chuck Wendig on the Battle of Jakku, Han and Leia's Complex Relationship, and More from ''Aftermath: Empire's End''}}</ref> Gilroy realized that there was not much canon information on Mothma, allowing him to make Vel Sartha her cousin.<ref name="Easter eggs">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-tony-gilroy-talks-luthen-rael-monologue-easter-eggs-1235258961|text=‘Andor' Creator Tony Gilroy Talks Luthen Rael's Future and Being Surprised by Certain Easter Eggs|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221109220924}}</ref> He wanted Mothma and the other legacy characters to not provide fan service.<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How ‘Andor' Became the First ‘Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: ‘I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> Executive producer [[Sanne Wohlenberg]] and her team put much thought into how they would represent Mothma and show her journey, and they stayed aware of where she ended up in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="ProductionBrief" />

[[File:MonMothmaCostumeSDCC.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Mon Mothma's costume was designed by Michael Wilkinson.]]
Production designer [[Luke Hull]] created a sketch of Mon Mothma exiting a Senate limousine on Coruscant.<ref name="Period drama">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theverge.com/23445550/star-wars-andor-production-costume-design-interview|text=Andor's designers approached it like a Star Wars period drama|author=Webster, Andrew|work=[[Wikipedia:The Verge|''The Verge'']]|archivedate=20221109181234}}</ref> Costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]] styled Mothma in flowing robes that evoked her sense of style seen in her ''Revenge of the Sith'' deleted scene. He knew that Mothma was a senator from Chandrila who was stationed on Coruscant, so he thought about people from different countries that work at the [[Wikipedia:Headquarters of the United Nations|United Nations building]] in [[Wikipedia:New York|New York]]. Wilkinson's team intended to bring elements of clothing from Mothma's home, so they came up with a set of colors and textures mainly drawn from other iterations of her. He leaned into pale neutral tones, and Mothma was given slightly shimmery organic textures with hints of metals.<ref name="Dressing the galaxy">{{SW|url=news/dressing-the-galaxy-designer-michael-wilkinson-defines-the-look-of-andor-s-costumes|text=Dressing the Galaxy: Designer Michael Wilkinson Defines the Look of <i>Andor</i>'s Costumes}}</ref>

The crew tried to show Mothma's public face and the private woman within it.<ref name="Never thought">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-star-genevieve-oreilly-never-thought-shed-get-the-chance-to-flesh-out-mon-mothma-1235221270|text=‘Andor' Star Genevieve O'Reilly Never Thought She'd Get the Chance to Flesh Out Mon Mothma|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-09-15|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20220915165314}}</ref> O'Reilly was delighted to have an opportunity to better understand her character.<ref name="ProductionBrief" /> She also wanted to explore Mothma as a Rebel leader and as a woman,<ref name="Never thought" /> which included showing the private face of someone who navigates through systems of oppression.<ref name="Potent Moment">{{SW|url=news/andor-launch-interview-gilroy-and-cast|text="A Potent Moment in History": Insights from Tony Gilroy and the ''Andor'' Cast}}</ref> O'Reilly tried to understand the pain and personal cost felt by Caroline Blakiston in ''Return of the Jedi'', and she enjoyed learning more about Mothma's life.<ref name="Never thought" /> She was excited for the audience to see Mothma's journey of becoming the Rebel leader that she is in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Potent Moment" /> O'Reilly wanted her character's new look in the show to reflect her new stage as a successful member of high society.<ref name="Marriage" /> Scenes in the Chandrilan embassy were filmed in a practically built set that had a wraparound [[Wikipedia:Light-emitting diode|LED]] screen that used [[Wikipedia:StageCraft|StageCraft]] technology.<ref name="Slashfilm">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1090902/heres-where-andor-actually-used-lucasfilms-stagecraft-technology-exclusive|text=Here's Where Andor Actually Used Lucasfilm's StageCraft Technology [Exclusive]|author=Meyer, Joshua|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|''/Film'']]|archivedate=20221109201335}}</ref>

Composer [[Nicholas Britell]] created a musical signature for Mothma.<ref name="Rustling leaves">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/artisans/news/andor-composer-nicholas-britell-score-star-wars-1235383443|text=‘Andor' Composer Nicholas Britell Breaks Down His Score and Why He Incorporated Rustling Leaves|author=Burlingame, Jon|date=2022-09-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220926170019}}</ref> For [[Andor Season 2|Season Two]], Michael Wilkinson worked on costumes that would evolve Mothma into the leader of the Rebellion.<ref name="Dressing the galaxy" /> In an interview with ''Tech Radar'', O'Reilly and [[Faye Marsay]]—who played Mothma's cousin [[Vel Sartha]] in the series—reflected on their characters, with Marsay saying that, to Sartha, their relationship was not difficult and instead was one of tough circumstances: while Sartha acted on the frontlines of rebellion, Mothma was more in the shadows.<ref name="Many cards">{{WebCite|url=https://www.techradar.com/streaming/disney-plus/hes-holding-a-lot-of-the-cards-andor-stars-tease-luthens-important-role-in-the-evolution-of-mon-mothma-and-vel-sarthas-familial-dynamic|text='He's holding a lot of the cards': Andor stars tease Luthen's 'important' role in the evolution of Mon Mothma and Vel Sartha's familial dynamic|author=Power, Tom|date=2025-04-22|work=''Tech Radar''|archivedate=20250501215700}}</ref> Factoring in Mothma's mother in regards to Leida's wedding, O'Reilly mentioned how "within the dialogue" there were "three generations of women," which turned the scene into a very "interconnected, intergenerational story." Further, she had pushed Gilroy to give Mothma a scene in which she gave Leida an out of the wedding, which culminated in the scene where Mothma does, but Leida gives what O'Reilly reflected to be a "pretty brutal" response.<ref name="YahooNews">{{WebCite|url=https://ca.news.yahoo.com/andor-star-genevieve-oreilly-on-leidas-pretty-brutal-response-to-mon-mothma-before-wedding-021432659.html|text='Andor' star Genevieve O'Reilly on Leida's 'pretty brutal' response to Mon Mothma before wedding|author=Elisabetta Bianchini|date=2025-04-25|work=''Yahoo'' News|archivedate=20250424030919}}</ref> After the conclusion of ''Andor'', O'Reilly reflected on the wonderful surprise that returning to ''Star Wars'' had been and how ''Andor'' revealed more about Mothma to her. While she was unsure if it was possible to push Mothma's character further, she was open to the idea of returning once again.<ref name="Goldderby">{{WebCite|url=https://www.goldderby.com/article/2025/andor-star-genevieve-oreilly-on-her-unlikely-two-decade-mon-mothma-journey-ive-closed-the-circle-on-her|text=‘Andor' star Genevieve O'Reilly on her unlikely two-decade Mon Mothma journey: ‘I've closed the circle on her'|author=Scott Huver|date=2025-06-06|work=GoldDerby|archivedate=20250609222729}}</ref>

===Discrepancies===
{{Quote|Bail Organa of Alderaan. How long have you known him?''"<br />"''Since I first joined the Senate, I suppose.''"<br />"''And how long ago was that?''"<br />"''You know the answer.''"<br />"''How long ago, please?''"<br />"''Thirteen years? Just about.|Mon Mothma, under Imperial interrogation|<ref name="MOF" />}}
According to ''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'', Mothma was elected senator in "[[Imperial calendar|8 BFE]]," i.e. 8 [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclamation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Rebel Files" /> in [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> which would place her election in [[27 BBY]].<ref name="Rebel Files" /><ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> However, in the novel ''[[Queen's Shadow]]'', Mon Mothma says that she was "very new to the Senate when [Padmé Amidala] made [her] speech as Queen of Naboo,"<ref name="Queen's Shadow">''[[Queen's Shadow]]''</ref> referring to a scene of the movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Episode I">{{Film|I}}</ref> According to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', the events of the movie took place in [[32 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> which would place Mothma's election that year or earlier.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /><ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> In ''[[Reign of the Empire: The Mask of Fear]]'', the novel's events taking place in 19 BBY, Mothma stated that she joined the Senate nearly thirteen years ago, also placing her election circa 32 BBY.<ref name="MOF" />

In the novel ''[[Leia, Princess of Alderaan]]'', both Mothma and Winmey Lenz are identified as the Senior Senator of Chandrila.<ref name="Leia Princess of Alderaan" /> "[[Welcome to the Rebellion]]" went onto corroborate that it was Mothma who served as Senior Senator.<ref name="Welcome to the Rebellion" /> As such, this article assumes Mothma acted as Senior Senator, not Lenz.

===Role in ''Star Wars'' Legends===
{{Quote|This great struggle is a people's struggle: a struggle between the strong and the weak, the rich and the poor, the cruel and the gentle.|Mon Mothma, describing the Rebellion in a quote from the ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''|<ref name="TRAS">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Bail_Organa_and_Mon_Mothma.jpg|thumb|150px|Mon Mothma and Bail Organa, in an image from ''The New Essential Chronology'']]
[[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] appeared in numerous stories in the Expanded Universe of books, comics, and games, which have since become non-canon and rebranded as [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]].<ref name="Legends Announcement">{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}}</ref> These stories saw her role in the Rebellion fleshed out, showing her as the leader of the Rebel Alliance. The [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'', written by [[Timothy Zahn]], showed her becoming [[Chancellor (New Republic)|Chief of State]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]],<ref name="Heir to the Empire">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref> setting the stage for her canonical counterpart to become the first chancellor of the New Republic.<ref name="Aftermath" /> The 2005 reference book ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' established that the Legends version of Mon Mothma died in her sleep [[24 ABY/Legends|twenty years]] after the Battle of Endor.<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> After the character continued appearing in Legends stories, Blakiston became aware of her character's prolific appearances. She was intrigued by this fact<ref name="Blakiston interview" /><ref name="Knightley" /> and credited it to what she saw as Mothma's strong personality. Blakiston stated that, despite the character's limited screentime in ''Return of the Jedi'', she saw Mothma as an archetypal figure not unlike Darth Vader and Obi-Wan Kenobi.<ref name="Knightley" />

{{Quote|In my life, when you find people who need your help, you help them, no matter what.|Ahsoka Tano|audio=Ahsoka-help-them.flac|<ref name="Dangerous Debt">{{TCW|Dangerous Debt}}</ref>}}
'''Ahsoka Tano''' was a [[Gender|female]] [[Togruta]] who was a [[Force-sensitive]] [[Force-Sensitive Outcast|outcast]] from the [[Jedi Order]]. After the [[Clone Wars]], she helped establish a [[Fulcrum|network]] of various [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|rebel]] cells against the [[Galactic Empire]]. Tano was discovered on her [[homeworld]] of [[Shili]] by [[Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon]], who brought her to the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]] to receive [[Jedi training]]. Following the [[First Battle of Geonosis|outbreak]] of the Clone Wars, [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] assigned the young Tano to be the [[Padawan]] learner of [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], who nicknamed her "'''Snips'''" when she joined him at the [[Battle of Christophsis]]. Whereas Tano was eager to prove herself, Skywalker had a reputation for recklessness, and they had a rather difficult start as master and apprentice. Yet they worked together to [[Battle of Teth|rescue]] [[Rotta]], the son of [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], and [[Mission to Jabba's Palace (Clone Wars)|returned]] Rotta to his [[Parent|father]], thus facilitating a crucial [[Hutt–Republic treaty|alliance]] between the [[Hutt Clan]] and the [[Galactic Republic]].

As a [[commander]] in the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], Tano found a mentor in [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]] of the [[501st Legion]], with whom she and Skywalker collaborated to lead frontline campaigns against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. In her first command position at the [[Battle of Ryloth]], Tano disobeyed orders and lost her entire [[Blue Squadron (Galactic Republic)|squadron]] of [[Clone trooper pilot|pilots]], but she rebounded and helped secure a victory at [[Ryloth]]. Her assignments pitted her against a variety of opponents, from [[General]] [[Grievous]] and [[Sith apprentice]] [[Asajj Ventress]] to [[bounty hunter]]s such as [[Cad Bane]] and [[Aurra Sing]]. Over [[time]], she matured into a respected leader, contributing to key Republic victories like the [[Second Battle of Geonosis]] and the [[Battle of Mon Cala]]. Tano even [[Death|died]] during a [[Mission to Mortis|series of events]] on [[Mortis]], but the [[Daughter]], a [[Force wielder]] who personified the [[Light side of the Force|light side]], sacrificed herself to [[Resurrection|resurrect]] Tano and bring her back to life.

Tano gained much experience on and beyond the war front, leading a group of [[Jedi Initiate|Jedi younglings]] to [[Battle on Wasskah|revolt]] against their [[Trandoshan]] captors, helping [[Battle of Kadavo|rescue]] a [[Artisan colony|colony]] of Togruta from [[Slavery|enslavement]] by the [[Zygerrian Slave Empire]], and serving as an [[advisor]] to the [[Onderon rebels]]—with her close friend, [[Lux Bonteri]], among them—as they [[Onderonian Civil War|liberated]] their [[Onderon|world]] from the Confederacy. In a stark turn of events, Tano was framed for the [[bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar]] and other homicides, and she [[Escape from the Republic military base|escaped]] into the [[Coruscant Underworld]] to clear her name. Though she formed an unlikely alliance with Asajj Ventress, she was [[Capture of Ahsoka Tano|detained]] by Republic forces and was consequently barred from the Jedi Order. Ultimately, Skywalker uncovered the true culprit, Tano's friend, and fellow Padawan [[Barriss Offee]], and prevented his former apprentice from being [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano|convicted]] of [[Treason|sedition]]. Nevertheless, the ordeal dislodged Tano's faith in the Jedi. She refused the [[Jedi High Council]]'s offer to rejoin the Order, instead departing in search of a new path. Tano briefly returned to lead Republic forces during the [[Siege of Mandalore]] and faced [[Maul]] and his allies. [[Order 66]] was enacted shortly after the Sith Lord's capture and Tano alongside Rex, after freeing Rex from the [[Behavioral modification biochip|control]] of Order 66, [[Skirmish aboard the Tribunal|escaped]] the rest of [[332nd Division|her 501st division]]. Faking her death, she was forced into hiding.

After the Galactic Empire came to power, Tano went into hiding on [[Thabeska]] and [[Raada]] disguised as "'''Ashla'''." Following the [[Raada Uprising|evacuation of Raada]], Tano joined [[Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa's]] growing rebel movement. She became the manager of his [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service|intelligence network]] and adopted the codename "'''Fulcrum'''." As [[Fulcrum]], Tano provided intelligence to various rebel factions including [[Hera Syndulla]]'s [[Spectres]] rebel cell. Tano took a particular interest in Syndulla's rebels because one of their members, a Jedi named [[Kanan Jarrus]], had begun to train his own Padawan, [[Ezra Bridger]]. In addition, Tano's efforts against the Empire brought her into [[Attack on Phoenix Squadron (4 BBY)|contact]] with the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth]] Vader—who, unknown to her, was actually her former master, Anakin Skywalker—as well as the Imperial [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]] known as the [[Fifth Brother]] and the [[Seventh Sister]], but it also gave her the chance to reunite with Rex. Following the [[Mission to Malachor|mission]] to [[Malachor]], Tano became lost to the rubble and shadows of the [[Malachor Sith Temple|Sith temple]] and was believed by many, including Jarrus and Bridger, to have perished during a [[Lightsaber duel|duel]] with Darth Vader.

However, Tano was unexpectedly saved from Vader's wrath by a future Ezra Bridger, who pulled her through a [[portal]] into the [[World Between Worlds]], a mystical plane of [[the Force]] connecting all time and space. After a confrontation with [[Darth Sidious]], who desired access to the dimension, Tano returned to her time, promising Bridger that she would find him once she returned. After the end of the [[Galactic Civil War]], Tano joined [[Sabine Wren]] in her [[Quest to find Ezra Bridger|quest]] to find the missing Bridger, who had disappeared during the [[Liberation of Lothal]], and trained Wren in the ways of the Jedi until parting ways. Tano later journeyed to the [[city]] of [[Calodan]] on the [[forest]] [[planet]] [[Corvus]] looking for information on the location of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], who had disappeared alongside Bridger, from [[Magistrate]] [[Morgan Elsbeth]]. Needing to [[Liberation of Calodan|rescue]] the city from Elsbeth's rule, she allied herself with the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]], who had been on a quest to bring the Force-sensitive [[youngling]] [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] to the Jedi. After freeing Calodan, Tano refused to train Grogu and directed Djarin to the planet [[Tython]] instead. She later visited [[Luke Skywalker]] at his new [[Jedi Temple of Luke Skywalker|Jedi Temple]] and, when Skywalker found Grogu in his care following a summons from the [[seeing stone]], oversaw his training of the child temporarily.

Faced with Thrawn's return, Tano returned to Lothal and enlisted Wren's help once again in finding Bridger and the missing Grand Admiral. Decades after Tano began her search, her voice joined a multitude of Jedi [[Immortality|spirits]] to guide the young Jedi [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]], the granddaughter of a [[Resurrection|resurrected]] Darth Sidious, during the [[Battle of Exegol|final battle]] of the [[First Order-Resistance War]]. Ahsoka inspired Rey to stand up to Sidious and destroy him once and for all.

==Biography==
===Childhood===
{{Quote|It was Master Plo Koon who found me and brought me to the Temple where I belonged…|Ahsoka Tano, to Anakin Skywalker|audio=PloKoonFoundMe-RM.flac|<ref name="Rising Malevolence">{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}}</ref>}}
In [[36 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Ahsoka Tano was [[Reproduction|born]] on the [[planet]] [[Shili]]<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> to the [[Togruta]]s [[Pav-ti Tano|Pav-ti]] and [[Nak-il Tano]]. Early in her life, Tano was taken on a journey by her mother, who taught her about life and [[death]]. During that period, the young girl encountered a [[raxshir]] [[feline]], which she reached out to without fear. She proceeded to ride atop the animal to return home. Upon her return, the elder Togruta [[Gantika]] realized the infant was [[Force-sensitive]] and declared that she would be a [[Jedi]].<ref name="Life and Death" /> [[33 BBY|When]] Tano was three [[Standard year|years]] old,<ref name="DB:Ahsoka old">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20201130184749}}</ref> she was discovered by [[Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon]] among her people on Shili<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> after her natural ability to sense the intentions and feelings of others had marked her as Force-sensitive.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

[[File:PloDiscoversAhsoka.png|thumb|left|250px|Plo Koon discovering a three-year-old Ahsoka Tano.]]
Around the same time, however, Tano was nearly [[Slavery|enslaved]] by an [[Unidentified false Jedi|impostor]], who intercepted the signal to the [[Jedi Order]] and hoped to use her [[Force power|powers]] for their own ends. Being unable to properly explain to the village elders the danger she knew the impostor posed, Tano's fellow villagers held scorn towards her when she refused to demonstrate her Force powers, but the impostor's plan was ultimately thwarted. Although the impostor had scared the young Tano, she trusted Koon instantly, and he taught her how to breathe slowly to calm herself.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> Afterward, she was accepted into the Jedi Order,<ref name="DB:Ahsoka" /> beginning her new life<ref name="Ahsoka" /> after Koon brought her to the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]],<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> where, like all Jedi of her era, she was raised.<ref name="Kneobi-Bio">{{Databank|obi-wan-kenobi-biography-gallery|Obi-Wan Kenobi Biography Gallery}}</ref> Training as a [[Jedi Initiate]] restored her self-confidence after the fear caused by the impostor impacted it,<ref name="Ahsoka" /> and the life of a Jedi became the only life she ever knew.<ref name="Gone with a Trace">{{TCW|Gone with a Trace}}</ref>

At some point, Tano traveled to the [[Jedi Temple (Ilum)|Jedi Temple]] on the [[Water|ice]] planet [[Ilum]] to acquire a [[kyber crystal]] for a [[lightsaber]], feeling the [[crystal]]s, albeit without knowing that was what she sensed, as soon as the Jedi [[starship]] came out of [[hyperspace]]. She entered into the temple's [[cave]] after [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] told her she would know her crystal when she found it. As the opening to the cave slowly closed as the [[Star|sun]] of [[Asar]] set, she urgently looked for her crystal until she calmed herself, thinking back on Yoda's words and only then seeing its light. Excited and ready to leave, she quickly made her way out of the cave with the tool for which she could build her [[Ahsoka Tano's lightsabers|own lightsaber]]. Although her visit to Ilum had overall been unremarkable, her decision to trust Yoda's teaching restored her ability to trust others after it was impacted by the false Jedi.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> From there, she would construct said lightsaber using the kyber crystal under the tutelage of Jedi [[architect droid]] [[Huyang]],<ref name="LaJE">{{EncyclopediaCite|Lightsabers and Jedi Equipment}}</ref> who fussed over her shoulder as she worked on it. At another point, Yoda taught her that she could sometimes find something she was not looking for in a situation.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

During her time at the Jedi Temple, Professor Huyang would regale her with the ''[[History of the Galaxy, Parts One, Two and Three]]'', of which she considered part one the best.<ref name="Part Six">{{Ahsoka|Part Six: Far, Far Away}}</ref>

===In the midst of galactic war===
====Becoming Skywalker's Padawan====
{{Quote|I'm the new Padawan learner. I'm Ahsoka Tano.|Ahsoka Tano introduces herself|audio=NewPadawanAhsokaTano.flac|<ref name="TCWFilm" />}}
At the age of fourteen,<ref name="DB:Ahsoka" /> mere [[Standard month|months]] after the [[First Battle of Geonosis]] and the beginning of the [[Clone Wars]],<ref name="Collapse of the Republic">''[[Collapse of the Republic]]''</ref> Tano was assigned to [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] to learn the ways of the Force as his apprentice on the orders of Yoda.<ref name="TCWFilm" /> Her training had been accelerated due to the galactic conflict<ref name="HC 52" /> that overshadowed her apprenticeship.<ref name="X-Wing 52">{{BuildXWingCite|23|Starfighter Aces}}</ref> Having been granted the rank of [[Padawan]],<ref name="DB:Ahsoka" /> which made her a [[Jedi Commander]]<ref name="Storm Over Ryloth">{{TCW|Storm Over Ryloth}}</ref> under the [[Jedi Military Integration Act]],<ref name="Brotherhood">[[Brotherhood (novel)|''Brotherhood'']]</ref> she demonstrated an eagerness to prove herself worthy to be his apprentice. Yoda did this to alleviate Skywalker's fear and inability to lose loved ones, as he believed that by becoming a teacher, Skywalker would develop emotionally and understand that his excessive bonding to those he cared about was unnecessary once Tano was ready to go off on her own.<ref name="Yoda">{{Databank|yoda|Yoda}}</ref>

[[File:R2-D2AnakinandObi-WanmeetAhsoka.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka introduces herself to Anakin and Obi-Wan during the Battle of Christophsis.]]
The Jedi Council finally sent Tano on her first mission to the planet [[Christophsis]] in order to meet her new mentor and inform Kenobi and him that they were needed back at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. However, after arriving on the planet moments after a wave of Separatist forces pulled back and giving that message to the two, she learned that the Republic had in fact failed to take the planet as the Jedi on Coruscant had believed, leaving the generals and their forces trapped and outnumbered as the battle dragged on. Kenobi introduced himself, presuming that she was his new Padawan learner. She corrected him, insisting that Master Yoda specifically assigned her to Skywalker, who was shocked to hear the news due to the fact that he had spoken adamantly against the idea of taking on a Padawan learner. Despite Kenobi's confusion, he accepted that having a Padawan would be good for Skywalker, who vehemently disagreed.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

Meanwhile, the [[Whorm Loathsom's army|droid army]] set up a deflector shield that would block the Republic artillery bombardment that earlier halted their advancements. Skywalker took Tano to check on [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex|CT-7567]] "Rex," who was also confused by Tano's presence, referencing Skywalker's earlier affirmation against taking on a Padawan learner. Tano stood up for herself, saying that Yoda believed she was capable and that she would prove it. As Skywalker went on ahead, Tano asked Rex if she outranked him, to which Rex responded that experience outranked any kind of designated command. However, Tano just responded that she was eager to get some.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

====Liberation of Christophsis====
{{Quote|You're reckless, little one. You never would have made it as Obi-Wan's Padawan… but you might make it as mine.|Anakin Skywalker to Ahsoka Tano, following the Battle of Christophsis|audio=RecklessLittleOne-TCWf.flac|<ref name="TCWFilm" />}}
Skywalker and Tano eventually made a plan to infiltrate the enemy lines while Kenobi and his troops held off the enemy forces in order to buy them time. The two Jedi hid inside a box while the droid [[tank]]s moved around them. As they made their way to the source of the shield, Tano tripped on a [[sensor]] [[antenna]], accidentally activating a batch of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] [[LR-57 combat/retail droid|retail droids]]. While Skywalker was occupied with the droids, Tano began to place charges around the generator. As she was planting charges, a [[battle droid]] snuck up behind her, but Tano noticed it and sliced it in half. The battle droid's body rolled over more sensors and activated additional retail droids. With her master pinned down by the horde, Tano noticed a piece of wall behind him with a convenient hole right where Skywalker was positioned. She used the Force to push the wall down, crushing the droids around her master.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

[[File:Christophsismeeting.png|thumb|left|250px|Yoda, Skywalker, Tano, and Kenobi after the victory.]]
Meanwhile, in the city, Kenobi tricked Separatist [[General]] [[Whorm Loathsom]], stalling for time until the shield blew up. Then, Kenobi took the Separatist General hostage. When the battle was over, Skywalker noted how reckless his new Padawan was, saying that she might not have made it as Kenobi's Padawan. Tano felt disappointment until her master reaffirmed himself, thanking Tano for her help on their mission and noting that her recklessness might serve her well as his student. As Tano and Skywalker found themselves settled, Yoda wondered if having a Padawan would calm Skywalker's wild ways.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

====Battle of Teth and rescuing Jabba's son====
{{Quote|Ahsoka, a very wise Jedi once said, "Nothing happens by accident." It is the will of the Force that you are at my side. I just want to keep you there in one piece.|Skywalker, to Tano|audio=WillOfTheForce-TCWf.flac|<ref name="TCWFilm" />}}
After the [[Battle of Christophsis]], Skywalker and his new apprentice were dispatched to find and rescue [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt's]] missing son [[Rotta]], who was captured by Separatist forces and brought to the planet [[Teth]]. Rescuing Rotta was critical to ensure trade and shipping routes for the Republic through [[Hutt Space]] in the Outer Rim Territories.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

As Skywalker communicated with the [[scout]]s who had been sent to Teth, Tano quickly became friendly with the clones, telling them about her rescue of Skywalker on Christophsis. Skywalker approached them and told them that it would be impossible to land at the [[B'omarr Order Monastery]]. As Rex sent the men to their positions, Skywalker told Tano to remain humble, who replied that she was trying to keep the men inspired.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

[[File:AhsokaStinky-TCWf.png|thumb|250px|Ahsoka holds the young huttlet Rotta.]]
Republic forces were forced to land below the monastery, with Tano riding in a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry|LAAT/i gunship]] with Skywalker, Rex, and several other [[trooper]]s. After landing, their forces began to scale the [[mountain]] with [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer|AT-TE]] [[walker]]s and [[ascension cable]]s where the building was located. Skywalker led the charge and Tano stood on top of a walker and deflected oncoming [[laser]] fire. The climb proved to be a challenge, but the Jedi and clones eventually reached the top of the mountain.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

After securing the outer perimeter, they discovered a [[caretaker droid]] called [[4-A7]], who revealed the location of the captured Hutt. Skywalker and Tano went to look for him and were forced to fight several enemy battle droids, but eventually found the cell where the Hutt was located. Rotta turned out to be just a Huttlet. Meanwhile, 4-A7, who actually served the Separatists and [[Dark Acolyte]] [[Asajj Ventress]], recorded the Jedi's speech. Ventress transmitted the recording to her master, [[Count of Serenno|Count]] [[Dooku]], who gave the "evidence" to Jabba that the Jedi were behind the kidnapping. Dooku assured Jabba that he would sent his [[army]] to "rescue" Rotta, intending to gain Jabba's favor for safe passage through the system.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

With the incoming droid army on their way and the little Huttlet sick, the Jedi had to look for another way out to bring the kidnapped Hutt back to [[Tatooine]]. On their way out, Ventress had arrived and eventually located the two and engaged them in battle. After a brief [[Lightsaber duel|duel]], they escaped on a [[can-cell]] to a nearby [[hangar]], followed by Skywalker's [[astromech droid]], [[R2-D2]], to where a ship, the ''[[Twilight]]'', was berthed. Once on the other platform, they encountered 4-A7 once again. However, it became obvious the droid was a [[spy]] when three battle droids came out of the ship. The Jedi destroyed the droids and hijacked the ship.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

[[File:AhsokavsVentressTeth-TCWFilm.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka duels Ventress for the first time on Teth.]]
While on the escape, Master Kenobi and Republic reinforcements had arrived with Kenobi engaging in a duel with Ventress. Now on the ship, Skywalker and Tano attempted to land on a Republic Star Destroyer, but the [[cruiser]]'s hangar was destroyed, forcing the Jedi to make their way to Tatooine on their own. As the two jumped to hyperspace, Ventress and Kenobi sensed their withdrawal. Kenobi, knowing that Ventress had failed her mission and that her master would be displeased to learn that, managed to gain the upper hand over Ventress until she boarded a Vulture droid to escape capture.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

Meanwhile, Tano and Skywalker found medicine for the Huttlet, which saved his life as they made their way back to Jabba's palace on Tatooine. However, as they approached Tatooine, they came under attack by two [[IG-100 MagnaGuard|MagnaGuards]] in [[Rogue-class Porax-38 starfighter|''Rogue''-class Porax-38 starfighters]]. Despite destroying the fighters, their ship was forced to crash-land in the [[Dune Sea]]. Tano, Skywalker, and R2 then took Rotta across the Dune Sea to reach his father's palace. However, she and Skywalker sensed Dooku's presence.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

[[File:Truce-SWDConv.png|thumb|right|250px|Tano returns "Stinky" to his father.]]
While Skywalker distracted Dooku in a duel, Tano and R2 took Rotta to Jabba's palace. However, they came under attack by several MagnaGuards. Tano fought the MagnaGuards, destroying them all and meeting up with her master at Jabba's palace. However, Jabba ordered their [[Death penalty|execution]] until he was contacted by his uncle, [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure|Ziro]]. Senator [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] then revealed to Jabba that his uncle was working with Dooku and was the one who arranged Rotta's kidnapping. Jabba then spared their lives, and Tano and her master were picked up by Master Kenobi and Yoda.<ref name="TCWFilm" />

====The ''Malevolence''====
{{Quote|Wait! Just because there haven't been any survivors before doesn't mean there won't be any this time!|Ahsoka Tano, to Chancellor Palpatine and Jedi Council|audio=AhsokaBoldlySpoken-RM.flac|<ref name="Rising Malevolence" />}}
At some point, Kenobi told Tano about how his own master, [[Qui-Gon Jinn]], found Skywalker because of his quick reflexes.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> During the [[Malevolence Campaign|hunt]] for the Confederacy's new [[warship]], the ''[[Malevolence]]'', which was a [[Subjugator-class heavy cruiser|''Subjugator''-class heavy cruiser]] armed with two [[mega-ion cannon]]s powerful enough to disable the power systems of an entire [[fleet]] of warships, Tano, along with her master, were sent to protect the staging area in the [[Bith system]]. She and Skywalker were contacted by Master Plo Koon, who had tracked the Confederacy's secret weapon to the [[Abregado system]]. When Koon's transmission was lost, Tano urged her master to send support to Koon, but he required the Chancellor's and Jedi Council's permission. During the meeting, Skywalker and the Council believed that there were no survivors and Skywalker was ordered to protect the Republic's [[convoy]]s. Tano then spoke up and urged them to search for survivors, but she was rebuffed by the Council and the [[Supreme Chancellor]] for her outburst. Skywalker had [[Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen|Yularen]] deploy their fleet while Skywalker and Tano took the ''Twilight'' to "scout ahead."<ref name="Rising Malevolence" />

Despite Tano's outburst, her master agreed with her that they must search for survivors. At first, they were unsuccessful and were ordered by both Kenobi and Palpatine to give up their search. However, as Skywalker [[pilot]]ed the ''Twilight'' away, Tano sensed Koon and took the controls, piloting the ''Twilight'' to his [[escape pod]]'s location. Tano and Skywalker found Koon with the clones Commander [[Wolffe]], [[Sergeant]] [[Sinker]], and trooper [[Boost]]. They learned from Koon that the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} weapon was an [[ion cannon]] mounted on an enormous ship that could disable ships. Tano then detected the ''Malevolence'' approaching them and hurried to disable power so they could blend into the debris field. At first, the ship passed, but it then detected the ''Twilight''{{'s}} [[medical droid]] [[TB-2]], who was caring for the injured Wolffe, and fired the mega-ion [[cannon]]. Skywalker was able to outmaneuver debris and jump to hyperspace before the blast wave reached them.<ref name="Rising Malevolence" />

[[File:AhsokaTanoGunner-SWZ.png|thumb|left|250px|Tano served as gunner on Skywalker's Y-wing fighter.]]
Following their return to the Republic fleet and the ''[[Resolute]]'', Skywalker and Tano were given command of [[Shadow Squadron]] and dispatched on their next mission: to destroy both General [[Grievous]] and the ''Malevolence''. Tano and Koon were both skeptical of the plan, knowing that Grievous would be well protected by his ship's defenses. Tano and Skywalker were then informed Grievous had [[Battle of the Ryndellia system|attacked]] a medical convoy in the [[Ryndellia system]]. Skywalker deduced that Grievous's next target was the Republic's secret Outer Rim [[Kaliida Shoals Medical Center|medical center]] near the [[Kaliida Nebula]]. Tano served as Skywalker's gunner aboard his [[BTL-B Y-wing starfighter/bomber]] as Shadow [[Squadron]] flew to intercept Grievous.<ref name="Shadow of Malevolence">{{TCW|Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence''}}</ref>

Tano, along with her master, Koon, and Shadow Squadron, took a [[Balmorra Run|shortcut]] through the nebula. During the journey, Tano detected several [[Neebray]] mantas. Despite damage to one of the bombers and an astromech, Tano, Skywalker, Koon, and Shadow Squadron reached the medical station. The ''Malevolence'' then arrived, and Tano shot down several of the vulture droids despite her master's fancy flying. When Shadow Squadron started to lose more ships, Tano convinced her master to target the ion cannon instead of the bridge. This strategy succeeded in disabling both the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} ion cannons and its hyperdrive.<ref name="Shadow of Malevolence" />

Tano, Skywalker, and Koon then rejoined Kenobi aboard the ''Resolute'' as he continued [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula|attacking]] the ''Malevolence''. However, Tano detected a [[H-type Nubian yacht|Naboo ship]] approaching the battlefield. Tano then picked up a comm signal from the ship's pilot, Senator Padmé Amidala. When Amidala was captured by a tractor beam, Skywalker decided to rescue the senator. Tano remained on the bridge of the ''Resolute'' with Koon and Admiral Yularen and guided both her master and Kenobi through the ship to find Amidala and her [[protocol droid]], [[C-3PO]], until Grievous jammed their transmissions. Tano watched as Skywalker, Kenobi, and Amidala made their escape, and the the ''Malevolence'' crashed into the [[Dead Moon of Antar]].<ref name="Destroy Malevolence">{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}}</ref>

====Battle of Bothawui and search for R2-D2====
{{Quote|They sent a child to destroy my station? The Republic must be running out of Jedi.''"<br />"''You must be General Grievous. He's just another tinny, boys. Let's scrap him like the rest.|Grievous goads Tano above the Ruusan moon|audio=ScrapHim-DotD.flac|<ref name="Duel of the Droids">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref>}}
Following the Republic's [[Battle of Falleen|defeat]] at [[Falleen (planet)|Falleen]], Tano, Skywalker and their fleet were stationed at Bothawui to protect it. Tano agreed with Kenobi that they should retreat, but stood by her master when he refused to do so. Tano was part of [[Resolute command|''Resolute'' command]] as Skywalker, R2, and [[Gold Squadron (Galactic Republic)|Gold Squadron]] [[Battle of Bothawui|engaged]] Grievous's fleet. As Grievous's fleet hit them, Tano signaled Rex and his AT-TEs to open fire from the asteroids behind Grievous's fleet. Though they destroyed the bulk of Grievous's fleet, Grievous himself escaped.<ref name="Downfall of a Droid">{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}}</ref>

[[File:AnakinAhsokaandR3-S6searchforR2-D2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Anakin and Ahsoka on the search for R2 with the spy droid R3-S6.]]
After Skywalker was injured when his starfighter collided with a large piece of shrapnel, he was brought to the ''Resolute'' to recover, though R2 was left behind. Tano later accompanied her master along with R2's temporary replacement [[R3-S6]], secretly a spy for General Grievous, on a subsequent salvage operation to try and recover the droid. Tano was optimistic R3 would be a suitable replacement but failed to convince Skywalker that R3 could ever replace R2. The pair boarded a nearby salvaging ship piloted by the [[Trandoshan]] scavenger [[Gha Nachkt]]. R3, secretly in league with the Separatists, activated several [[IG-88 assassin droid]]s, which attacked the two Jedi within the ship's cargo hold. After failing to find R2, they left to continue their search, unaware that Nachkt was also in league with Grievous and was secretly hiding R2 from the Jedi. After Skywalker was caught in an ambush by Grievous as a result of R3's sabotage, Tano and Rex were forced to rescue him, once again escaping the General's clutches. Tano continued to stick up for R3, but this only made Skywalker angrier since they were no closer to finding R2.<ref name="Downfall of a Droid" />

[[File:AhsokaSavesRex-DotD.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka duels Grievous inside the Separatist listening post.]]
Upon receiving a transmission from R2 aboard [[Vulture's Claw|Gha Nachkt's ship]], Tano and Skywalker followed the transmission coordinates to Grievous's Separatist [[listening post]] on one of [[Ruusan]]'s moons. To avoid the station's scanners, Tano, Skywalker, R3, Rex, [[Denal]], and several other clones skydived from the ''Twilight'' onto the station's surface, gaining entry via lightsaber. Once inside, Skywalker went to rescue R2 while Tano and the clones began to plant explosives all around the station. However, as Tano and the clones advanced through the station, they were found by a force of droids and were pinned down. Unbeknownst to them, R3 was the one who contacted Grievous to help him locate the infiltration team. After they defeated the enemy, Grievous personally came to attack them. While Tano initially remained confident that they could defeat him like the other droids, Grievous quickly overpowered her before he killed all of the troopers save Rex and Denal. Before he could deal a killing blow to Rex, his strike was parried by Tano's own lightsaber, and the two engaged in a duel. Far outmatched by the [[cyborg]] General, Tano retreated into another room full of spare droid parts along with R3. As she hid, she contacted Rex and ordered him to proceed with the mission and continue to plant explosives with Denal while she distracted Grievous. Then, she was discovered and ambushed by Grievous thanks to the betrayal of R3. She escaped into the ventilation shaft and rendezvoused with the rest of the crew at the hangar and saw that R2 had been rescued. They escaped on board the ''Twilight'', this time with R2, just as the station exploded.<ref name="Duel of the Droids" />

====Capture of Viceroy Gunray====
{{Quote|If it isn't the hairless harpy.''"<br />"''If it isn't Skywalker's filthy, obnoxious little pet.''"<br />"''How nice of you. Tell you what, I'll give you a merciful death.|Ahsoka Tano and Asajj Ventress|audio=HairlessHarpyObnoxiousPet.flac|<ref name="Cloak of Darkness">{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}}</ref>}}
Following the Republic's apprehension of Separatist [[Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]], thanks to the efforts of Padmé Amidala and Senator [[Onaconda Farr]] on [[Rodia]], Ahsoka Tano, and Master [[Luminara Unduli]] were tasked with overseeing Gunray's voyage to Coruscant aboard the ''[[Tranquility]]'', where he would be put on trial for his crimes. Several [[Senate Commando]]s under [[Captain]] [[Faro Argyus]] were also dispatched as extra security to accompany the Jedi. Though Tano was initially skeptical of the need for so much security for just one [[Neimoidian]], Unduli assured the Padawan that his allies could easily be conspiring against them and devising a [[Rescue on the Tranquility|rescue]] plan. The [[Mirialan]] Jedi Master was indeed correct, as Count Dooku had already sent his most trusted [[assassin]], Asajj Ventress, to extract the Viceroy and return him to the Separatists. As Tano and Unduli attempted to interrogate Gunray, with the Jedi Master chastising Tano for threatening him out of impatience, Ventress and her small contingent of Super Battle Droids breached the hull of the ship.<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" />

[[File:AsajjAhsokafocus.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka duels Ventress aboard the ''Tranquility''.]]
Tano was left to guard Gunray as Unduli and Commander [[Gree]] went to deal with the droids, where she was confronted by Ventress, who had slipped inside the ship undetected. Tano was once again confident enough to taunt Ventress as they dueled. The two dueled for a short time before Ventress managed to free Gunray and tricked Tano, trapping the Padawan behind an energy shield in his holding cell. Unduli arrived shortly after, freeing Tano so the two of them could duel Ventress together. However, instead of surrendering, Ventress set off several explosives which she had planted in the engine room, knocking both Jedi to the deck, and escaped down the elevator shaft. Though Tano wanted to follow and confront the assassin once again, Unduli beckoned her to stay put despite her protests.
