As of [[2005]],<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> the character was named Ashla, a reference to an early name for the [[light side of the Force]] when Lucas was developing [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], and later canonized as the [[Lasat]] name of the Force.<ref name="Lasat-Gallery">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/legends-of-the-lasat-trivia-gallery|text="Legends of the Lasat" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 2}}</ref> Ashla is also the name of one Togruta Jedi youngling who appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="DB Bear">{{Databank|bear-clan|Bear Clan}}</ref> Filoni played with the idea of them being the same character, but he realized the ages would not work.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> The two characters, however, are otherwise unrelated.<ref name="Leland Ashla">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=1755#17143245|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2008-02-18|time=1:47 PM|quote=No. The ages don't match up.}}</ref>

Lucas replaced the name "Ashla" with "Ashoka" after [[Wikipedia:Ashoka|Ashoka the Great]], the [[Wikipedia:India|Indian]] Emperor of the [[Wikipedia:Maurya Dynasty|Maurya Dynasty]]. [[Henry Gilroy]] then tweaked it to "Ahsoka" to make her name unique.<ref name="Henry Gilroy">{{Twitter|HGilroy67|status/1019372713712893952|[[Henry Gilroy]]|quote=In honor of #CloneWars 10th, the title page for the series bible I wrote back in 05. When we met with George to discuss the bible he changed Anakin's Padawan from 'Ashla' to 'Ashoka', after the Indian Emperor of the Maurya Dynasty. I later tweaked it to Ahsoka to make her unique.}}</ref> Ahsoka Tano was one of the first characters that Filoni drew when he was working at Lucasfilm,<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> inspired by San, the female wolf-riding protagonist of the 1997 [[Wikipedia:Hayao Miyazaki|Hayao Miyazaki]] and [[Studio Ghibli]] film [[Wikipedia:Princess Mononoke|''Princess Mononoke'']].<ref name="Mononoke">{{SW|url=news/swco-2017-11-things-we-learned-from-dave-filoni-and-pablo-hidalgos-animated-origins-and-unexpected-fates-panel|text=SWCO 2017: 11 Things We Learned from Dave Filoni and Pablo Hidalgo's "Animated Origins and Unexpected Fates" Panel}}</ref> Ahsoka's facial markings were partially inspired by those of San.<ref name="Insider 118">{{InsiderCite|118|Red Five|Red Five: Dave Filoni}}</ref> The character was revealed on [[January 29]], 2008, on [[StarWars.com]],<ref name="firstlook">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news/news20080129.html|text=Padawan Ahsoka Joins the ''Star Wars'' Cast}}</ref> along with toy industry shows.<ref name="This Week! Ep1">{{ThisWeek|Li4auBiXm_0|Star Wars: The Clone Wars, The Child, Star Wars Nite, and More!|sw_url=video/star-wars-the-clone-wars-the-child-star-wars-nite-and-more}}</ref>

[[File:Ahsoka-PP.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ahsoka Tano's younger appearance]]
Producer [[Catherine Winder]] felt ''The Clone Wars'' crew was fortunate in finding Eckstein, as she felt the actress naturally embodied the character.<ref name="SW:TCW Blu-Ray Commentary">The [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] Blu-ray Creative Conversation commentary</ref><ref name="SW:TCW DVD Commentary">The [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] DVD audio commentary</ref> Eckstein recorded the show's [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] before the film premiered in [[2008]]. She had many conversations with Filoni, and she spoke with Lucas about their hopes for Tano and her journey in the series.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> Ultimately, Tano's story,<ref name="Skywalker: A Family at War" /> particularly the events surrounding her decision to leave the Jedi Order,<ref name="TCW4">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Four]]</ref> became a major part of Skywalker's own story and, ultimately, his fall to the dark side.<ref name="Skywalker: A Family at War" /> Indeed, Filoni himself noted as such in the "Obi-Wan Undercover" featurette for [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Four]]: in teasing the story of Tano leaving the Jedi, he noted [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|Season Five]] included a story that helped explain why Skywalker believed the Jedi Order had betrayed his trust.<ref name="TCW4" /> However, even though there were ideas for her to die during ''The Clone Wars'', Filoni did not want Tano's character to just exist as another factor that pushed Skywalker to the dark side. He figured that, if Tano only existed to be part of Skywalker's story, she would have been included in the films.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" />

===''The Clone Wars''===
Tano started out very young and naive because of the way the show was written, the crew's own naiveness, and their lack of experience.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> As "[[Downfall of a Droid]]" was initially the second episode to be developed for the ''Clone Wars'' series, Ahsoka's maneuver when attempting to fly between the Separatist frigates would've explained Anakin's hesitance for her to fly in the later produced episode "[[Shadow of Malevolence]],"<ref name="DoaD Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/downfall-of-a-droid-trivia-gallery|text="Downfall of a Droid" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> although "Shadow of Malevolence" would later be revealed to take place prior to "Downfall of a Droid."<ref name="Clone Wars Chronology">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-chronological-episodeorder|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Chronological Episode Order}}</ref> Ahsoka's visions within the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[Assassin (episode)|Assassin]]" were made to have the same distorted effect as her master Anakin's did in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. In an early version of the script for the episode, Ahsoka visited the young bounty hunter Boba Fett in his [[Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center|prison cell]] in an attempt to learn information upon his former ally Aurra Sing.<ref name="Assassin EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/assassin-trivia-gallery|text="Assassin" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

[[File:SWEAhsokaTano.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano's character model was updated to showcase her growth and increased maturity.]]
Ahsoka's model was updated for [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|''The Clone Wars'': Season Three]] to suggest time had passed,<ref name="New Look">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/newcharacterlooks/index.html|text=A New Look for ''The Clone Wars'' Heroes}}</ref> further showcasing that she had grown older, more mature, and more experienced. The updated character model debuted in the episode "[[Heroes on Both Sides]]."<ref name="HoBS Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/heroes-on-both-sides-trivia-gallery|text="Heroes on Both Sides" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> The update was first teased to fans in an announcement article on [[StarWars.com]]—which revealed a screenshot of Tano and Skywalker's updated models and a promotional image of the two of them with Kenobi in his own updated model—on [[November 16]], [[2010]]. Also included was a link<ref name="New Look" /> to a promotional video showcasing the three new models in action, featuring Tano leaping to the ground before her two mentors and igniting both her lightsabers.<ref name="New Look in Action">{{SWArchive|url=video/view/001152.html|text=New Character Models}}</ref><ref name="New Look in Action Backup">{{YouTube|video=LT9LwclXPfo|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': Season 3: New Character Models|channel=jbjsaltbox|name=Jason Jones}}</ref> While Kenobi and Skywalker's updates brought their designs closer to their appearances in ''Revenge of the Sith'', ''The Clone Wars'' crew had to work around the lack of any live-action reference for Tano, but her character development was as noticeable as any other cast member's: as Filoni explained to StarWars.com in the announcement article, Tano had much to learn at the start of the war, but she had grown and changed, which was reflected in her older, more mature appearance. Furthermore, he promised "Heroes on Both Sides" was yet another step forward in her emotional journey as she met Separatists face-to-face.<ref name="New Look" />

For the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[Ghosts of Mortis]]," the model for Ahsoka's [[goggles]] was repurposed from the one used for Hondo Ohnaka's [[pirate]] gang.<ref name="GoM Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/ghosts-of-mortis-trivia-gallery|text="Ghosts of Mortis" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> In the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[Citadel Rescue]]," Saesee Tiin's starfighter was modeled with the same pattern as Ahsoka's starfighter.<ref name="Citadel Rescue EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/citadel-rescue-trivia-gallery|text="Citadel Rescue" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> When Wilhuff Tarkin enters Ahsoka's cell in the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[The Jedi Who Knew Too Much]]," it is framed as a homage to when Darth Vader enters Leia Organa's cell aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] in ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. Similar to this, his interaction with her while in her cell was meant to mirror his interaction with Leia shortly before he commands the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction of Alderaan]]. Ahsoka's leap from the water pipe in the ''Clone Wars'' episode "The Jedi Who Knew Too Much" is an homage to a similar scene in [[1993]] film ''[[Wikipedia:The Fugitive (1993 film)|The Fugitive]]''.<ref name="JWKTM EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-jedi-who-knew-too-much-trivia-gallery|text="The Jedi Who Knew Too Much" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> When Filoni and the crew were writing the story about Tano leaving the Jedi Order, they made it about her being pulled in different directions and becoming frustrated. They wanted to show young people that they can take a predetermined path or use the information to make their own choice.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" />

===''The Clone Wars'' cancellation and revival===
[[File:Ahsokawalkabout.png|thumb|right|300px|Ahsoka, as she appeared in a story reel that eventually became the episode "Gone with a Trace."]]
Following the cancellation of ''The Clone Wars'' in [[2013]], Filoni revealed that he had planned out [[The Clone Wars Legacy#Unfinished Episodes|twelve more episodes]] that continued Ahsoka's story. He described each four-episode arc at [[Celebration Europe (2016)|Celebration Europe]]. With the release of the seventh season of ''The Clone Wars'' in [[2020]], eight of the twelve episodes Filoni mentioned were fully completed.

In the first arc, Ahsoka would find a new way of life in the underworld of Coruscant and get close to a scoundrel called [[Nyx Okami]]. This arc eventually became the seventh season episodes "[[Gone with a Trace]]," "[[Deal No Deal]]," "[[Dangerous Debt]]," and "[[Together Again]]."<ref name="Reels">When comparing the reel shown in the {{SWYouTube|lS4sclln5J4|Ahsoka's Untold Tales Panel | Star Wars Celebration Europe 2016}} to the opening of "[[Gone with a Trace]]," it is clear that the reel footage was eventually developed into this episode.</ref> In the final release, several major changes were made to the arc, most notably the replacement of Nyx Okami with the Martez sisters, Trace and Rafa.<ref name="Gone with a Trace" />

[[File:AhsokaSithTemple-Concept.png|thumb|left|200px|Ahsoka being shocked by Darth Sidious' force lightning]]
The second arc, which was never completed, would have dealt with Ahsoka helping the Jedi Order and traveling beneath the Jedi Temple to a [[Shrine in the Depths|Sith shrine]]. The arc begins with Tano returning to warn the Jedi of a threat she discovered in the underworld of Coruscant.<ref name="Ahsoka's Untold Tales">{{SWYouTube|lS4sclln5J4|Ahsoka's Untold Tales Panel | Star Wars Celebration Europe 2016}}</ref>

Thereafter, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker enlist her help to rescue Yoda from the Sith shrine underground. During this journey, Ahsoka and Anakin would have flown [[Wikipedia:Autogyro|autogyro]]-style vehicles and encountered large beasts resembling ''[[Wikipedia:Kaiju|Kaiju]]''. At some point during the arc, Ahsoka would protect the Jedi [[Holocron Vault]] from Darth Sidious, who would shoot [[Force lightning]] at her through the vault's doors.<ref name="Ahsoka's Untold Tales" />

[[File:AhsokaVsMaul-TPA.png|thumb|right|300px|Ahsoka Tano faces off against Maul in Season Seven's completed Siege of Mandalore arc.]]
The last planned arc centered around the Siege of Mandalore and was released fully as the episodes "[[Old Friends Not Forgotten]]," "[[The Phantom Apprentice]]," "[[Shattered]]," and "[[Victory and Death]]."<ref name="Old Friends" /> The color of Ahsoka's lightsabers in this arc changed during development. In the initial story pre-cancellation, the lightsabers were meant to have their original green hue, while the final version released in 2020 had a blue hue, reflecting changes that Anakin Skywalker made while the sabers were in his care.<ref name="OFNF Episode Guide" /> For the character's duel with Maul in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|''The Clone Wars'': Season Seven]], stuntwoman [[Lauren Mary Kim]] provided motion caption work to portray Tano's acrobatic fighting style.<ref name="TPA" />

===''Rebels'' continuation===
[[File:AhsokaHS_Rebels.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano in ''Star Wars Rebels'']]
In the television series ''Star Wars Rebels'', Tano was meant to be a wandering [[Wikipedia:Samurai|samurai]],<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> and she carried new, slightly curved lightsabers that are meant to resemble the weapons carried by samurai.<ref name="FAtG EG">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/fire-across-the-galaxy-trivia-gallery|text="Fire Across the Galaxy" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

Ahsoka's conversation with Rex in the ''Star Wars Rebels'' episode "[[Twilight of the Apprentice]]" is meant to mirror their first conversation in the ''Clone Wars'' film.<ref name="TotA EG">{{SW|url=series/episodes/twilight-of-the-apprentice-trivia-gallery|text="Twilight of the Apprentice" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

In an interview with the official ''[[Star Wars]]'' website, ''Rebels'' co-creator and executive producer Dave Filoni stated that Vader wouldn't want a memory of Tano, a relationship that he considered a failure, and that he would be angry with her in a twisted way.<ref name="filoni">{{SW|url=news/interview-dave-filoni-on-star-wars-rebels-part-3|text=Interview: Dave Filoni on ''Star Wars Rebels'', Part 3}}</ref>

===Encounter with Bendu===
{{Quote|You are set on this confrontation then?''"<br />"''I have to know the truth.''"<br />"''So be it, but understand this, much will change as a result of this encounter, including you.''"<br />"''Isn't that true of all things, as time advances?''"<br />"''My dear, when I say change, I mean death.''"<br />"''So I will die?''"<br />"''Will you? I didn't know that. Goodbye then, Ahsoka Tano, former Jedi Knight.|Bendu and Ahsoka Tano, prior to Tano's confrontation with her former master|<ref name="Dave Filoni Tweet">{{Twitter|dave_filoni|status/883124880157192192|[[Dave Filoni]]}}</ref>}}
[[File:AhsokaandBendu.png|thumb|right|175px|Dave Filoni's artwork of Ahsoka meeting the Bendu.]]
After the conclusion of the third season of ''Star Wars Rebels'', series executive producer Dave Filoni revealed that Tano met the [[Bendu]] during the events of "[[The Mystery of Chopper Base]]." Though these events were never depicted on screen, Filoni tweeted dialogue from their encounter as well as artwork illustrating the event. During their conversation, Bendu mentioned Tano's upcoming confrontation with her former master. When Tano explained that she had to know the truth, Bendu retorted that everything would change as a result of their encounter, including her. As the Togruta failed to see his point, he specified that "change" meant death. Tano asked then if she would die, but Bendu acted as if she was affirming it, and so replied that he did not know that before telling her goodbye.<ref name="Dave Filoni Tweet" />

===''The Mandalorian'' and ''The Book of Boba Fett''===
{{Quote|I wanted to kind of have some [of Ahsoka Tano's] playfulness and her fun — the cocky eyebrow thing that she does. You know that she's got that feistiness. You know that she's willing to push the rules a little bit in order to get what needs to get done. But I also really like that she does have that wisdom. She's gone through a lot. She's really gone through a lot of things. And she's grounded, more than when you first meet her as a young teen. It was really fun to find moments to throw homages to the different aspects to Ahsoka that I've always loved.|Rosario Dawson|<ref name="Best of Jedi">{{SW|url=news/rosario-dawson-ahsoka-tano-interview|text=The Best of the Jedi: Rosario Dawson on Bringing Ahsoka Tano to Live-Action and ''The Mandalorian''}}</ref>}}
In [[February]], [[2017]], a ''[[Star Wars]]'' fan asked Dawson on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] if she would ever play Ahsoka Tano, and she replied that she would want to play her, causing fans to be excited about Tano appearing in live-action. According to Dawson, someone at Lucasfilm forwarded the Tweet to ''The Mandalorian'' executive producer Dave Filoni,<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> and he thought she would make a good Ahsoka Tano.<ref name="Tells all">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2020/11/rosario-dawson-dave-filoni-mandalorian-ahsoka-tano-grogu|text=Star Wars The Mandalorian: Rosario Dawson Tells All About Ahsoka Tano|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2020-11-30|archivedate=20201207031817}}</ref> Filoni and ''Star Wars'' then followed Dawson on Twitter, but nothing happened for a long time.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> Filoni kept loosely aware of Dawson's [[Wikipedia:Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel]] career and he watched interviews of her expressing excitement for the role.<ref name="Tells all" /> When Dawson and Filoni discussed the show, he revisited Dawson's casting and realized Dawson's age would fit Tano's age in the show, and he decided the casting was feasible. Filoni and ''The Mandalorian'' creator and executive producer [[Jon Favreau]] did not want to include Tano in [[The Mandalorian Season One|Season One]]<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> because Filoni did not want to mess up Tano's portrayal.<ref name="Ahsoka transformation">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-mandalorian-guide-to-season-two-exclusive-excerpt|text=Explore Ahsoka Tano's Transformation in ''Star Wars: The Mandalorian: Guide to Season Two'' – Exclusive Excerpt}}</ref>

During early production of Season One, Favreau told Filoni that the Child's name would be Grogu, prompting Filoni to think of ways the audience could learn his name. He thought that Tano could learn Grogu's name by communicating through memories and experiences, and she could tell this to the Mandalorian and the audience. Filoni and Favreau knew they wanted Tano in the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season's]] story, so they started visualizing Dawson in the role, and art of the actress playing Tano was created. After they showed that art to Dawson, they asked if she would take the role and she agreed.<ref name="Tells all" /> Concept designer [[Brian Matyas]] explained that the effects team shortened Tano's lekku due to practicality reasons when performing stunts.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/mandalorian-ahsoka-montrals-lekku-character-design|text=Mandalorian's Character Designer Explains Ahsoka's Shorter Montrals/Lekku|author=Wasserman, Ben|date=2020-11-29|archivedate=20201201074637}}</ref>

Tano appeared in the episode Chapter 13: The Jedi, which was written and directed by Filoni.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> According to Filoni, the episode was a test run to see how audiences would react to seeing Tano in live-action.<ref name="Ahsoka for life">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/rosario-dawson-ahsoka-tano-star-wars-series|text=''Star Wars'': Rosario Dawson Aims To Play Ahsoka Tano For Life|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-20|archivedate=20220520134642}}</ref> When Filoni wrote the scene in which Tano reveals Grogu's history, he shaped it around when Obi-Wan Kenobi told Luke Skywalker about his father in ''A New Hope''. When Filoni was working on the episode, he knew the actress who plays the Magistrate would have to be someone who can instantly challenge Tano.<ref name="Tells all" /> After being cast as Tano, Dawson watched ''The Clone Wars'', ''Star Wars Rebels'', and the [[Star Wars saga|''Star Wars'' saga]] as preparation.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> Dawson studied Ashley Eckstein's portrayal of Tano in animation and tried her best to honor it. Dawson was fascinated by how Tano was the center of "this whole other world" shown in ''The Clone Wars''. Dawson played Tano like a wandering [[Wikipedia:Samurai|samurai]] and a knowledgeable [[Wikipedia:Knight|knight]].<ref name="Tells all" /> Filoni pointed to [[Wikipedia:Gandalf|Gandalf]] from [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings (film series)|''The Lord of the Rings'']] as a touchpoint, and all of this factored into Dawson's portrayal. Dawson wanted to have Tano's playfulness and fun, including her cocky eyebrow. She liked Tano's wisdom and how she is grounded after everything she has gone through. Dawson enjoyed having homages to the different aspects of Tano. Filoni talked about classic samurai films such as [[Wikipedia:Yojimbo|''Yojimbo'']], and he described Tano as someone wandering the galaxy helping people in need.<ref name="Best of Jedi" />

[[File:The_Mandalorian_Season_2_Ahsoka_Tano_Poster.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano character poster for ''The Mandalorian'']]
Many screen tests were done because the Volume tends to look magenta. Everything in Tano's costume was considered to an intense degree, including her headtails and horns. Filoni wanted Tano's facial markings to be subtle and look very natural instead of looking like face paint in ''The Clone Wars''.<ref name="Tells all" /> Makeup designer [[Brian Sipe]] had a difficult time finding the right look between human-realistic and pleasing to fans of ''The Clone Wars'' graphic image.<ref name="Ahsoka transformation" /> The crew tried to make Tano's makeup warm and natural, as well as have a different energy compared to animation.<ref name="Tells all" /> Dawson wanted to be as authentic to the animated Tano as possible, so she insisted on wearing blue contacts to match the character's eye color.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> All of the prosthetics were built to Dawson's skull and body, and Tano's headband clipped in the back and held the headtails in place.<ref name="Tells all" /> The make-up artists tucked Dawson's hair away so she could wear the headpiece.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> The total transformation initially took three hours.<ref name="EW Rosario Natasha">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@entertainmentweekly|name=Entertainment Weekly|link=Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|video=SNhSdfQI7Gc|text=Rosario Dawson and Natasha Liu Bordizzo on 'Ahsoka' | Star Wars Celebration | Entertainment Weekly}}</ref> Dawson thought the face markings, different skin color, and costume were incredible, but she did not feel like Tano until she put the contacts in. The crew had to worry about the Volume's temperature changing Tano's skin color, so small considerations were made and adjusted.<ref name="Tells all" />

Tano was again played by Dawson in "[[Chapter 6: From the Desert Comes a Stranger]]," the sixth episode of ''[[Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett]]'' television series.<ref name="BOBF6" /> Dawson did not learn that her character would interact with Luke Skywalker until the day of filming. She was very excited that she got to work with [[Mark Hamill]],<ref name="Rosario Dawson Tweet">{{Twitter|rosariodawson|status/1507180811782549504|[[Rosario Dawson]]|quote=Are you kidding?! I was freaking out. I'm still pinching myself that I got to work with MARK HAMILL as AHSOKA. I didn't know my scene was with LUKE till day of...! @bobafett}}</ref> who provided Skywalker's voice in the episode.<ref name="BOBF6" />

===''Ahsoka''===
{{Quote|Man, I am not a workout-y person, and I'm in my 40s getting into the most physically demanding role of my life. [Ahsoka's] not someone who gets tired. I can't play this like a human. She is an ''indefatigable'' alien. She's precise. She's master-level. The challenge is for me to show up and express that. It's like, I won't necessarily work out for myself, but I'll work out for Ahsoka any day of the week. I'm a huge fan, and I don't want to watch and be like, 'Yo, Ahsoka's hand seems a little shaky there.'|Rosario Dawson|<ref name="Ahsoka for life" />}}
[[File:ArianaRosario-Ahsoka.jpg|210px|thumb|right|Ariana Greenblatt and Rosario Dawson in costume as Ahsoka Tano.]]
Dawson continued to play Ahsoka Tano in the ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]'' television series.<ref name="Announcement">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref> She rewatched the animated shows as preparation for reprising her role.<ref name="Rosario Natasha SWCA">{{SWYouTube|8RZiIf_oEAc|Rosario Dawson and Natasha Liu Bordizzo takes the stage at SWCA 2022 | Star Wars Celebration Live!}}</ref> Dawson cut most of her hair, leaving enough to be hidden comfortably under her headpiece.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> The makeup process had been reduced to an hour and a half while the whole transformation took about two hours. The process would start at 4:30 or 5:00 in the morning.<ref name="EW Rosario Natasha" /> Dawson wanted to show how Tano does not get tired, so she dedicated herself to intense lightsaber and fight training as well as studying Tano's past.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> Dawson and [[Natasha Liu Bordizzo]], the actress who played Sabine Wren, received [[Wikipedia:Chinese martial arts|wushu]] training from stunt coordinator [[Ming Qiu]]. Dawson showed Qiu freeze frames and clips from animated shows and asked Qiu to train her to do Tano's stunts. Qiu would say the stunts are not possible, but she showed Dawson what she could do instead.<ref name="Rosario Natasha SWCA" /> Dawson said this was the most physically demanding role of her life.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> She tried to show that Tano is struggling with balancing her humanity, experiences, and desires.<ref name="EW Rosario Natasha" />

A [[Ahsoka Season 2|second season]] of ''Ahsoka'' was announced to be in development on [[January 9]], [[2024]],<ref name="Mando Announcement">{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-and-grogu|text=''The Mandalorian & Grogu'' Journeys to the Big Screen}}</ref> with Filoni later revealing a development sketch on [[January 11]] that depicted Tano and Wren atop a statue of the Father,<ref name="Ahsoka Sketch">{{SW|url=news/ahsoka-season-2-dave-filoni-sketch|text=''Ahsoka'' Season 2 in Development, New Sketch Revealed}}</ref> a path previously braved by Baylan Skoll in the [[Ahsoka Season 1|season one finale]].<ref name="Part Eight">{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}}</ref> Ahead of season two, Dawson reflected on Tano's character arc in season one and her hopes for the upcoming episodes, specifically expressing hope for "some levity and some lightness" and calling back to Tano's "spunky energy" seen in her early ''The Clone Wars'' appearances. She also noted how Filoni compares Tano's journey to that of Gandalf's arc, a story in ''Lord of the Rings'' that sees an already-powerful and experienced wizard continue to grow and adopt a more joyful personality.<ref name="Levity and Lightness">{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-ahsoka-season-2-evolution-character-arc-rosario-dawson|text=Rosario Dawson Addresses Ahsoka's Evolution & Her Hopes For Season 2's Character Arc|author=Declan, Riz|date=2024-08-24|archivedate=20240825183423}}</ref>

===Video game appearances===
[[File:SWFA_-_ahsoka-tano.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano in ''Star Wars: Force Arena'']]
Tano has appeared in various ''Star Wars'' video games. She could be deployed into battle in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]''.<ref name="Galactic Defense" /> She was playable as part of the player's team in ''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]''<ref name="FA">''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]''</ref> and is playable in ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''.<ref name="GoH">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref>

Tano appeared as a playable character in the 2015 toys-to-life video game ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'', which featured an original, but non-canonical, story set during the Clone Wars. Tano and her allies begin the story by learning a secret droid factory on Geonosis has been activated, kicking off a [[third battle of Geonosis]] and forcing the group to unravel who is behind a new Droid Army's creation. In the end, Tano and company would learn it was Maul's doing and engage the former Sith Lord in a battle on Naboo.<ref name="Infinity 3">''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''</ref> As part of ''Infinity''{{'s}} toys-to-life aspect, Tano was given her own figure that could be beamed into the game. In 2023, former ''Disney Infinity'' story lead [[Adrian Ropp]] revealed he had pushed for Tano to get her own figure despite reluctance on the part of higher-ups. He received support from the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] that ultimately cemented her place as a figure.<ref name="Ahsoka AMA 1">{{Twitter|toonbaboon|status/1691227826949947392|🎨[[Adrian Ropp|ToonBaboon]]📝|date=2023-08-14|quote=And we have a winner! This is one of my big reveals. I was the story person managing Star Wars content and guess who they didn’t want to make a figure of? Ahsoka!!! I had to fight tooth and nail to get that to happen and I got some much needed backup from the Lucasfilm…}} {{C|In response to: "What Star Wars characters didn't make the cut? If it's a big list, some big ones that were unknown to the public are good, just curious."}}</ref><ref name="Ahsoka AMA 2">{{Twitter|toonbaboon|status/1691228335362453504|🎨[[Adrian Ropp|ToonBaboon]]📝|date=2023-08-14|quote=…story team. I was one of a couple of people that passionately fought for a female character to be one of the playset pack characters. Holly, Jessie, Mrs. Incredible, Ahsoka, Gamora… so when girls played it they'd start with the choice!}}</ref>

===Other appearances===
[[File:Acme-AhsokaJourney.png|thumb|right|300px|The life and journey of Ahsoka Tano, as depicted by artist [[Kayo Takahata]] in the piece "Ahsoka's Journey Continues"]]
Tano appeared in "[[Kamino Crisis]],"<ref name="CoK">{{LSWCite|101|Kamino Crisis}}</ref> a non-canon comic story written by [[Martin Fisher]] and published on [[October 7]], [[2023]]<ref name="jedi-bibliothek">{{WebCite|url=https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/lego-star-wars-magazin-101|text=LEGO Star Wars Magazin 101|archivedate=20240303173302}}</ref> in the [[LEGO Star Wars 101|101st issue]] of the magazine [[LEGO Star Wars (magazine)|''LEGO Star Wars'']]. In the comic, Anakin Skywalker, Tano and Clone Captain Rex were returning from a successful mission onboard the ''Resolute''. After Rex told them that their missions were too easy, the two Jedi planned to test the Captain by manipulating a training session for new clone troopers that was led by Rex. Tano disguised herself as a clone trooper named Tank, while Anakin Skywalker disguised himself as clone trooper Thrower to take part in a course in the [[Tipoca City Training Facility]] on [[Kamino]]. While they were fighting B1 battle droids that were repurposed as [[training droid]]s, a voltage peak caused the droids to become much more aggressive and skilled in combat.<ref name="CoK" />

The droids managed to break out of the training arena, after which Tano and Skywalker, still disguised as clone troopers, joined forces with Rex and other troopers to stop the rogue group of droids. While they were fighting in the hallways of [[Tipoca City]], the clone trooper [[Glider (clone trooper)|Glider]] went into the [[Control room (Tipoca City)|control room]] and destroyed the controls with his blaster, which caused the battle droids to be powered down. As Rex gathered the troopers to thank them, Tano and Skywalker took of their helmets and revealed themselves. They explained that they wanted to test the Captain and Rex responded that he wouldn't call their missions easy ever again. He then invited them to join his [[Rex's bowling team|bowling team]] if they ever left the Jedi Order.<ref name="CoK" />

Tano is depicted alongside Plo Koon on the cover of the ''[[Star Wars: Shatterpoint]]'' "First Contact" Mission Pack, which depicts both Jedi involved with a struggle against droidekas in a city environment during the Clone Wars.<ref name="First Contact">{{Asmodee|url=products/star-wars-shatterpoint-first-contact-mission-pack|text=Star Wars: Shatterpoint - First Contact Mission Pack}}</ref> It is unclear if this is meant to be taken as a canonical event.

===Contradictions===
====Height====
Carrying over information seen in Tano's entry on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]],<ref name="SWE:Ahsoka">{{SWE|characters|ahsokatano|Ahsoka Tano}}</ref> Tano's initial entry on the StarWars.com [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] in 2014—which at that time covered only the events of her teenage years in the initial run of ''The Clone Wars''—gave her height as 1.7 meters,<ref name="DB:AhsokaOldest">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20140703012405}}</ref> which was then carried over as the height of the adult Tano seen in ''Star Wars Rebels''<ref name="DB:Ahsoka2017">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20170706184708}}</ref> and ''The Mandalorian'' despite the obvious growth she had seen over the in-universe years.<ref name="DB:Ahsoka2020">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20201207224646}}</ref>

Meanwhile, the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''<ref name="AEYNTK" /> and its [[2017]] update ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' listed the adult Tano's height as 1.88 meters, or 6 feet and 1 inches tall.<ref name="Absolutely Updated" /> The [[2021]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] affirmed that 1.7 meters, or five feet and seven inches, was Tano's height at some stage of her teenage years<ref name="Join the Battle" /> while that same year's ''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' gave an adult height of 1.76 meters, or 5 feet, 9 inches.<ref name="CEUAEK" /> However, in 2023, her Databank entry was updated to reflect an adult height of 1.79 meters.<ref name="DB:Ahsoka2023">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20230729214640}}</ref>

====Tales of the ''Ahsoka'' novel====
{{Quote|There isn't a big conspiracy behind the changes in Ahsoka's story. Dave approved the book six years ago and then kept working on her journey. It's frustrating to see people gleefully declare my book non-canon instead of just...using their imaginations. Like we did.|EK Johnston|<ref name="EK contradictions tweet">{{Twitter|ek_johnston|status/1553725660459417602|EK Johnston|quote=There isn't a big conspiracy behind the changes in Ahsoka's story. Dave approved the book six years ago and then kept working on her journey. It's frustrating to see people gleefully declare my book non-canon instead of just...using their imaginations. Like we did.}}</ref>}}
The ''Ahsoka'' novel by E. K. Johnston features a flashback to the Siege of Mandalore, in which Tano duels Maul in a plaza with green lightsabers before capturing him in a ray shield. After the execution of Order 66, which is implied to occur on Mandalore itself, Rex—who is suggested to already have had his inhibitor chip removed—and Tano fake their deaths by burying a [[Unidentified clone trooper (Rex's false grave)|clone trooper]] in Rex's armor and with her lightsabers. Rex then departs from the gravesite before Tano.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> These events were later overruled by the seventh season of ''The Clone Wars'', however.<ref name="TPA" /><ref name="Shattered" /><ref name="Victory and Death" /> An updated version of the novel was released that changed the color of Tano's lightsabers to blue, but the remaining contradictions were later left in place.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

The main plot of the novel sees Tano in hiding on the farming moon Raada under the name Ashla, only for her activity to be uncovered by the Sixth Brother Inquisitor, whom she slays before reuniting with Bail Organa.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> This series of events is also very similar to those depicted within the ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (television series)|Tales of the Jedi]]'' episode "[[Resolve (episode)|Resolve]]," where the Inquisitor and farming site are not identified.<ref name="Resolve" /> Indeed, Dave Filoni stated that the ''Ahsoka'' novel and "Resolve" are the same story as "Resolve" is born from the same outline he had given to Johnston.<ref name="Nerdist">{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/article/tales-of-the-jedi-dave-filoni-interview-ahsoka-tano-count-dooku-star-wars|text=Dave Filoni on How TALES OF THE JEDI Explores Choices Between Light and Dark|author=[[Amy Ratcliffe]]|date=2022-10-26|archivedate=20221026222129}}</ref> Johnston herself expressed a similar sentiment, claiming the ''Ahsoka'' novel and ''Tales of the Jedi'' episode could be the same events seen from the differing points of view of different creators.<ref name="JohnstonTempleGeek">{{YouTube|video=KgiFqFHA3fc|text=A conversation with author EK Johnston - Portrait of a Fangirl Podcast|channel=@templeofgeek|name=Temple of Geek|date=10-11-2023}}</ref> Before the episode's release, however, Johnston had theorized the book and episode depicted separate incidents. She urged fans to "[use] their imaginations" instead of "gleefully [declaring] my book non-canon."<ref name="EK contradictions tweet" />

Sources released since "Resolve" have seemingly attempted to separate it from the ''Ahsoka'' novel despite their similar plots. The 2023 reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side Pocket Expert]]'' reflects the Sixth Brother as appearing in novels and comics but makes no mention of him having been in ''Tales of the Jedi'' despite including information about the show elsewhere in its pages.<ref name="Dark Side Pocket">''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side Pocket Expert]]''</ref> The character then went onto appear in the 2023 novel ''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]'' by [[Delilah S. Dawson]], whose text describes the Sixth Brother<ref name="Rise of the Red Blade">''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]''</ref> as he appeared in ''Ahsoka'' and his comic appearances,<ref name="Dark Side Pocket" /> instead of adopting the appearance of the ''Tales'' Inquisitor.<ref name="Resolve" /> The [[2024]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' then outright confirmed the ''Tales'' Inquisitor and Sixth Brother are separate characters by providing them separate entries. The book identified the ''Tales'' character as the First Brother,<ref name="SW Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> a name quickly revealed to actually be intended for Marrok.<ref name="Discord">{{WookDiscord|discordname=.holocronkeeper|name=Leland Chee|date=2024-11-21|messagelink=https://discord.com/channels/397848917036761090/492457166771322881/1309008181808336926|quote=There was miscommunication and we got the number wrong in the Encyclopedia.|archivefile=File:LelandChee-Inquisitor-Discord.png}}</ref> The ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article "[[Inquisitor Countdown]]" then revealed the ''Tales'' Inquisitor was named the [[Eleventh Brother]] and, again, separated him from the Sixth Brother.<ref name="Countdown">{{InsiderCite|229|Inquisitor Countdown}}</ref> While neither the ''Star Wars Encyclopedia''<ref name="SW Encyclopedia" /> nor "Inquisitor Countdown" reflect the events of ''Ahsoka'' in the Sixth Brother's description,<ref name="Countdown" /> this article takes the separation of both Inquisitors as proof that the events of ''Ahsoka'' and "Resolve" are separate, if similar, incidents.

The novel features Bail Organa first learning of Ahsoka Tano's survival of Order 66 a year into Imperial rule, while Tano is surprised to learn a known Jedi sympathizer like Organa is still alive.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> However, "Resolve" later revealed that he and Tano met during the funeral of Padmé Amidala.<ref name="Resolve" /> Therefore, the two must have both assumed the other died in the year between these events.

====Other matters====
[[File:SWR_Ahsoka_Gandalf.jpg|thumb|left|226px|Ahsoka Tano arrives on Lothal]]
The ''Rebels'' finale "[[Family Reunion – and Farewell]]" depicted Tano traveling to Lothal with white [[clothing]] and a matching [[staff]] on a T-6 shuttle to meet with Sabine Wren, who sought to bring Bridger home.<ref name="Family Reunion – and Farewell" /> This scene was later adapted for the ''Ahsoka'' series<ref name="Part 2 Highlights">{{SW|url=news/ahsoka-part-2-toil-and-trouble-highlights|text=''Ahsoka'' Analyzed: 5 Highlights from "Part Two: Toil and Trouble"}}</ref> with some changes, including Tano's clothing.<ref name="Part Two" /> This article assumes the most recent depiction—the version of the scene in ''Ahsoka''—is correct.

As a Padawan, Tano is featured on a variant cover for the [[Star Wars (2025) 6|sixth issue]] of [[Star Wars (2025)|''Star Wars'' (2025)]] by [[Alex Segura]]. Drawn by the artist "[[Bengal]]," the cover depicts Tano with Skywalker as representative of their time together as Jedi guardians. However, Tano—despite being depicted<ref name="SW2025 6">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/130734/star_wars_2025_6_variant/variant|text=Star Wars (2025) #6 (Variant)}}</ref> in her ''The Clone Wars'' seasons three<ref name="Altar of Mortis" /> through six attire<ref name="Destiny" />—is mistakenly depicted with a blue-bladed lightsaber,<ref name="SW2025 6" /> something she only wielded during the events of ''The Clone Wars'' Season Seven in her Mandalorian attire.<ref name="Old Friends" />

{{Top}} {{Update|[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]], [[The Separatists (reference book)|The Separatists]]}} {{Character |type=CIS |image=[[File:Poggle_the_lesser_-_sw_card_trader.png]] |name=Poggle the Lesser |homeworld=[[Geonosis]]{{SWE|characters|pogglethelesser|Poggle the Lesser}} |birth= |death=[[19 BBY]], [[Mustafar]]{{Film|III}} |species=[[Geonosian]] |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.83 [[meter]]s (6 [[Foot|ft]])''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' |mass=80 [[kilogram]]s''[[Star Wars Journeys: Beginnings]]'' |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color|Yellow]] |skin= |cyber= |families=new |parents=new |partners=new |siblings=new |children=new |affiliation=*[[Stalgasin hive]]''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]'' *[[Techno Union]] *[[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] **[[Executive Separatist Council]] *[[Galactic Republic]] {{C|briefly}}''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]'' |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Geonosians do not hold life to be as precious as you humans do, Lieutenant Commander.|Poggle the Lesser, to Orson Callan Krennic|}} '''Poggle the Lesser''', also known simply as '''Poggle''', was a [[Geonosian]] [[Gender|male]] who served as the [[Archduke]] of the [[Stalgasin hive]] under [[Geonosian hive-mind|hive-minded]] [[Queen]] [[Karina the Great]], and as such served as the public face of the Geonosians during the Clone Wars. Having risen to prominence by gaining oversight of [[Baktoid Armor Workshop]]'s [[battle droid]] [[Factory|factories]] on Geonosis, Poggle the Lesser became a powerful figure within the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and joined the [[Executive Separatist Council]]. With his leadership cemented, Poggle soon slayed Archduke [[Hadiss the Vaulted]] to take their position for himself, and, shortly thereafter, served as a [[warlord]] [[commander]] for the [[Separatist Droid Army|Separatist droid armies]] when the [[Galactic Republic]] attacked them during the [[First Battle of Geonosis|first]] and [[Second Battle of Geonosis|second battles]] of Geonosis. As a result of his high-ranking position among the Separatists, Poggle was captured by the Republic during its second invasion of Geonosis. Incarcerated on [[Coruscant]], Poggle was subjected to several rounds of interrogation by [[Republic Intelligence]] before being approached by [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] of the [[Republic Special Weapons Group]], who sought to utilize the Stalgasin hive as a [[Sentience|sentient]] workforce in the [[Project Stardust|construction]] of a [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|secret battle station]]. While initially agreeing to provide his drones for the project, Poggle later sabotaged the project and absconded back to Separatist [[Realspace|space]]. In the final days of the Clone Wars, Poggle and the rest of the Separatist Council were relocated to [[Utapau]], and later to [[Mustafar]], where they were all [[Death|killed]] by the new [[Galactic Empire|Empire's]] enforcer, [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]]. ==Biography== ===Rise to power=== {{Quote|Some of you gathered here today are old enough to remember when Baktoid Armor Workshop came to Geonosis and struck a deal with us to build foundries and produce battle droids and other automata for which we were handsomely rewarded. Then, as ever, we were able to overcome our natural contempt for outsiders in order to fulfill what seemed a noble task.|Poggle the Lesser|}} [[File:PoggleTheLesser-TCWCE.png|thumb|right|300px|Poggle the Lesser, archduke of Geonosis]] Once a member of the drone caste, Poggle the Lesser, with strategic aid from the manipulative [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]],{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Poggle the Lesser - Geonosian Separatist}} rose to the position of [[Archduke]] of [[Geonosis]], the public position of leadership that secretly answered to the [[Geonosian]] [[queen]].''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' Poggle also became [[controller]] of the large [[Geonosis droid factories|Geonosian droid factories]] on the [[planet]] and manufactured millions of [[B1-series battle droid]]s for the [[Trade Federation]] corporation.''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' As part of his rise to power,{{EncyclopediaCite|The Separatists}} he also killed the previous leader of the Geonosians, [[Hadiss the Vaulted|Hadiss]] the Vaulted, ensuring his control over Geonosis.{{BuildFalconCite|19|Guide to the Galaxy}} During the [[Separatist Crisis]], Poggle was one of the first and one of the most ardent supporters of its cause,{{SW|url=poggle-the-lesser-biography-gallery|text=Poggle the Lesser Biography Gallery}} which had been set off by [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Head of State]] and former [[Jedi]] [[Dooku]].{{Film|II}} Dooku had personally ensured the droid building contract between the Geonosians and [[Baktoid Armor Workshop]] continued on. Poggle profited greatly from the arrangement, and, thanks to Dooku, rose to a position of power like that of no other Geonosian ruler before him. Despite his prominence, Sidious and Dooku viewed Poggle as highly expendable.{{HelmetCollectionCite|12|Weapons & Uniforms}} In addition to dealings with the Separatists, Poggle continued to operate as an extension of Karina the Great's rule over the Stalgasin hive,{{HelmetCollectionCite|31|Databank A-Z}} the most dominant hive on Geonosis. He would receive instructions from her on how to run the hive. Later in life, during his brief tenure with the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars]], Poggle would claim that the Geonosians and himself did not know that Dooku was leading a Separatist confederacy, also claiming that they did not know how the Federation would use the droids they had been provided. This was in spite of evidence to the contrary. Ultimately, these claims were made by Poggle during an elaborate ploy to escape back to the CIS during the war. Indeed, the Geonosians joined the Confederacy ahead of the war and became incredibly loyal to Dooku,{{TCW|Landing at Point Rain}} with Poggle himself actively being involved in planning for the coming war during that time. ===The Clone Wars=== ====First Battle of Geonosis==== {{Quote|noquote=1|«We have to order a retreat.»''
"''My master will never allow the Republic to get away with this treachery.''"
''«I'm sending my warriors to hide in the catacombs. The Jedi must not find our designs for the Ultimate Weapon. If they find out what we are planning to build, we're doomed.»''
"''I will take the designs with me to Coruscant. They will be much safer there with my master.|Archduke Poggle the Lesser and Count Dooku|}} For the [[Geonosian accord]], he hosted a meeting of fellow Separatist conspirators on Geonosis. Poggle pledged the [[Army|armies]] of his people to Dooku. [[File:Poggle_Geo.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Poggle the Lesser inside the Geonosian Command Center, during the First Battle of Geonosis]] Poggle, Dooku, and the rest of their Separatist conspirators then went to the [[Petranaki Arena]] to watch the [[Death penalty|executions]] of [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and [[Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker]]. However, [[Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu]] and a [[Jedi assault team|team of 212 Jedi]] arrived to [[First Battle of Geonosis|rescue]] Kenobi, Skywalker, and Amidala. As the [[battle droid]]s overwhelmed the Jedi, they were then rescued by [[clone trooper]]s under [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]]. Poggle and the rest of the separatist conspirators then went to the underground [[Geonosian War Room]] to oversee the battle. As the [[Grand Army of the Republic|Republic Army]] forced their [[Separatist Droid Army|Droid Army]] to retreat, Poggle ordered his warriors to hide in the [[Geonosian catacombs|catacombs]]. He then gave Dooku the [[Death Star plans|plans]] for their [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|ultimate weapon]], who assured that they would be safe with his [[Sith Master|Master]], [[Darth]] Sidious. ====Dealings with Clovis==== {{Quote|Are you suggesting we change the terms of our agreement? No. A deal's a deal.|Rush Clovis to Lott Dod and Poggle the Lesser|{{TCW|Senate Spy}}}} [[File:PoggleLottDod-SS.jpg|thumb|right|272x272px|Lott Dod and Poggle]] Poggle, along with [[Trade Federation]] Senator [[Lott Dod]], conspired with [[Scipio]] Senator [[Baron]] [[Rush Clovis]] to rebuild the [[Geonosis primary droid foundry|primary droid foundry]] on Geonosis. When Clovis arrived on [[Cato Neimoidia]] at [[Great Vaults of Cato Neimoidia|Dod's palace]], Poggle and Dod [[Mission to Cato Neimoidia|demanded a greater share of the profits]] than the [[foundry]] would produce. When Clovis refused to change the terms, Poggle agreed with Dod's plan to [[poison]] his companion, Padmé Amidala. However, Clovis helped Amidala's guard (who was really Anakin Skywalker in disguise) get the [[antidote]] for her. Poggle and Dod then confronted Clovis about the missing [[Hologram disc|holodisc]]. ====Second Battle of Geonosis==== {{Quote|Poggle is out in the open, and I intend to grab him before he can get offworld.|Luminara Unduli|{{TCW|Legacy of Terror}}}} Poggle returned to Geonosis and served as the [[Overseer]] of the new [[Geonosis primary droid foundry]].[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]] However, the war would soon return to the Geonosian [[homeworld]]. When the Galactic Republic [[Second Battle of Geonosis|invaded]] the planet, Poggle led both the droid army and the native Geonosians against the Republic. As the Republic forces approached his foundry, Poggle and his [[T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|T-series tactical droid]], [[TX-21]], oversaw the construction of [[Separatist super-tank prototype|super tank]]s. They then deployed ten [[garrison]]s of droids against the [[Cloning|clone]] [[trooper]]s serving under [[Jedi General]]s Anakin Skywalker and [[Luminara Unduli]]. Poggle and TX-21 then sent-in the super tanks, which were able to push the clones back. Poggle was then informed that two Jedi had infiltrated the reactor room; accompanied by a pair of soldiers and one of his super tanks, Poggle ordered his soldiers to [[bomb]] the Jedi.{{TCW|Weapons Factory}} [[File:PoggleRetreat-LegacyOfTerror.png|thumb|left|275px|Poggle escaped to the Temple in a damaged AAT]] After the foundry's destruction, Poggle took an [[Armored Assault Tank Mk I|AAT]], along with several of his droids and soldiers, to the [[Progate Temple]]. Along the way, Poggle dropped crates, leaving a trail for Unduli and clone trooper [[Buzz]] to follow; when the two entered the temple, Poggle and several undead Geonosians ambushed and killed Buzz, and captured Unduli. Poggle then took her into the catacombs of the temple and brought her before his queen, Karina the Great, as a gift. Together, they hoped they could use Geonosian [[brain worm]]s to control Unduli. However, Poggle and Karina were soon discovered by Kenobi and Skywalker. As they blinded the queen, Poggle was captured by Skywalker and Unduli. He was taken aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Resolute]]''.{{TCW|Brain Invaders}} On board the ''Resolute'', Poggle was [[Torture|interrogated]] by Kenobi, [[Ki-Adi-Mundi]], and Unduli, but refused to answer their questions. When the worms were aboard his Padawan's [[TB-73|supply ship]], Skywalker interrogated Poggle alone. At first, Poggle refused but was then punched and [[Telekinesis|Force-choke]]d by the Jedi. He then revealed the worms' weakness to the [[Temperature|cold]]. Poggle was then transported to [[Coruscant]], where he was [[Prison|imprisoned]] in a cell at the [[Imperial Inspectorate HQ|Republic Center for Military Operations]].{{TCW|The Jedi Who Knew Too Much}} ====Imprisonment and Republic service==== {{Quote|Whatever it is can wait, Poggle. Your workers are dismantling everything they put together.''"
"''Try not to be too hard on them. They are simply following my orders.|Orson Krennic and Archduke Poggle the Lesser during his escape|}} [[File:PoggleIncarcerated-TJWKTM.png|thumb|right|270px|Poggle was incarcerated in the Republic Center for Military Operations]] During his [[time]] in prison, Poggle was subjected to routine interrogation by agents of [[Republic Intelligence]]. One of the main topics, even though information on it was removed by Poggle from the [[Geonosian War Room|Stalgasin war room]], of the interrogations was the supposed deep-space mobile [[battle station]] project, the "Ultimate [[Weapon]]" designed by the Stalgasin hive, that was thought to be under construction by the Confederacy. However, the Archduke repeatedly denied any Geonosian association, and feigned ignorance to the existence of the plans, which were actually in the possession of the [[Republic Special Weapons Group]]. Poggle was later approached by [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] of the Special Weapons Group, in another attempt to garner information on the Confederacy's Ultimate Weapon. Krennic, who himself was attempting to spearhead the [[Project Stardust|project]] to develop the station, was able to appeal to Poggle's loyalty to his people and convinced him to provide the Geonosian drone population as a workforce for the battle-station's construction. While Poggle would ultimately agree to Krennic's offer, he was still within a Center for Military Operations cell in [[19 BBY]].{{TCWcanondates|518}} Poggle took to flying in its midst while being watched by secruity cameras and was captured as such one day as, unknown to him, Ahsoka Tano—the same Jedi Padawan who had helped to destroy his foundry during the Second Battle of Geonosis and whom he had confronted face-to-face—was framed for the murder of anti-war activist [[Letta Turmond]] in another cell. The culprit was none-other-than Barriss Offee,{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}} the other Padawan whom Poggle had confronted and lost his factory to. With his supposed allegiance to the Republic established, the Archduke was returned to his homeworld on the eve of [[Meckgin]], in which, amidst [[blood]]y celebrations, was able to convince the Geonosians to assist in the Republic's construction efforts. However, Poggle had ulterior motives for providing such assistance to the Republic. Allotted with a private retinue of drones, Poggle secretly directed a massive uprising of the Geonosian soldiers servicing the battle-station as a diversion for his own escape to the Confederacy. In addition to sabotaging the construction project, the Archduke, with his own modified personal [[shuttle]], was able to [[Uprising on Geonosis|slip through]] the [[Republic Navy|Republic flotilla]] in [[orbit]] and flee into [[hyperspace]]. ====Last days of the Clone Wars==== After escaping from Geonosis, Poggle rejoined the Confederacy as the war began to draw to its close. An image of Poggle on the Separatist Council was included in the survival compendium "[[Neyo's Almanac of Clankers]]."{{GermanFanCite|122|Database}} Following a string of Republic victories, General Grievous ordered the members of the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]], including Poggle, to remain under his protection. Grievous hid them on [[Utapau]] while he prepared a [[Battle of Coruscant|strike]] on Coruscant. Following Count Dooku's death and Grievous's failure at Coruscant, Poggle and the other Separatist leaders met with Grievous on Utapau. During the meeting, he informed them that he was transferring them to the [[Volcano|volcanic]] planet of [[Mustafar]] for their own safety. Grievous then dismissed the council, telling them that their ship was waiting shortly before his own [[Battle of Utapau|death]]. ====Death==== {{Quote|When my new apprentice, Darth Vader, arrives, he will... take care of you.|Darth Sidious, to Poggle and the other Separatist leaders|}} [[File:PoggleDies-ROTS.png|thumb|left|250px|Poggle's death at the hands of Darth Vader]] After arriving on Mustafar, Poggle and the rest of the Council settled in a [[Klegger Corp Mining Facility|fortified bunker]]. Soon after, they were contacted by Darth Sidious, who had informed them that his new [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], Darth Vader, would be arriving shortly, but claimed that he had come to make peace with them. When Vader arrived on Mustafar, the Separatist leaders discovered that he was sent not to reward the council, but to [[Mission to Mustafar|execute]] them. Poggle attempted to defend himself using his staff, to no avail, and was quickly [[Dismemberment|decapitated]]. Vader would eventually murder Gunray, shut down the Battle Droids and end the Clone Wars. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|With Poggle dead, the hive queen has appointed a new archduke to oversee the soldiers and drones, but the process is nothing more than conciliatory.|Lt. Commander Orson Krennic, to [[Governor]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]]|}} After Poggle's death, a [[Unidentified Geonosian archduke|new archduke]] was appointed by the hive queen. However, the appointment was really a way to placate the Geonosians, as the [[species]] now essentially belonged to the Republic's successor state, the [[Galactic Empire]]. The Geonosisans continued to be used in the battle station project the Republic had started, which was dubbed the "Death Star." To keep the Death Star a secret, the Empire [[Sterilization of Geonosis|sterilized]] the population of Geonosis, with only [[Klik-Klak|one Geonosian]] surviving.''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' [[Standard decade|Decade]]s later, Poggle was mentioned in the ''[[Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'', a survival guide written by [[Hondo Ohnaka]] and [[DK-RA-43]].''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|How many of you have gazed into the heavens at night and seen something new taking shape above our world? A crescent, a circle, a gleaming ring that is like the portal to another dimension?|Poggle the Lesser describes the Death Star to his subjects|}} [[File:WeServeTheQueen-SWL113.png|thumb|right|250px|Poggle the Lesser was a cunning and charismatic leader.]] A male Geonosian who rose to the rank of archduke from that of a drone, Poggle the Lesser was an early and loyal supporter of the Confederacy of Independent Systems. While he attempted to distance Geonosis from the Separatists in front of Orson Krennic and other Republic representatives after his freedom from Republic capture, he, in time, was able to escape back to the Separatists, having never truly given his loyalty over to the Republic. ==Skills and abilities== Poggle was a powerful and cunning leader, being skilled at military tactics as well as negotiating. He also possessed a knowledge of [[engineer]]ing. ==Equipment== Poggle wielded the [[Staff of Command]], which was the symbol of his office. Made of [[bone]] allegedly taken from a conquered adversary, it also served as a walking stick and, due to its sharp point, a weapon if the Geonosian ruler ever felt the need to motivate or punish those around him. He was [[Clothing|clothed]] in ornate and aristocratic garments that reflected his position, wealth, and power. For similar reasons, Poggle also wore jewels as well as chain-like [[visgura thread]]. His chosen emblem of rank was [[Spider|arachnid]]-inspired, crafted from the [[egg]] cases of an extinct [[giant cave spider]]. ==Behind the scenes== Poggle the Lesser was portrayed by [[Marton Csokas]] and voiced by [[Ernie Fosselius]] in the [[2002]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], the second installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]]. The character later returned in a nonspeaking capacity in the [[2005]] sequel [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. He was voiced by [[Matthew Wood]] in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' animated series. [[File:Poggle_maquette.jpg|left|thumb|142x142px|Poggle's marquette]] On [[July 18]], [[2000]], [[StarWars.com]] announced that Csokas would join the cast of ''Attack of the Clones'' in a role that was described as that of "a [[planet]]ary leader", an announcement that was accompanied by casting director [[Robin Gurland]]'s praise for Csokas' talents.{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/production/news20000718.html|text=Casting Update: Local Talent Continues}} Initially written to have a major role in the screenplay, Poggle's role was reduced by the time production started running.{{InsiderCite|65|Behind the Magic}} However, as the film neared completition, Csokas was informed by Gurland through a letter that his performance would be removed despite keeping a credit for it due to director [[George Lucas]] taking the decision that Poggle should be rendered through visual effects and voiced by sound effects.{{WebCite|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/lifestyle/marton-csokas-swimming-with-hollywood-sharks/LEFFTUWT7F2G5DOAYLHGKTX3YQ|text=Marton Csokas, swimming with Hollywood sharks|author=Baillie, Russell|work=[[Wikipedia:The New Zealand Herald|The New Zealand Herald]]|archivedate=20201113204338}} Poggle would be ultimately realized by having [[Industrial Light & Magic]] animator [[Charles Alleneck]] serve as the moddle to animate his movements and sound designer [[Ben Burtt]] recorded himself reading the character's lines and playing them backwards during rehearsals, but later in production, Burtt recorded Fosselius reciting Poggle's dialogue in reverse, who also recorded some [[Wikipedia:Swahili language|Swahili]]-type clicking noises and the sound of blowing on the edge of a piece of paper, with all of this added to Poggle's voice in the finished product.''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]'' In the DVD commentary of ''Attack of the Clones'', it is stated that Poggle was made to look different than other Geonosians so it was obvious he was their leader, similar to how [[Boss]] [[Rugor Nass|Nass]] was designed to look different from the other [[Gungan]]s.{{Film|II}} DVD commentary In a [[Content cut from Star Wars|deleted scene]] for ''Attack of the Clones'', Poggle sentences Anakin and Padmé to their deaths, finding them guilty of espionage, leading [[Nute Gunray]] to hurry him up to give the sentence. In the final cut of ''Revenge of the Sith'', Poggle gets cut in half by Darth Vader.
