[[Tatooine]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} |species=[[Twi'lek]]{{Databank|bib-fortuna|Bib Fortuna}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=2 [[meter]]s |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color|Red]][[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]] |skin=Pale |cyber= |families=[[Fortuna family]]''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=[[Jabba's criminal empire]]{{Film|VI}} |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Jabba the Hutt is dead, long live Jabba the Hutt. His empire is now ripe for the taking, and I, for one, know just the person to lead it to greatness.|Bib Fortuna|{{StoryCite|story=Fortuna Favors the Bold|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}}}} '''Bib Fortuna''' was a [[Twi'lek]] [[Gender|male]] who lived on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. He served as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]'s [[majordomo]] and chief of staff for [[Standard decade|decades]], handling all of the day-to-day operations at [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]], while secretly hating the Hutt and longing for a chance to [[Death|kill]] him in order to assume his place. By [[32 BBY]], Fortuna had assumed the position as Jabba's majordomo, and it was he and the [[Hutt]] who oversaw that year's [[Boonta Eve Classic]], in which a nine-year-old [[Anakin Skywalker]] won the podrace. By the time of the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Fortuna continued to serve Jabba as his right-hand-man. In [[19 BBY]], Fortuna contacted [[Ciddarin Scaleback|Cid]] and asked that she retrieve a [[rancor]], [[Muchi]], from [[Zygerrian]] [[enslaver]]s. With the help of [[Clone Force 99]], Murchi was brought to Fortuna, who in turn brought the rancor to Jabba. Twenty-three years later, and Fortuna continued to serve Jabba. That year, [[Luke Skywalker]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] went to Tatooine to rescue [[Han Solo]]. During a battle over the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]], Jabba was [[Death|killed]] by [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and his sail barge, [[Khetanna]], was destroyed. Following Jabba's death, Fortuna assumed control of his palace as a [[crime lord]], becoming obese in the process. In [[9 ABY]], Fortuna was killed by [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]], who took over his [[Fett gotra|throne]]. ==Biography== ===Early years=== {{Quote|What a pleasant surprise. I'm graced by the presence of Jabba's right-hand man.|Cid|{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}}} [[File:Jabba_Boonta_Eve.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Bib Fortuna came to serve Jabba the Hutt]] A [[Gender|male]] [[Twi'lek]], Bib Fortuna hailed from [[Ryloth]], the [[homeworld]] of his [[species]]. Fortuna was [[Reproduction|born]] to a [[Fortuna family|prominent clan]] that had close ties to the criminal underworld, though his more politically minded cousin [[Beezer Fortuna|Beezer]] resented his family's associations. Before coming into the service of [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], Fortuna worked as a [[Slavery|slave]] trader, one who was focused on members of his own species. He became rich from selling his fellow Twi'leks into slavery.''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' At some point, Fortuna came into Jabba's service and competed against [[Bidlo Kwerve]] to become the Hutt's [[majordomo]].[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] Fortuna also gave Jabba his pet [[rancor]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' [[Pateesa]]''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' as a [[birthday]] present. Ultimately, Fortuna succeeded and claimed the job whereas Kwerve ended up as an early victim of the rancor. In truth, however, Fortuna hated Jabba and longed to find a chance to [[Death|kill]] him, hoping to claim [[Jabba's criminal empire]] for himself. [[File:Bib_TPM.png|thumb|right|250px|Fortuna attends the Boonta Eve Classic.]] He served as Jabba's majordomo as far back as the [[time]] of the [[Invasion of Naboo]],{{Film|I}} in [[32 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' That [[Standard year|year]], Fortuna attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic]], which his master hosted to commemorate the [[Boonta Eve]] holiday.{{Databank|boonta-eve-classic-podracer-pilots|Boonta Eve Classic Podracer Pilots}} From his master's private balcony, he witnessed the victory of a local [[human]] boy named [[Anakin Skywalker]] against the reigning champion [[Sebulba]]. As the Hutt was not interested in podracing aside from the [[gambling]] aspect of the sport, Jabba fell asleep before the end of the race, forcing Fortuna to wake him up in order to announce the ending. ===Imperial Era=== ====The Ord Mantell ordeal==== {{Quote|Assure your employer he'll be reunited with Muchi soon.|Cid, to Bib Fortuna|}} [[File:Bib-and-Cid.png|thumb|left|270px|Tired of her promises, Bib Fortuna personally journeyed to Cid's office for an update on the rescue of Muchi.]] As the years of [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]] passed, Fortuna continued to serve Jabba as the [[Galactic Republic]] was reorganized into the [[Galactic Empire]].{{Film|III}} In [[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' places the events of [[The Bad Batch Season 1|''The Bad Batch'' Season 1]] in [[19 BBY]]. during the early [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Imperial Era]], Fortuna came into contact with [[Ciddarin Scaleback|Cid]], a [[Trandoshan]] who operated on the planet [[Ord Mantell]], and hired her to [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Clone Force 99)|retrieve]] the young [[rancor]] [[Muchi]] from a group of [[Zygerrian]] [[enslaver]]s. As [[time]] passed and Muchi was not yet rescued, however, Fortuna contacted her via [[hologram]], informing her that Jabba was impatient and wanted to know why the rancor had not yet been returned.{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}} {{AD|Disney+}} As she ate, Cid noted that the operation required a delay due to planning and asked him to assure Jabba that Muchi would soon be rescued. Although Fortuna attempted to threaten her, Cid remained unintimidated, claiming she had her best team working to save the rancor. Cid had actually hired [[Clone Force 99]], a group of [[clone commando]] deserters she had only just met and who she was uncertain could actually succeed. With Muchi still not returned to Jabba, Fortuna arrived personally at [[Cid's Parlor]] with two [[Gamorrean Warrior]]s, entering into her office and demanding an update on behalf of Jabba. Cid again claimed Muchi would be rescued, trying to ease his concerns after he threatened consequences for failure by noting how delicate the operation was. Before Fortuna could respond to her request that Jabba be patient, Muchi was heard outside, as Clone Force 99 had succeeded in their mission. Quickly getting outside to reunite with Muchi, the majordomo was overjoyed to see his master's pet safe, greeting the young rancor before ordering a guard to give Cid her payment with a snap. With the rancor safe, Fortuna told her they would return home before leaving with his guards. Cid proceeded to give Clone Force 99 thirty percent of Fortuna's payment, as they had agreed upon. ====Solo troubles==== {{Quote|''«Marshal Buck Vancto''. To what do I owe the pleasure? And by 'pleasure,' I, of course, mean having my afternoon ''interrupted''.''»
"''I'm pursuing a ''warrant'' out for Han Solo. I'm given reason to believe he's doing a job for your slug as we speak.|quotestart=0|Bib Fortuna and Buck Vancto|[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 2|''Han Solo & Chewbacca'' 2]]}} Later in the Imperial Era, Jabba welcomed two new [[smuggler]]s into his employ, the [[Corellian]] human [[Han Solo]] and his [[Wookiee]] [[Pilot|co-pilot]] [[Chewbacca]]. As the Hutt's majordomo, Fortuna often found himself dealing with the pair, handing them assignments from Jabba and delineating their pay. One such assignment[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 1|''Han Solo & Chewbacca'' 1]] between around [[8 BBY]] and [[2 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars: Han Solo & Chewbacca]]'' to between around [[8 BBY]] and [[2 BBY]]. was no different, as Fortuna informed Solo that the Hutt [[lord]] was willing to pay one million [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for the delivery of a [[verillix]] [[Unidentified urn|urn]] that contained the ashes of [[Krestrel D'Naran]], a rival of Jabba. To Solo's dismay, Fortuna also specified that the smugglers would be required to work with [[Greedo]], a [[Rodian]] [[bounty hunter]] of Jabba's who had been the first to learn of the urn. Reluctantly, the trio agreed to the [[Heist on Corellia|job]] and headed for Solo's homeworld of [[Corellia]]. With some personal time to spare, Fortuna gallivanted to the streets of [[Mos Espa]] to bet on [[nuna]] fights, where he promptly lost one thousand of his own credits. During his time off, Fortuna was questioned by an old acquaintance, [[Buck Vancto]] of the [[Benelex Marshal Service]], who was pursuing a warrant put out on Solo for a recent [[heist on Galator III]]. Knowing that the Twi'lek owed him a favor, Vancto threatened to drag Fortuna back to Ryloth should he not disclose Solo's location. Although Fortuna took the [[marshal]]'s warning seriously, he feared retribution from Jabba, and agreed to divulge the information so long as Vancto waited to apprehend Solo until after the smuggler had completed his mission. ===Galactic Civil War=== ====Conflicts on Tatooine==== {{Quote|Those men worked for my master, the mighty Jabba the Hutt. He is most displeased with your hostility.|Bib Fortuna contacts the mercenaries following the battle|''[[Star Wars: Commander]]''}} During the [[Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]], the Twi'lek remained in Jabba's service. A short time after the [[Battle of Yavin]], which had cost the Empire its [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]], the Empire elected to open negotiations with Jabba, but a [[Heroes of Yavin|Rebel strike team]] took advantage of the negotiations to [[Assault on Cymoon|destroy]] [[Weapons Factory Alpha]]. Following that loss, the Empire moved negotiations to take place at Jabba's Palace, but the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader arrived a day early to request bounty hunters for private business. After Vader arrived and [[Death|killed]] two [[Gamorrean]] warriors, Fortuna ran to the [[Sith]] to speak with him, only to be met with a [[Darth Vader's lightsaber|lightsaber]] and a demand to see Jabba. Rushing to his master, Fortuna awoke him and informed him of what had happened. Fortuna stood beside Jabba as he began to talk with Vader, who ordered him to remove the audience so they could talk in private. After Jabba had many of them return in a failed attempt to collect the [[bounty]] on Vader's head, the Sith Lord threatened him with a [[Force choke]], and the Hutt crime lord acquiesced, having his two best bounty hunters—[[Boba Fett]] and [[Krrsantan]]—dispatched to fulfill Vader's missions.[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] The following day, Vader returned to oversee the Empire's official negotiations, accompanied by [[stormtrooper]]s. Although Fortuna tried to greet Vader, the Sith Lord cut off his pleasantries, beginning the ultimately successful negotiations with Jabba.[[Star Wars (2015) 4|''Star Wars'' (2015) 4]] At some point between the Battle of [[Yavin]] and [[Battle of Hoth]], Fortuna contacted the Tatooinian [[mercenary]] [[Saponza]] and [[Saponza's partner|his partner]] in the name of Jabba. The two men had reacted violently to the presence of Jabba's henchmen around [[Saponza's homestead]], killing six of them. Fortuna let the two mercenaries know they had made an enemy of his Hutt master. Some time later, Jabba's henchmen razed Saponza's estate to the ground in retaliation, and the majordomo contacted Saponza once again to gloat over his misfortune and warn him that Jabba's revenge was not over. ====Return of Crimson Dawn==== {{Quote|All of you want to live. Who doesn't? But I promise. Fight me…some of you die. Maybe ''most'' of you. And you'd be dying…for ''him''. Doesn't seem fair, does it?|Boba Fett convinces Jabba's court not to lay their lives down for Bib Fortuna|[[War of the Bounty Hunters 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 1]]}} In [[3 ABY]], Boba Fett [[Escape from Cloud City|captured]] Han Solo, who had since fallen out of Jabba's favor and earned a price on his head from the mighty Hutt. En route to the crime lord's [[Boba Fett's Palace|Tatooinian palace]] with his [[bounty]], Fett contacted Fortuna and assured the majordomo that Solo was alive, safely secured within [[Carbon-freezing|frozen]] [[carbonite]]. To Fortuna's confusion, however, Fett abruptly ended their communication when the [[carbonite matrix]] containing Solo became unstable, forcing him to take a detour to [[Nar Shaddaa]] to fix the issue. There, Solo was stolen from Fett[[War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha'' 1]] by agents of [[Crimson Dawn]], a [[The galaxy|galactic]] crime syndicate that had long been considered obsolete. Fett declined to immediately inform Fortuna of his bad luck, instead simply telling the Twi'lek that his delivery would "be a [[Standard minute|minute]]." Representing the interests of an increasingly impatient Jabba, Fortuna warned Fett not to disappoint the mighty Hutt lord. Soon after, Crimson Dawn sent invitations to many of the major crime lords in the galaxy, including Jabba. Revealing that they held Solo in their possession, they bid the invitees to travel to [[Jekara]] and witness the return of Crimson Dawn. Believing that Fett had cheated him and sold the smuggler to a competitor, Jabba placed a bounty on the [[Hunting|hunter's]] head before departing for Jekara, leaving Fortuna to look over his palace. Unaware that the Hutt had left, Fett stormed through the castle's dusty gates, incinerating two Gamorrean guards and demanding that Fortuna give him answers. After explaining that his master was absent, Fortuna suggested that Fett leave, lest the retinue of thugs and mercenaries that made up Jabba's court turn their weapons on the hunter. Fett reminded the rabble, however, that many of their number would perish in a firefight against him, dying in the meager name of Bib Fortuna. With this in mind, no one fired a shot. At the behest of Fett, Fortuna showed him Jabba's invitation, which depicted a [[Qi'ra|human woman]] requesting that her audience "await the Dawn." Accepting her as his new target, Fett ordered Fortuna to have his ship, ''[[Slave I]]'', repaired of damage it had sustained on Nar Shaddaa before leaving for Jekara himself. Fett was eventually successful in his mission, managing to retrieve the frozen Han Solo and deliver him to Jabba intact. At some point before or during [[4 ABY]],{{SW|url=news/the-illustrious-jabba-the-hutt-bids-you-welcome-to-his-new-marvel-comic-jabbas-palace-exclusive-reveal|text=The Illustrious Jabba the Hutt Bids You Welcome to His New Marvel Comic, ''Jabba's Palace'' - Exclusive Reveal}} establishes that [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (2023)|''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'']], including [[Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion 1|''Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion'' 1]], takes place in the era of {{Film|VI}}, which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. As ''Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion'' 1 establishes that Zarah Bliss had [[Death|died]] prior to the events of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]], she must have died by 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]]. Fortuna helped ensure that [[Zeva Bliss]] could arise to power over the [[Spice Runners of Kijimi]], further ensuring that her mother and its current leader, [[Zarah Bliss]], fell from power,[[Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising 2|''Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising'' 2]] with Zarah ultimately dying.[[Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion 1|''Return of the Jedi – The Rebellion'' 1]] ====Trouble at the Great Pit of Carkoon==== =====Enter the Rebellion===== {{Quote|Die wanna wanga!|Bib Fortuna|}} [[File:BibFortunaJabba-CGSWG.png|thumb|right|250px|Fortuna serving alongside Jabba at the palace during the Galactic Civil War.]] Later in the war, Fortuna greeted two [[droid]] visitors to his master's palace. The two mechanical units, called [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]], claimed that they had a gift for the Hutt. The majordomo demanded that they hand over that gift to him so he could bring it to Jabba himself, but the droids answered that their instructions were to give it only to the crime lord himself. Fortuna relented, and led the droids into the throne room, where they delivered a [[Hologram|holographic message]] from their owner, the Rebel hero and fledgling [[Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. In the message, Skywalker asked to bargain for the life of his friend Han Solo, offering C-3PO and R2-D2 in exchange. Fortuna was present when [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] arrived under the disguise of notorious bounty hunter [[Boushh]]. She brought along a chained Chewbacca and demanded a higher payment for the Wookiee's capture, under the threat of a [[thermal detonator]]. Later that night, Fortuna was hiding alongside Jabba as part of the Hutt's plan to capture Organa when she attempted to free Solo herself. Jabba had Solo sent to the dungeons, while Organa was enslaved. =====Mind-tricked majordomo===== {{Quote|He's no Jedi.|Bib Fortuna, to Jabba the Hutt, regarding Luke Skywalker|}} The next morning Luke Skywalker [[Rescue of Han Solo|arrived]] to rescue his friends. Fortuna tried to stop him from entering the audience chamber. However, he was influenced by Skywalker's [[mind trick]], though he was not as weak-minded as some of Jabba's other guards. Skywalker only succeeded in his mind trick by finding and exploiting Fortuna's weak point,''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]'' his alleged strong loyalty to Jabba. Fortuna proceeded to wake Jabba, and presented the Jedi to his master. Angry that Fortuna had been manipulated by Skywalker, Jabba pushed him off his dais. As the negotiations became more tense, Jabba dropped Skywalker into the rancor pit. After the Jedi slew the beast, he was imprisoned and sentenced to death, with Jabba wanting him executed at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]]. =====Making preparations===== Before the visit to Carkoon, Fortuna prepped [[Klatooine paddy frogs]] in a larder in the palace. One of the creatures escaped containment, causing Fortuna to decide an excruciating death for the paddy frog, though the Twi'lek's thoughts were interrupted by a delivery droid beeping at him. After deciphering the beeps, Fortuna ordered the droid to put the paddy frog pallet in the middle of the larder. As the droid left, Fortuna thought about calling the droid back and getting the pallet delivered to its correct location but did not like the thought of communicating with the droid without C-3PO, who was already aboard Jabba's [[sail barge]], the ''[[Khetanna]]''. Fortuna briefly thought about turning his hidden blaster on the droid but restrained himself as his blaster was a one-shot weapon, and he hated enacting vengeance on immaterial annoyances. As a rumbling laughter shook the walls of the palace, the Twi'lek took a step backwards, accidentally killing the paddy frog. As Jabba's laughter continued, Fortuna instinctively reached for the blaster in his cloak. Taking a deep breath and relaxing, he removed the blaster from his clothing and stuck the pistol to a wall—with sticky paddy-frog residue—behind a stack of beverage tanks where no one would see it. Using a datapad, the Twi'lek instructed for the tanks to be loaded onto the ''Khetanna''. Clenching a fist as the Hutt continued to laugh, Fortuna had the plan of murdering his master that day. To the majordomo's annoyance, the delivery droid returned, this time with more paddy-frogs. The Twi'lek sighed and wondered if there was a second blaster he could use. Now in the palace's hanger bay, as one of Jabba's skiff's needed fixing, Fortuna was of half a mind to blow the vehicle up. His thoughts went to Jabba, who he was lost in a fantasy about killing, until a Gamorrean went up to him for a question. The alien communicated that that there would be eight guards on the skiff holding the prisoners. After Fortuna told the Gamorrean that only seven guards were necessary, the alien continued that he'd heard Jabba wanted to be there during the execution. Realizing that one more guard on the sail barge was one more in the way of him getting to kill Jabba, Fortuna let the Gamorrean keep the guard on the skiff. The majordomo then told the Gamorrean to leave and close the door on the way out, which he did punching the door controls, making Fortuna give a snarl of frustration that could be heard from throughout the palace. =====Execution time===== Fortuna accompanied Jabba and many of his palace denizens to the pit. One the way over, Jabba pulled Organa over to him, telling her she will soon learn to appreciate him as Fortuna pushed her to him. As the ''Khetanna'' arrived at its destination, Fortuna looked out a window to view the proceedings, before moving to sit in the sail barge's kitchen. As he thought about leaving Jabba's service and realized that Jabba would kill him as he knew too much, Max Rebo entered for keys to his instrument. He told the Ortolan that he really should get back to the topside of the sail barge to check in on the serving droids, and that he would string the droid manager up if one of his charges went rogue. The rebels managed to escape custody, kill Jabba, and destroy his sail barge. Though he was presumed to have died in the explosion,{{HelmetCollectionCite|18|Databank A-Z}} Fortuna survived the battle.{{InsiderCite|219|Day Wanna Wanga - The Tale of the Twi'leks}} ===Death=== {{Quote|Boba. I thought you were dead. I am so glad to see you. I had heard many rumors.|translated=1|Bib Fortuna's final words|}} [[File:Bib_Fortuna_MS2-EP8.png|thumb|left|200px|Fortuna as a crime lord]] After Jabba's death, Fortuna gained control of Jabba's palace and amassed servants and slaves of his own, becoming a crime lord.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} {{AD|Disney+}} Over time, he lived an unhealthy lifestyle consisting of over-indulgence and inactivity.''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' Years into Fortuna's reign,{{Topps|set=2023 Topps Star Wars|cardname=8D8|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/370777/cid/22170335}} after the [[Assault on Moff Gideon's cruiser|second rescue of Grogu]], Boba Fett and his companion [[Fennec Shand]] [[Attack on Jabba's Palace (Boba Fett)|arrived]] at the palace, killing Fortuna's guards and releasing an [[Unidentified Rutian Twi'lek|enslaved individual]] of Fortuna's. The Twi'lek greeted Fett and said he believed the bounty hunter had died, and that he had heard many rumors regarding him. Fett immediately shot Fortuna, killing him and assuming Fortuna's throne in the palace. Following his death, Boba Fett visited the many vassals of Jabba the Hutt and Bib to continue the crime underworld on Tatooine. Unlike Bib Fortuna and Jabba, Boba intended to rule with respect, catching the eye of many.{{BOBF|Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land}} According to Fennec Shand, Fortuna was a terrible leader with no right to the throne.{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}} ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Great Jabba… I regret to inform you… a Coruscant cartel figured out how to ''synthesize'' the desert wine… and n-now… it's… it's… worthless.''»
«''Worthless? No, fool… ''[drinks the desert wine]'' it was ''priceless''.|translated=1|Bib Fortuna and Jabba the Hutt|[[Age of Rebellion - Jabba the Hutt 1|''Age of Rebellion - Jabba the Hutt'' 1]]}} [[File:FortunaAgainstSandPeople-AORJabba1.png|thumb|right|250px|The majordomo of Jabba the Hutt, Bib Fortuna would greet all who arrived at his master's palace.]] A pasty-faced male Twi'lek who served Jabba the Hutt for decades despite secretly hating the Hutt, Fortuna greeted all those who sought an audience with the Hutt, forcing those who wanted to meet with Jabba to maneuver past the majordomo. Even so, Fortuna at times understood his duties included denying visitors permission to see Jabba, whom he called his master. The majordomo held great patience thanks to his job, needing to deal with individuals ranging from haughty emissaries to drunken ruffians. Even so, the Trandoshan Cid felt that Fortuna could get too impatient and nervous when an operation was taking a long time. Additionally, his master's own volatile mood was another possible job hazard, especially because Jabba did not have the same respect Fortuna showed towards him; Jabba believed Fortuna to be a fool. Indeed, the majordomo proved to be weak minded enough for Luke Skywalker to use a mind trick on him once Skywalker exploited his seeming loyalty to the Hutt. Otherwise, Fortuna was not as weak minded as some of Jabba's other guards. When not leaving Jabba's side to greet visitors or travel off-planet, Fortuna often remained at the side of his master, whispering advice and information. When talking, Fortuna elected to only speak [[Huttese]] despite understanding other languages and sometimes using words from [[Galactic Basic Standard]]. Fortuna was also willing to threaten business partners in order to try to get better results. Able to represent Jabba on off-world missions, a visit from the greatest ally of the Hutt was considered an honor, although Cid mocked Fortuna during one such occasion. Nevertheless, Fortuna cared greatly about Jabba's interests, being overjoyed when the rancor Muchi was rescued. Fortuna also cared greatly for Muchi, calling the rancor his "sweet girl." Following the minimal protocol rules that existed in Jabba's court and marking excessive concerns with propriety and modesty, Fortuna was mortified upon hearing Sy Snootles's saucy lyrics for the song ''[[Jedi Rocks]]''. Fortuna maintained a list of seven hundred and sixty-two items that he hated. At the top of the list was none other than Jabba, and Klatooine paddy frogs were also far up, although Fortuna was ultimately able to develop a taste for them. Item three hundred and five was wastefulness, and according to his recollection, maintenance requests were in the six hundreds. He also had no love for the bounty hunter Boba Fett, whom he thought of as a suck-up and a stumbling glory-hound. Max Rebo was at one point on his list, though the Ortolan found his way off due to his jatz-wail music capturing the tense feeling of working for a crime lord. Fortuna would have deeply loved to have used his "conversation starter" tools on Luke Skywalker, as he had, in the Twi'lek's mind, made a fool of him. Upon learning of Jabba's death, Fortuna laughed madly and decided to begin eating the paddy frogs he had previously hated, electing to cement himself as his own master by trying the second most hated item on his list. While he was a crime lord, Fortuna had grown larger in size and was scared of Fett, attempting to act friendly to the bounty hunter, only for his attempts to fail when Fett assassinated him. ==Equipment== During his servitude to Jabba, Fortuna wore a black-colored overcoat, black boots, and a chestplate.''[[Star Wars Costumes: The Original Trilogy]]'' In order to document his extensive list of things he hated, Fortuna, for redundancy's sake, used three datapads and the memory banks of a repurposed service droid. When executions were scheduled, the Twi'lek had favorited tools that he called "conversation starters," which he used to extract information from the people sent to death. After taking control of Jabba's palace[[Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising 2|''Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising'' 2]] in 4 ABY,The events of ''[[Star Wars: Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising]]'' take place after the [[Battle of Endor]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. The series is also set before the events of ''[[Star Wars: Battle of Jakku — Republic Under Siege]]'', which in turn are before the [[Liberation of Sullust]], an event dated to 4 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]] by ''Timelines''. Fortuna wore bandages on his head and lekku. By 9 ABY, he sat upon a throne and wielded a staff. ==Behind the scenes== ===Creation and costume=== {{Quote|He was one of my favorite characters. Phil started the design and I picked it up. I actually did a whole bunch of those Twi'lek creatures, because I wanted to populate them all over the place.|Nilo-Rodis Jamero|}} Bib Fortuna was played by [[Michael Carter]] and voiced uncredited by the late [[Erik Bauersfeld]], who also voiced [[Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar]], in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. In earlier drafts of ''Return of the Jedi'', Fortuna's title was the "High Beeser of [[Hoth]]," and his original design sketches depicted him as a wizened old human man sporting a dark cloak and a tall hat. References to this title and design, however, were left out from the finished version of the film.{{DB|character|bibfortuna|Fortuna, Bib}} The character's sharp fingernails and teeth were inspired by a [[Wikipedia:National Geographic|''National Geographic'']] article on the indigenous people of [[Wikipedia:Borneo|Borneo]], which to [[Nilo Rodis-Jamero|Nilo-Rodis Jamero]] was a favorite source of inspiration. The makeup process that Michael Carter needed to perform to create the custom of Bib Fortuna took over eight hours to first transform Carter into the Twi'lek advisor. By the end of Carter's five-week shoot, make-up artist [[Nick Dudman]] had streamlined the process down to 58 minutes. Removing the make-up took another 25 minutes. The most intricate effect was Fortuna's "air bladders" or bubbles. These were made of foam and latex that were fitted in Carter's brows and temples and inflated by off-stage-operated hoses to make them appear to pulsate. Carter also used dayglow orange contacts and claw-like finger extensions.{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-7-things-you-might-not-know-about-twileks|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 7 Things You Might Not Know About Twi'leks}} ===Later appearances=== Fortuna was portrayed by sound engineer [[Matthew Wood]] in{{DB|character|bibfortuna|Fortuna, Bib}} the podrace scene in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film ''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace]]'', who remained uncredited for the role. [[Alan Ruscoe]] also played a different visually similar Twi'lek character in the film. The character was one of the aides of [[Senator]] [[Orn Free Taa]] on [[Coruscant]] and was nicknamed "Bib Fortuna" by the production crew, but was ultimately cut from the final film. However, Ruscoe still described his character as Fortuna in an interview with [[Star Wars Insider 117|''Star Wars Insider'' 117]] in [[2010]]. Ruscoe was initially only contracted to portay [[Plo Koon]] in the film, but ended up also portraying [[Daultay Dofine]] and "Fortuna". He wore a major three piece prostetic that took four hours to apply and two additional hours to remove. In the interview, Ruscoe empathized that it was "nothing" compared to the time Carter needed for his makeup and that the real work was done by the makeup artists and not him.{{InsiderCite|117|Phantom Menaces (article)}} [[Kilian Plunkett]] created unused concept art of Bib Fortuna during the initial production of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' in July [[2006]].''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' Wood later reprised his role as Fortuna in a post-credits scene in "[[Chapter 16: The Rescue]]," the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|season two]] finale of the live-action series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', released on [[December 18]], [[2020]],{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-december-2020|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in December 2020}} where he was subsequently killed. [[Jesse La Flair]] served as a stunt double in the episode. Concept art of the character for the episode was done by [[Christian Alzmann]], [[Ryan Church]] and [[Brian Matyas]]. Design director [[Doug Chiang]] told them that he would look different from his appearance in ''Return of the Jedi'', leading Church to design him with giant lekku longer than himself that he wrapped around his body. Matyas also drew him with more pieces of cloth and jewlery and without the chest armor he wore in the film.[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season Two)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season Two]] Wood again reprised his role in "[[Rampage (episode)|Rampage]]," the fifth episode of the [[The Bad Batch Season 1|first season]] of the animated series [[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]], released in 2021. Just because I haven't flown across the galaxy like you have doesn't make me some sort of ignorant hick.|Owen Lars, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|[[Star Wars (2015) 15|''Star Wars'' (2015) 15]]}} '''Owen Lars''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] from the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] who worked as a [[moisture farmer]]. He was the son of [[Aika Lars|Aika]] and [[Cliegg Lars]], and he became the stepbrother of [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] when Cliegg [[Marriage|married]] Anakin's mother, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]]. In [[22 BBY]], Shmi was [[Death|killed]] by [[Tusken Raider]]s, and Cliegg passed away soon after. Lars married his girlfriend, [[Beru Whitesun Lars|Beru Whitesun]], and they toiled to maintain the [[Lars homestead|homestead]]. In [[19 BBY]], Lars and his wife were contacted by Skywalker's [[Jedi Master]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], and they were tasked with caring for Skywalker's infant son, [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]]. Lars believed that Skywalker had died due to his role as a [[Jedi]], so to protect Luke, the [[farmer]] forbade Kenobi from visiting or [[Jedi training|training]] the boy. In the following [[Standard year|years]], Lars prevented Luke from knowing the truth about his father, and he kept the boy busy with [[farm]] work. In [[1 BBY]], Lars and Luke Skywalker purchased the [[Astromech droid|astromech]] [[droid]] [[R2-D2]], who, unbeknownst to them, possessed stolen [[Death Star plans|plans]] for the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]], an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] planet-destroying [[battle station]]. Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s tracked the droid to Lars' homestead, where they interrogated and murdered both him and his wife. When Skywalker discovered that his family had been killed, he left Tatooine with Kenobi to train as a Jedi, joining the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] and destroying the Death Star in the [[Battle of Yavin]]. ==Biography== ===Early life and tragedy=== {{Dialogue|Owen Lars|Where are you going?|Anakin Skywalker|To find my mother.|Cliegg Lars|Your mother's dead, son. Accept it.|attr=Owen Lars, Anakin Skywalker, and Cliegg Lars|src=}} Owen Lars was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Reproduction|born]] to the [[moisture farmer]] [[Cliegg Lars]]{{SWE|characters|cliegglars|Cliegg Lars}} and his [[Marriage|wife]], [[Aika Lars|Aika]], after they met on a bustling [[Core Worlds|Core World]]. When Aika died, the [[Parent|father]] and son traveled to Cliegg's [[homeworld]], the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Tatooine]], where they lived on the [[Lars homestead|Lars family's homestead]] near the [[City|township]] of [[Anchorhead]]. As a young man, Lars had a strong vision of who he wanted to become, believing that he should be rooted on Tatooine and focused on improving the homestead. During a trip to Anchorhead, Lars met a local girl named [[Beru Whitesun Lars|Beru Whitesun]],{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Owen Lars - Homestead}} a third-generation moisture farmer. The two fell in love and began dating. When Cliegg went to [[Mos Espa]] in search of a new farmhand, he met [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], a woman who was [[Slavery|enslaved]] by the [[Toydarian]] junk dealer [[Watto]]. Cliegg fell in love with Shmi, with Shmi returning his feelings. With the family working together, Watto was tricked into a losing gambling game over Shmi.''[[Queen's Hope]]'' With that, Cliegg purchased her, set her free, and married her. Lars loved his stepmother very much, but he saw her sadness whenever she thought of her son, [[Anakin Skywalker]], who had left Tatooine to join the [[Jedi Order]] on [[Coruscant]].{{Film|I}} Seeing his mother's sadness made Lars wonder how anyone could have left her behind. In the following years, the family lived quietly. [[File:Lars-family.png|thumb|left|300px|The Lars family tells Anakin Skywalker about Shmi Skywalker's abduction.]] Though Lars planned for a comfortable future on his family homestead, the peace was broken by [[22 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] to [[22 BBY]]. Since ''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' establishes that [[Shmi Skywalker Lars]] was abducted a [[Standard month|month]] before the events of the film, it can be deduced that Skywalker's abduction occurred by 22 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. when one morning, Shmi was attacked and abducted by [[Tusken Raider]]s. Furious, Lars' father rallied 29 other moisture farmers to help search for her. When the group returned, there were only four survivors, including Cliegg, who had lost a [[Limb|leg]] and used a [[repulsorlift chair]]. As [[time]] passed, Lars and his father had little hope for Shmi's survival. A [[Standard month|month]] later, Anakin Skywalker returned to Tatooine after a ten year absence to look for his mother. He found that she had been sold to Cliegg, so he, along with [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], visited the homestead. Lars introduced himself and Whitesun to the visitors, and when Skywalker asked about Shmi, Cliegg introduced himself, inviting the Jedi inside to talk. Cliegg told the [[Jedi]] about Shmi's kidnapping, telling the Jedi that she was [[Death|dead]]. Refusing to believe his stepfather, Skywalker borrowed Lars' [[swoop]] and tracked the Tusken Raiders. The next [[Standard day|day]], Skywalker returned with Shmi's corpse. The [[Lars family]] buried Shmi outside their home and held a quiet funeral. Following the funeral, Skywalker and Amidala left, and Lars never saw them again, but was left with the lasting impression that his step-brother was a wrathful and violent man, observing him to not be very much like his mother Shmi. However, seeing how well Owen and Whitesun worked together convinced Skywalker to [[Wedding of Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala|marry]] Amidala. After the wedding, although he was unsure if he wanted to go down the road of reaching out to his stepbrother, he also realized that Lars was the only person in his life whom he could ask for advice about married life. During an [[Mission to Zygerria|undercover mission]] to bring down the reborn [[Zygerrian Slave Empire]] in the ensuing [[Clone Wars]], Skywalker used{{TCW|Slaves of the Republic}} his stepbrother's name by pretending to be a slaver named "Lars Quell." Meanwhile, Lars' father was determined to continue the life he worked hard to create, but the tragedy weakened Cliegg, and he died soon after of a broken heart, leaving his farm and traditions to Lars. Soon after, Lars and Whitesun married, and together they toiled to maintain the farm. Owen and Beru decided to have a child, but problems of infertility precluded them to have one, leading them to consider seeing one of the [[fertility droid]]s at [[Mos Eisley]].{{StoryCite|story=Beru Whitesun Lars (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}} ===Raising Luke Skywalker=== [[File:Owen-Beru-sunset.png|thumb|right|300px|Beru and Owen Lars hold the infant Luke Skywalker and watch Tatooine's binary sunset.]] In [[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which includes [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] delivering [[Luke Skywalker]] to the [[Lars homestead|Lars moisture farm]], to [[19 BBY]]. Lars and his wife were contacted by [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], the [[Jedi Master]] who had trained Skywalker, and he tasked the couple with protecting Skywalker's infant son, [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]]. Although Lars was initially reluctant, Beru convinced him to adopt the child. When Kenobi arrived at the moisture farm, he presented Lars and Beru with the infant Skywalker, and the couple held their newly adopted child as they watched the [[Binary star system|binary sunset]] of Tatooine.{{Film|III}} Lars came to believe that his stepbrother had died and that Kenobi was responsible. However, in secret, Lars' stepbrother was alive, having turned to the [[dark side of the Force]], betraying the Jedi Order and becoming the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader. After delivering the child, Kenobi went into exile, changing his name to "Ben" and keeping watch over the young Skywalker. In an effort to protect Luke, Lars forbade Kenobi from training the boy and from visiting.{{Databank|owen-lars|Owen Lars}} Lars was still very reluctant to adopt his nephew knowing another mouth to feed was something they could barely handle as struggling farmers and the previous impression he had been left of Anakin, but given Beru was unable to have children naturally and she fervently wished for a family, he was convinced and grew to care for the boy. When Skywalker was seven years old, Lars found him alone, planning to watch a [[meteor shower]]. Fearing that his nephew could have been attacked by Tusken Raiders, Lars scolded him and then argued with Beru, stating he would keep the boy occupied with more chores. The following morning, Lars told Skywalker that he could not protect him all the time, and that he would teach him the safety basics of the farm. Then, to Beru and Skywalker's surprise, Lars revealed he planned to show him how to use a [[blaster]] rifle. Although Beru felt Skywalker was too young, Lars went forward with his plan to teach his excited nephew.[[Star Wars (LINE Webtoon)|''Star Wars'' LINE Webtoon]]: Chapter 1—"An Old Friend" ===Run-in with the Inquisitorius=== {{Quote|When the time comes, he must be trained.''"
"''Like you trained his father? Anakin is dead, Ben, and I won't let you make the same mistake twice.|Kenobi and Lars|{{Kenobi|Part I}}}} In [[9 BBY]],{{KenobiDate|I}} Lars and Skywalker were carrying out work at the homestead when they were observed from a distance by Kenobi, who left some spare parts for a [[Luke Skywalker's T-16 skyhopper model|toy T-16 skyhopper]] for Luke. Lars later confronted Kenobi in a stable in Anchorhead, tossing the toy parts on the ground and asking the Jedi to stay away from his family. When Kenobi reminded Lars that Skywalker must be trained when he grows up, the farmer reminded him of his failure to train Anakin Skywalker. As Lars left the stable, [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]] [[Fifth Brother]] and [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]]—hunting a supposed fugitive Jedi residing on Tatooine—arrived at the town square, with Lars caught in the ordeal. [[File:LarsInTrouble-KenobiPartI.png|thumb|left|300px|Lars is held at lightsaber-point by the Third Sister.]] After amputating the hand of an [[Unidentified Anchorhead woman|insubordinate woman]] with her [[Reva's lightsaber|lightsaber]], the Third Sister approached Lars, questioning him about his family and threatening to kill them unless someone in the town square provided information on the fugitive Jedi. As she held Lars at lightsaber-point, the Fifth Brother interfered and ordered the Third Sister to stand down. Afterward, Kenobi thanked Lars for not revealing anything about him or his whereabouts, with Lars retorting that it was not for him. Later, Owen and Luke visited a mechanic at Mos Eisley in order to obtain a new belt for their [[landspeeder]]. During the course of their visit, the shop owner assumed that Luke's uncle was a patient man, to which Owen emphasized that he was not patient.{{Kenobi|Part VI}} [[File:Owen-fires-at-Reva.png|thumb|Reva attacks Owen and Beru|300x300px]] Just then, [[Dardin Shull]] approached Owen and informed him that the Third Sister had inquired about Owen's whereabouts, as she was on the hunt to kill Luke. Horrified, Owen rushed back to the homestead, where he urged Beru to come inside. Once Owen had told Beru about the situation, he started to fret that they had to run, hide, and find help. However, to Owen's surprise, Beru retorted that the two of them were enough, then handed Owen a blaster. That night, as the Third Sister approached the homestead, Owen warned Luke that if anything went wrong, he needed to run from the Tusken Raiders, who Owen told Luke were on the attack. Reva soon entered the homestead, and Owen and Beru opened fire on the Inquisitor. She then faced Owen, who attacked her with a metal stick. The Third Sister pointed out that Owen loved Luke like he was his own, to which Owen pointed out that Luke was his own. The Third Sister eventually managed to defeat Owen, who called out to Beru that the Inquisitor was coming, prompting her to distract Reva long enough for Luke to escape. In the course of the skirmish, Kenobi returned to the homestead, where he found Owen and Beru frantically searching for their nephew. Soon enough, the Third Sister appeared and returned Luke to his aunt and uncle, having shown the boy mercy. The next day, as Owen worked at the homestead, Kenobi approached. Owen asked Kenobi was doing, as he had promised to keep his distance, and Kenobi replied that he had accept that Luke should be allowed to grow up as a normal boy instead of being trained as a Jedi. He went on to say that the only protectors Luke needed were Owen and Beru, and Owen said he would care of the boy. Kenobi then started to ride off into the desert, but Owen called out if Kenobi wanted to meet Luke. Kenobi accepted Owen's offer, then continued on his journey in the desert. ===The Great Drought and beyond=== {{Quote|I told you, I'm not gonna let you warp the boy like you did his father. You brought him to me to protect, and that's what I'm doing. Protecting him from ''you''.''"
"''I'm not asking to train the boy. You've made yourself quite clear on that matter. But Luke has potential to be something…truly remarkable. Just as his father was, before he—''"
"''Before you got him ''killed''! Haven't you murdered ''enough'' Skywalkers already, Kenobi?|Owen Lars and Obi-Wan Kenobi|}} While Skywalker was still a boy, Tatooine was plagued by the [[Great Drought]], which halted [[water]] collection for moisture farmers. During the drought, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], the [[Hutt]] [[crime lord]] of Tatooine, declared a [[water tax]], and he had his enforcers take the farmers' harvests, sometimes by force. However, unknown to Lars, Kenobi was protecting the Lars homestead from Jabba's thugs, so the family was never forced to pay. Still, the drought continued to worsen, and one night, Skywalker left the moisture farm to steal water from the Hutt's thugs. When Lars and Beru realized that Skywalker was missing, they searched for the boy, but they were unable to find him. Kenobi, however, sensed that Skywalker was in danger, and the Jedi found and rescued the boy, bringing him back to the homestead. In the morning, Beru found Skywalker, and called for her husband. Lars rushed to Skywalker's side, asking if he was all right. Skywalker, was unharmed, but he was unable to recall any of the previous night's events. About a [[Standard week|week]] later, the drought lifted, and the [[moisture vaporator]]s began collecting water again.[[Star Wars (2015) 7|''Star Wars'' (2015) 7]] [[File:OwenConfrontsKenobi-2015StarWars15.png|thumb|left|300px|Fearing that Kenobi will lead to Skywalker's death, Lars tells the Jedi to stay away from the boy.]] A year after the Great Drought's end, Skywalker took interest in [[pilot]]ing his family's [[T-16 skyhopper]], and during one adventurous flight, Skywalker became overconfident in his abilities, wrecking the skyhopper in [[Beggar's Canyon]]. Lars grounded Skywalker, enraged that they were short a speeder and could not afford repairs. When Skywalker suggested entering a race at Anchorhead and using prize money, Lars rejected the idea, telling Skywalker that he would never fly again. In the following days, Lars and Skywalker went to a market to purchase an [[astromech droid]] and a [[droid]] capable of speaking [[Bocce]]. While Lars was looking at droids, Skywalker was approached by two [[Jawa]]s, who handed him a box filled with the parts needed to repair the skyhopper. Skywalker believed it was a gift from his uncle, and the boy thanked him and rushed off; in actuality, the parts were from Kenobi, who believed that Skywalker needed more practice piloting. However, Lars immediately realized that Kenobi had interfered, also recalling the unusual absence of Tusken Raiders and Hutt thugs at the homestead. Furious, Lars visited [[Ben Kenobi's home|Kenobi's home]], bringing the skyhopper parts with him. Reasserting that he did not want Kenobi's help, Lars told the hermit to leave Skywalker alone, saying it was his own job to protect Skywalker, and that the Jedi was whom Skywalker needed protection from. Soon after, Lars purchased skyhoppper parts at [[Tosche Station]], hoping to fix the speeder with Skywalker and amend their strained relationship. However, when Lars returned home, the farmer was attacked by [[Krrsantan]], a [[Wookiee]] [[bounty hunter]] searching for the man who had defied Jabba's tax collectors the year before. Krrsantan took Lars to a clifftop near the [[Dune Sea]], where the Wookiee [[Stuncuffs|cuffed]] and beat the farmer with an electric baton, hoping to elicit a scream. Lars begged Krrsantan to stop, saying that he could not understand the [[Shyriiwook|Wookiee's language]] and was unable to answer his questions. The bounty hunter continued to attack until Kenobi appeared atop the cliff, revealing himself to be the man marked for [[bounty]]. Krrsantan immediately attacked Kenobi, quickly snaring the Jedi in a [[stun net]]. While Krrsantan's back was turned, Lars charged, but the Wookiee knocked him back, sending the farmer over the cliff edge. Lars caught himself on a protrusion from the cliff, hanging on as Kenobi summoned [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber|his lightsaber]], cutting the net and reengaging the Wookiee. Kenobi knocked the Wookiee over with [[the Force]] and turned his attention to rescuing Lars.[[Star Wars (2015) 20|''Star Wars'' (2015) 20]] [[File:OwenAndLuke-2015StarWars20.png|thumb|right|300px|Safe from the bounty hunter, Lars is reunited with Skywalker.]] However, Krrsantan quickly stood back up, grabbing a boulder and preparing to kill his target. Kenobi sliced the boulder in half, but one chunk fell and broke the rock which had been supporting Lars. The farmer began to fall, but he was saved by Kenobi, who held him through the Force. Kenobi struggled to concentrate on holding Lars and fending off the Wookiee, and the Jedi lost his grip on the farmer, who began to plummet toward the ground. As Lars fell, however, Skywalker who had repaired the skyhopper and went in search of his captured uncle—arrived, catching him on one of the skyhopper's [[cannon]]s. Skywalker landed the skyhopper and apologized, and Lars embraced his nephew, looking up to see Kenobi standing victorious on the clifftop. After the event, Lars and Kenobi never spoke, and they both returned to their homes. ===Proud uncle=== When Skywalker was twelve years old,''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' Beru compared Skywalker to his father after Lars noted he was proud of his nephew's hard work. Refusing to discuss Anakin any further, Lars told Beru that his nephew was like a son to him. Not wanting Skywalker to experience war in his lifetime, he admitted he would not let him join the Imperial Academy. Later that day, Skywalker and his friend [[Windy]] got lost in a [[sandstorm]] and encountered a [[krayt dragon]]. The two boys were saved by Kenobi, who took them back home. Lars thanked Kenobi for bringing Skywalker back safely, but again told the Jedi to stay away from the boy. In return, Kenobi revealed he had been observing Skywalker, informing Lars that the Force was strong in him and that he would leave the farm one day. Lars responded by saying that the Jedi went extinct with the [[Galactic Republic]], warning Kenobi to never visit the homestead again.[[Star Wars (LINE Webtoon)|''Star Wars'' LINE Webtoon]]: Chapter 2—"Meeting the Droids" ===Final days=== {{Quote|You know, I think that R2 unit we bought may have been stolen.''"
"''What makes you think that?''"
"''Well, I stumbled across a recording while I was cleaning him. He says that he belongs to someone named Obi-Wan Kenobi. I thought he might have meant old Ben. Do you know what he's talking about?''"
"''Mm.''"
"''I wonder if he's related to Ben.''"
"''That wizard's just a crazy old man. Now, tomorrow I want you to take that R2 unit to Anchorhead and have its memory erased. That'll be the end of it. It belongs to us now.|Luke Skywalker and Lars|}} [[File:Lars-buys-C3PO.png|thumb|left|300px|Lars and Skywalker purchase C-3PO from Jawas.]] In [[1 BBY]], a company of Jawas came by the homestead to sell miscellaneous droids. Lars, requiring an astromech droid and a droid capable of programming moisture vaporators, settled on purchasing the astromech droid [[R5-D4]] and the [[protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]], respectively. With the droids selected, Lars told Skywalker to clean them, despite the boy's plans of going to Tosche Station with his friends. However, Skywalker discovered that the [[R5 series astromech droid|R5 unit]] had a bad [[motivator]], and he informed his uncle. At the suggestion of C-3PO, Lars bought the astromech droid [[R2-D2]] in place of R5-D4. Later, while Skywalker was cleaning R2-D2, he discovered a [[Hologram|holographic]] message for "Obi-Wan Kenobi." Wondering if the droid was referring to Ben Kenobi, Skywalker asked his uncle during dinner. Lars replied that Kenobi was just a crazy old wizard, telling Skywalker to take the droid to Anchorhead and have its memory [[Memory wipe|erased]]. When Skywalker asked about the possibility of "Obi-Wan" coming to look for the droid, Lars denied the thought, telling Skywalker that the man had died around the same time as his father. The mention of his father piqued Skywalker's interest, and he asked if the man had known his father. Lars told Skywalker to forget it, telling his nephew to take care of the droids by morning. Thinking the droids would provide extra help on the farm, Skywalker, who desired to enroll in the [[Imperial Academy]] like his friends, asked Lars if he could join that year. Fearing that Skywalker was too much like his father, Lars denied his nephew's wish, stating that his help was still needed and that he could enroll in the following year. Disappointed, Skywalker left, leaving Lars and Beru to discuss if and when to let him join. [[File:Owen-Beru-burned.png|thumb|right|300px|The deaths of Lars and Beru prompted Skywalker to join the Rebellion.]] When the morning came, Lars could not find his nephew, so he asked his wife if she knew where he was. Beru believed that Skywalker was doing chores, but in actuality, Skywalker was searching for R2-D2, who had run off in search of Kenobi. Unknown to Lars, R2-D2 was carrying stolen [[Death Star plans|plans]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]], the [[Galactic Empire]]'s recently completed [[battle station]] capable of destroying entire planets. Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s, desperate to reclaim the data, traced the droid to the Lars homestead, where they proceeded to interrogate Lars and Beru. Failing to acquire the plans, the stormtroopers killed the couple, burning the home and leaving. When Skywalker returned, finding his family murdered and home in ruins, he decided to leave Tatooine with Kenobi and train to become a [[Jedi Knight]] like his father. The pair traveled to the [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]], where they met [[Han Solo]], a [[smuggler]] who agreed to take them to the planet [[Alderaan]] aboard the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|I guess it's an irony. If the boy was here when the jackboot came down, the Empire would still have a Death Star… But if the family wasn't killed, maybe he'd never have left.|Chelli Lona Aphra|[[Darth Vader (2015) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 7]]}} The deaths of Lars and Beru prompted Skywalker to leave Tatooine with Kenobi and join the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Upon joining the Rebels, Skywalker fought in the [[Battle of Yavin]], destroying the Death Star and becoming a Rebellion hero. Even beyond the realm of the living, Owen's wife Beru speculated that perhaps if Owen had allowed Luke to leave Tatooine sooner they could be still alive, but she ended up resting comfortably acknowledging what heroic actions Luke made after their deaths. Despite the recent loss of his family, Skywalker did not grieve until soon after the battle, when his love interest, [[Nakari Kelen]], was killed on the planet [[Omereth]]. Kelen's death provided Skywalker a moment to consider his losses, and he wept upon thinking of his aunt and uncle.''[[Heir to the Jedi]]'' Skywalker later returned to Tatooine to recover [[The Journals of Ben Kenobi|Kenobi's journal]], which contained stories of the Jedi's few encounters with the Lars family. In the weeks after the Battle of Yavin, Darth Vader searched for the pilot responsible for destroying the Death Star, discovering that the pilot was the son he never knew he had. Vader, accompanied by [[Doctor]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra]], revisited the abandoned homestead and followed Skywalker's trail. While assessing the destruction, Aphra speculated that Skywalker might have never left Tatooine, had his family been spared. As Luke never liked Lars' moisture farm and did not want to become a farmer, he eventually became a Jedi Knight like his father before him and eventually a Jedi Master following the [[Battle of Jakku|end]] of the Galactic Empire. However, after the [[Destruction of the Jedi Temple|destruction]] of his [[Jedi Order#A new generation|Jedi students]] at the hands of his nephew [[Ben Solo]], Luke went into [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] and temporarily became a farmer on the legendary planet [[Ahch-To]] of the [[First Jedi Temple]].''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]'' In [[34 ABY]], before the Force-sensitive [[scavenger]] [[Rey Skywalker|Rey's]] coming to Ahch-To, Skywalker had a [[dream]] about an alternate life where he ignored Organa's message and never joined the rebellion, remaining in the moisture farming business with Owen and getting married to his friend [[Camie Marstrap]]. In his dream, Skywalker, afraid of Owen's fury, retrieved [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]] earlier than he had. Owen also was taken by the stormtroopers to be interrogated, but released three days later, though remained silent and pale during the long ride back from Mos Eisley.''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]'' ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Beru, you know Luke is like a son to me. You know that I will do anything to keep you and Luke safe.|Owen Lars, to Beru Lars|[[Star Wars (LINE Webtoon)|''Star Wars'' LINE Webtoon]]}} [[File:AnakinClieggOwen-AotC.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Influenced by his father's teachings and his stepbrother's adventures, Lars could be strict and harsh.]] Lars was a male human with [[Color|light]] skin and blue [[eye]]s, and he stood at a height of 1.7 [[meter]]s (5 [[Foot|feet]], 7 inches). He had dark brown [[hair]] in his youth, and it turned gray with age. As his stepmother Shmi Skywalker recounted, the young Lars was a pragmatic and strong worker, who was also thankful for life's simple delights. The son of Cliegg, Lars was raised in the traditions of discipline and hard work, and taught this to his nephew. Lars was gruff and strict with the boy. As soon as Luke was able to hold a hydrospanner, he put him to work, and his nephew began to learn to fix vaporators, clean garden filters, and keep machinery working far past its prime from an early age.''[[Skywalker: A Family at War]]'' There was often tension between Lars and Skywalker, which forced Beru to mediate. Due to his Uncle's impatience, Skywalker could be fearful of his fury and reactions, something which he even dreamed about during his exile. Despite having a complicated relationship with his nephew, and initially reluctant to take him in, he still grew to care for him in his own gruff way. When the Third Sister attacked the Lars moisture farm, she noted that Lars loved Luke, like he was his own; Lars replied that Luke ''was'' his own.{{Kenobi|Part VI}} Feeling great disdain towards the Jedi Order, Lars believed that Kenobi had warped Anakin's mind into leaving Shmi on Tatooine, an act he considered to be unimaginable. Lars also held Kenobi responsible for the deaths of Shmi and Anakin (whom was believed to have died), believing that the Jedi's actions had torn the family apart. When Kenobi left Skywalker under Lars' reluctant protection, the farmer told the Jedi to stay away from them, fearing that Kenobi would create similar consequences with the boy. Despite his feelings about Kenobi, Lars helped him fight the Wookiee Krrsantan, which the Jedi viewed as an act of bravery, and Lars allowed Kenobi to meet with Skywalker when he allowed his nephew to grow like a normal child. To keep Skywalker out of trouble, Lars kept his nephew's Jedi lineage a secret, claiming that Skywalker's father was simply a [[navigator]] on a [[spice]] [[freighter]]. When Luke desired to leave Tatooine, Lars found it difficult to ignore his gruff, protective attitude, which had become a habit over the years. Kenobi believed Lars was a proud man, so he feared the farmer would rather fight than pay the protection money Jabba the Hutt demanded. The Jedi Master thought this would be a foolish choice, especially after he promised to raise Luke, though he also realized Lars was smart enough to know when to fight his battles.{{StoryCite|story=Time of Death|book=From a Certain Point of View}} Lars was not much given to expressing affection in words, but often did small things for Beru, surprising kindnesses that would cause her to smile and her eyes to light up. Lars spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard]]. However, he did not know how to speak [[Shyriiwook]], the language of the Wookiees, something which nearly costed him his live at the hands of Black Krrsantan, if not for Obi-Wan Kenobi's lucky intervention. ==Equipment== {{Quote|What I really need is a droid who understands the binary language of moisture vaporators.''"
"''Vaporators? Sir, my first job was programming binary loadlifters—very similar to your vaporators in most respects.|Lars and C-3PO|}} [[File:Lars_Homestead_ITW.png|thumb|right|300px|A cutaway of Lars' homestead]] In his youth, Lars owned a red [[Zephyr-G swoop]] bike, which Anakin used while searching for Shmi. Later in life, Lars acquired an inexpensive [[V-35 Courier]],{{Databank|v-35-landspeeder|V-35 Landspeeder}} and he allowed Skywalker to pilot a [[T-16 skyhopper]] and an old, battered [[X-34 landspeeder]]{{Databank|x-34-landspeeder|X-34 Landspeeder}} in which he kept a [[blaster rifle]]. In his work, Lars used an [[SX-14 Field Hover-Ute]], and he constantly maintained numerous [[GX-8 water vaporator|GX-8 Moisture Vaporators]] throughout the farm. To conserve power and [[Star|solar]] radiation, Lars would shut the farm down each night, only leaving on perimeter [[sensor]]s to warn him of approaching Tusken Raiders or dangerous [[Species|fauna]]. To assist in Lars' work, he owned an R5 astromech droid, a [[WED 15 "Septoid 2" Treadwell toolkit droid]], and a [[Standard century|centuries]]-old [[EG-6 power droid]] among others,[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] which were destroyed when the Galactic Empire razed the home. Lars dressed in rough [[clothing]] made in Anchorhead, also wearing a tool pouch and a simple overcoat to provide warmth on cold desert evenings. ==Behind the scenes== ===Creation and portrayal=== [[File:Owen-OP.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Joel Edgerton portrayed young Owen Lars.]] Owen Lars first appeared in the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which was written and directed by [[George Lucas]]. In ''A New Hope'', Lars was portrayed by [[Phil Brown]] and credited as "Uncle Owen". Historically, Lars was first mentioned in the [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough draft]] of ''A New Hope'', in which he and Beru were anthropologists working on [[Yavin 4|Yavin]]. In the film's second draft, titled ''[[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars]]'', Lars and Beru were rewritten to be the guardians of [[twin]]s [[Biggs Darklighter|Biggs]] and [[Windy]] Starkiller, and it was in this draft that Lars and Beru became the uncle and aunt of Luke Skywalker. In the second draft, Lars was also a Jedi, and it was not until the third draft, ''[[The Star Wars: From The Adventures of Luke Starkiller]]'', that Lars became a farmer.''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]'' Lars' origins as an anthropologist were a self-reference by Lucas, who had intended to study anthropology at [[Wikipedia:San Francisco State University|San Francisco State University]] before he switched to cinematography.''[[The Cinema of George Lucas]]'' Later, the screenplay for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] also revealed that Lars and Ben Kenobi were brothers, although the idea was removed from the script's final cut.''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' In [[2002]], a younger Lars, portrayed by [[Joel Edgerton]], appeared in the film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], the second installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]]. Lucas casted Edgerton as Owen for the film.{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/obi-wan-kenobi-first-look-photos|text=See exclusive first-look photos from ''Obi-Wan Kenobi''|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2022-03-09|archivedate=20220311122528}} [[Canon]]ically, ''Attack of the Clones'' is the first time Lars' name is mentioned in full. In [[2005]], Edgerton returned to the role for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], the prequel trilogy's conclusion,. Other than Brown and Edgerton, Lars has been portrayed by [[Charles Howerton]], who voiced the character in the young readers book [[A New Hope Read-Along Storybook and CD|''Episode IV: A New Hope Read-Along Storybook and CD'']],[[A New Hope Read-Along Storybook and CD|''A New Hope'' Read-Along Storybook and CD]] and [[Michael Donovan]], who voiced Lars in "[[Mission to Mos Eisley (episode)|Mission to Mos Eisley]]," an episode of the non-canon television show ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales]]''.{{DroidTales|Mission to Mos Eisley (episode)}} While shooting Episode II in [[Tunisia]], Edgerton filmed a scene for Episode III in which he is delivered the infant Luke by Obi-Wan, played by a stand-in actor rather than [[Ewan McGregor]], as Lucas did not desire to return to Tunisia for that single shot years later. However, the scene was changed during the Episode III shoot in [[September]] [[2003]], where McGregor playing Kenobi was filmed handing baby Luke to [[Bonnie Maree Piesse]] playing Beru, this time with Owen being played by a stand-in as Lucas "felt it would be better if Luke were handed over to a woman". Edgerton still appears in the scene, thanks to a specially-filmed chroma key shot that was added in post-production.''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]'' {{Top}} {{MultipleIssues|image|updatecontent=[[Thrawn: Treason]], [[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]], [[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]], [[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]], [[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]}} {{Character |type=Galactic Empire |image=[[File:GovernorPryce-TotOR2023.png]] |name=Arihnda Pryce |homeworld=[[Lothal]][[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']] |birth=Between [[49 BBY|49]]–[[45 BBY]]According to [[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']], Arihnda Pryce was in her mid-thirties when the events of the novel began. The [[Del Rey]] timeline places ''Thrawn'' between ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' and [[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']]. ''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' dates [[Kanan Jarrus]] and [[Hera Syndulla]]'s first meeting in ''A New Dawn'' to six years before ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', which according to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'', begins in [[5 BBY]]. This places ''A New Dawn'' in [[11 BBY]]. ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' dates the prologue of ''Solo: A Star Wars Story'' to six years after the [[Proclamation of the New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], which ''Star Wars: Galactic Atlas'' dates to [[19 BBY]], therefore ''Solo: A Star Wars Story'' must begin in [[13 BBY]]. This means that ''Thrawn'' must begin between 13 BBY and 11 BBY. If Pryce was in her mid-thirties during those years, it can be calculated that she was born between [[49 BBY]] and [[45 BBY]]. |death=[[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' [[Imperial Complex (Lothal)|Imperial Complex]], Lothal{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} |species=[[Human]] {{C|[[Lothalite]]}}{{Rebels|Steps Into Shadow}} |gender=[[Gender|Female]]''[[Star Wars: Women of the Galaxy]]'' |pronouns=She/her |height=1.74 [[meter]]s{{EncyclopediaCite|Imperial Officers and Agents}} |mass= |hair=[[Color|Black]] |feathers= |eyes=Blue |skin=Pale |cyber= |families=[[Pryce family]] |parents=*[[Talmoor Pryce]] *[[Elainye Pryce]] |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Pryce Mining]] *[[Higher Skies Advocacy Group]] *[[Galactic Empire]]''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' **[[Imperial Officer Corps]] **[[Lothal garrison]] **[[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|7th Fleet]] {{C|briefly}}{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|I serve the Empire until the end.|Governor Pryce's last words|}} '''Arihnda Pryce''' was a [[Lothalite]] [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who served as the [[Galactic Empire]]'s imperial [[Governor]] of the [[planet]] [[Lothal]] under the jurisdiction of [[Moff]] [[Stattata]]. Deceitful and opportunistic, Pryce rose to political power and gained the position of [[Planetary Governor]] through underhanded tactics and power plays. Under Pryce's governorship, Lothal became a center for Imperial expansion and industrialization. Pryce's Imperialization of Lothal gave rise to a [[Phoenix Cell|small rebellion]] on the planet, and her subsequent failures to foil this uprising gave way to a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|larger rebellion]] against the Empire. Pryce's destructive tendencies would be her undoing, and after a series of desperate attempts to defeat the rebels, she was [[Death|killed]] when they successfully [[Liberation of Lothal|liberated]] Lothal from her grip. [[Reproduction|Born]] and [[Homeworld|raised]] on Lothal, Arihnda Pryce was the heir and manager of her family's local [[mining]] business, [[Pryce Mining]]. After selling the company to the Galactic Empire, she began serving as an [[aide]] to Lothal [[Senator]] [[Domus Renking]] and became involved with the political elite of [[Coruscant]], while her parents relocated to [[Batonn]]. She was dismissed from her position, however, when she became entangled in a plot between Renking and Moff [[Ghadi]]. Working for a [[Proam Avenue Citizen Assistance|citizen assistance office]] shortly after, she joined the [[Higher Skies Advocacy Group]]. During this time, she allied with key figures such as Governor [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] and a rising [[Imperial Navy|Navy]] [[officer]], [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]], and began plotting to make her bid for power. In a series of betrayals and deceptions, Pryce engineered the downfalls of Moff Ghadi, her friends at Higher Skies, Lothal Governor [[Ryder Azadi]], and Senator Renking. Using her power as leverage, she petitioned and was appointed the Governorship of Lothal, taking Azadi's place. As Governor of Lothal, Pryce presided over the expansion of the Empire's presence on Lothal, which became a major Imperial base in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. Shortly after Pryce assumed the title, the nearby system of Batonn came under [[Batonn sector insurgency|insurgent threat]]. Under the pretense of gathering intelligence, Pryce traveled to the planet to rescue her parents. Pryce murdered [[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] [[Agent]] [[Gudry]] while trying to flee with her parents, and, to conceal her role in his murder, she detonated a [[Creekpath Mining and Refining complex|mining facility]], [[Siege of the Creekpath Mining and Refining complex|destroying]] the [[Batonn insurgents|insurgent forces]] and resulting in heavy civilian casualties. After escaping suspicion, she returned to Lothal to deal with the planet's growing rebellion, led by the [[Phoenix Cell]]. To help combat the rebels, Governor Pryce solicited [[Grand Admiral]] Thrawn to help ferret out and destroy them. Pryce joined Thrawn and ISB Agent [[Alexsandr Kallus|Kallus]] in combating the rebel presence in the Lothal sector. During the course of the insurgency, she worked to root out dissent on Lothal, took part in an unsuccessful [[Operation Handoff|hunt]] for rebel leader [[Mon Mothma]], and participated in the [[Battle of Atollon]], where Thrawn laid siege to Phoenix Cell's [[Chopper Base|base]]. As the small rebellion grew into the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and entered [[Galactic Civil War|war]] with the Empire, Lothal was strip-mined and industrialized further under Pryce. The rebel cell originating from Lothal, the [[Spectres]], returned to Lothal to free the planet from Pryce and the Empire. After defending against a [[Attack on Lothal|rebel attack]], Pryce [[Rescue of Hera Syndulla|destroyed]] the [[Lothal City fuel depot]], killing rebel leader [[Kanan Jarrus]] but falling out of favor with Thrawn, whose [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter|projects]] relied on the planet's resources. Terrified of what her punishment would be, Pryce mounted a desperate attack on the [[Lothal resistance group|Lothal resistance's]] [[Lothal cliff dwelling|base]]. Her attack failed, however, and she was taken captive. Pryce was killed during the [[Liberation of Lothal|final battle]] between the rebellion and Thrawn's [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|forces]], remaining loyal to the Empire until the end. ==Biography== ===Early life=== Arihnda Pryce was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Lothal]]. [[Reproduction|Born]] around [[49 BBY|49]]–[[45 BBY]], Arihnda was the daughter of [[Elainye Pryce]] and [[Talmoor Pryce]]. The [[Pryce family|family]] owned a [[Pryce Mine|mine]] on Lothal that was located on land shared by the [[Planetary Governor|Governor]] of the Lothal [[Ryder Azadi]]. She grew up a quiet life, which the [[Lothalite]] enjoyed as a child, watching the sunset and the laughter of children from all [[species]] and backgrounds playing. Pryce's early life was quite active with many social activities including dance recitals and school debates, many of which were recorded by her proud and loving parents. Although her upbringing had been happy and full, as Pryce grew older and life transitioned into the pressures and responsibilities of adulthood, she began to resent the quiet and dullness of the open spaces for lacking culture and excitement. Regarding Lothal as boring, Pryce sought to escape to more cosmopolitan worlds, where excitement and bright lights existed alongside what she regarded as "sophisticated people." Her [[Parent|father]] Talmoor eventually discovered a source of [[doonium]], a precious metal used in the manufacture of [[starship]] [[hull]]s and something valued by the expanding [[Imperial Navy]]. When Arihnda came of age, she inherited her father's [[mining]] company [[Pryce Mining]]. ===The Imperial takeover=== {{Quote|If you would consider selling the governor another 21 percent of Pryce Mining…"
"What? Absolutely not. You're not getting a controlling interest.|Arihnda Pryce turns down Arik Uvis' offer|[[Thrawn 3|''Thrawn'' 3]]}} [[File:ArihndaJustSayNo-Thrawn3.png|thumb|left|150px|Arihnda refuses Uvis' offer.]] When Pryce was in her mid-thirties, Azadi, then the [[Governor]] of Lothal, sought access to Pryce Mining's doonium mines. He sent one of his staffers [[Arik Uvis]] to buy another 21 percent stake in the company, giving him a controlling interest. However, Pryce rejected the offer. In retaliation, Governor Azadi's office framed Arihnda's mother Elainye for embezzlement. After learning the news from her father Talmoor, Pryce visited the police station only to learn that her mother's bail request had been denied and that she had not been allowed to receive visitors. She later conferred with Talmoor and realized that Uvis was behind her mother's trumped up charges. In desperation, Pryce sought the help of Lothal's [[Senator]] [[Domus Renking]]. Senator Renking agreed to help Pryce's mother by shifting the blame onto the [[Lutrillian]] heavy equipment inventory operations manager [[Pomi Harchmak]]. To prevent Azadi from taking over the company, Renking persuaded Pryce to sign over the rights of her company to the Empire. As compensation, he found Pryce's parents new jobs as the assistant manager and foreman of the [[Creekpath Mining and Refining complex]] on the planet [[Batonn]]. Renking also secured Pryce a new job as a staff member at [[Lothalian citizen assistance office|one]] of his [[citizen assistance office]]s on [[Coruscant]]. With little choice, Pryce accepted Renking's terms and sold Pryce Mining to the Empire. Following the meeting, Pryce spent three hours remonstrating with her parents about the opportunity they were given while warning of the dangers if they refused. While she was helpless in the past, she convinced them that she would help them in the future. In the end, Pryce's parents agreed to leave their home and relocate to Batonn. ===Serving Senator Renking=== {{Quote|Ah, Arihnda! I'd hoped to run into you. This is Arihnda Pryce, one of my aides. Ms. Pryce, this is Colonel Wullf Yularen of the ISB, Senior Lieutenant Thrawn, a rising star in the navy and Ensign Eli Vanto, the lieutenant's aide.|Senator Renking|}} On Coruscant, Arihnda Pryce developed a reputation as a tough and effective civilian assistance officer who lobbied for the interests of Lothalian expatriates on the galactic capital. On one occasion, Pryce confronted the landlady [[Chesna Braker]] for neglecting to repair a leaking pipe in one of her tenant [[Daisie]]'s apartment blocks. Following a tense argument, Braker reluctantly agreed to fix Daisie's leaking pipe after Pryce reminded her to comply with Coruscant laws and regulations. [[File:ImperialBallAlisandreHotel-Thrawn3.png|thumb|right|250px|Pryce attends an Imperial ball at the Alisandre Hotel during Ascension Week.]] In return for her services, Senator Renking took advantage of a new program encouraging senators to fund supplementary citizen assistance offices to provide Pryce with a managerial job at his fifth new office in the [[Bartanish Four Sector]]. This new job came with an apartment two blocks and six levels away from her workplace. Unlike her previous positing, this new office was open to all [[Coruscanti]] citizens.
