As Omega grew to be an adult, she learned of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Galactic Civil War|fight]] against the Empire.<ref name="Cavalry" /> At some point between [[2 BBY]] and [[4 ABY]],<ref name="RebelDate">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance]] to [[2 BBY]]. ''Timelines'' also dates the Rebel Alliance's reorganization into the [[New Republic]] to [[4 ABY]]. Therefore, the epilogue of "The Cavalry Has Arrived" must take place between 2 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]] and 4 ABY.</ref> she decided to answer the Rebellion's calls for new [[Rebel pilot|fighter pilots]]. One night, she prepared to leave Pabu, sneaking down to the cavern where her ship was docked. As she turned on the lamps that illuminated the cavern, she was surprised to see Hunter and Batcher waiting for her. Hunter smiled at her and told her that despite his aging, he could sense that she was trying to sneak off. Omega smiled, saying that he should not be surprised and that she needed to do more to help. Hunter countered that they wanted to keep her safe, and Omega said that they had already done that, reminding him that she was not a kid anymore. Hunter smiled sadly and said that she would always be their kid, and that even if she was ready, he was not. The two embraced, with Omega telling him to keep an eye on Wrecker and Crosshair while she was gone. As Omega also said goodbye to Batcher, Hunter told her that they would always be there for her if she needed them. As she powered up her [[Omega's ship|ship]], with Gonky in tow. Preparing for takeoff, Omega saluted to Hunter, who returned the gesture before Omega flew off to join the Rebellion,<ref name="Cavalry" /> which she successfully joined.<ref name="Quiz 227">{{InsiderCite|227|Jedi Master's Quiz}}</ref>

===Legacy===
The [[pirate]] [[Hondo Ohnaka]] recounted Omega's role in the battle between Bane and Shand in his book ''[[The Secrets of the Bounty Hunters]]'', mentioning the young girl whose bounty the two hunters were fighting over.<ref name="Secrets of the Bounty Hunters">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Bounty Hunters]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|She is my medical assistant. One with a curious mind that causes her to wander.|Nala Se|<ref name="Aftermath" />}}
[[File:OmegaGalaxyOfHeroes.png|thumb|left|180px|Omega was an unmodified clone who had a curious mind.]]
Aside from her gender, Omega was an unmodified clone, a pure replica of the original clone template Jango Fett,<ref name="Bounty Lost" /> who had spent her entire life on Kamino until she joined the Bad Batch and escaped.<ref name="Aftermath" /> From a young age, the Kaminoans identified Omega as special due to her independent thinking skills and ability to act on them.<ref name="Children">{{InsiderCite|225|Children of the Galaxy (article)}}</ref> Although she was a child, Tech noted that she had a heightened state of awareness.<ref name="Aftermath" /> According to her, she had no behavioral modification biochip.<ref name="Battle Scars" /> Nala Se was very protective of her, often telling her to stay close by. However, she was not a rule follower and was very curious, investigating the Bad Batch's quarters when they left on a mission.<ref name="Aftermath" /> Before joining the Bad Batch, Omega's constant companion was Nala Se. She had a special relationship with the Kaminoan, who always tried to take care of her.<ref name="Confined" /> Nala Se hired Shand to stop Lama Su from capturing Omega and using her for new cloning technology.<ref name="Bounty Lost" /> Even as the Empire held them hostage on Tantiss, Nala Se looked out for Omega, trying to prevent her involvement in the Empire's research<ref name="Confined" /> and helping her escape when she was in trouble.<ref name="Shadows" />

Omega was compassionate,<ref name="Aftermath" /> boundlessly<ref name="Kamino Lost Declassified">{{SW|url=news/bad-batch-declassified-kamino-lost|text=''Bad Batch'' Declassified: 5 Highlights from "Kamino Lost"}}</ref> empathetic,<ref name="Aftermath" /> optimistic, and determinedly positive.<ref name="Harbinger" /> She quickly took a liking to the Bad Batch, looking up to the squad and even copied some of their mannerisms. On Kamino, she repeating Hunter's gestures while sitting next to him<ref name="Aftermath" /> and, onboard the ''Marauder'', tried using one of Crosshair's toothpicks like him.<ref name="Infiltration" /> During the Bad Batch's brief imprisonment on Kamino, she consoled Crosshair even though he had made a snide remark about her earlier. As the group tried to make its escape, she saved Wrecker's tooka doll Lula for him amidst the battle. Although she had no combat experience,<ref name="Aftermath" /> Omega was a fast learner, quickly becoming skilled with blasters,<ref name="Aftermath" /><ref name="Shadows" /> an energy bow, which was her weapon of choice,<ref name="Rampage" /> and hand-to-hand combat.<ref name="Confined" /> Through her time with the Bad Batch, she became a skilled combatant<ref name="Databank">{{Databank|omega|Omega}}</ref> and picked up a lot of skills from them. Echo was responsible for helping her practice with her new energy bow.<ref name="Rampage" /> Wrecker instructed her on how to disassemble and defuse explosives.<ref name="Reunion" /> After being instructed by Tech, she became a capable pilot.<ref name="Tipping Point" /> Tech also made her memorize the Bad Batch's various battle plans, which Omega was able to do.<ref name="Shadows" /> Hunter and Tech both made her study every ship in the Imperial fleet, with Hunter personally quizzing her and Tech making sure she remained diligent with her studies.<ref name="Spoils" /> She was extremely skilled with electronics and technology,<ref name="Comprehensive">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> growing to become even more capable with tools, showcased by her ability to perform maintenance on Gonky.<ref name="War-Mantle" /> Although she had many skills, Omega was also impulsive, rash, and easily frustrated. She was impatient in many occasions, preferring to act instead of wait.<ref name="Comprehensive" /> Coupled with her intelligence,<ref name="Databank" /> resourcefulness,<ref name="Common Ground" /> determination, bravery, and strategic thinking, she was a formidable member of the squad.<ref name="Databank" />

[[File:OmegaEyesSparkle-Aftermath.png|thumb|250px|Omega was dazzled when experiencing hyperspace for the first time]]
Having spent her entire life in Kamino, Omega had never known anything but the facilities of the Kaminoans and the oceans of Kamino. She was naïve to many of the galaxy's intricacies. She was quick to trust strangers, which got her into some trouble on Pantora when she trusted Fennec Shand,<ref name="Cornered" /> although this friendliness was also helpful during the Bad Batch's mission to Corellia, when Omega quickly became friendly with Trace Martez.<ref name="Decommissioned" /> As the group traveled the galaxy to various planets, she was new to many of the things she saw, from the markets on Ord Mantell<ref name="Rampage" /> and Pantora<ref name="Cornered" /> to even simple things like sunshine and dirt. She was excited by seeing and experiencing new things, becoming fascinated by the soil, plants, and butterflies on Saleucami<ref name="Cut and Run" /> and insisting on accompanying Hunter to the [[central marketplace]] when they stopped on Pantora for a resupply so she could see the city.<ref name="Cornered" /> Her strong moral compass allowed her to see through dogma. Omega questioned the ways of the galaxy on multiple occasions.<ref name="Children" /> She was unaware of the phenomenon of slavery until educated on the subject by Tech and Echo and could not believe that it was an accepted practice.<ref name="Rampage" /> She was very skilled with strategy games, helping Cid make money playing dejarik while the other members of the Bad Batch carried out a mission to Raxus.<ref name="Common Ground" /> While on the run with Crosshair, she was able to hustle over thirty-thousand credits off of various opponents by beating them in balaans.<ref name="Different" />

As Omega became accustomed to her new life with the Bad Batch, she proved eager to be involved and be a contributing member of the group. She would adopt the action-oriented style of her brothers as well as the clipped and direct ways of speaking that reflected a regimented soldier. As her sense of wonder grew, so did her capabilities,<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|216|The Best of the Batch}}</ref> and as Omega continued to experience new adventures, she became more and more aware of her potential.<ref name="Children" /> Despite her initial inexperience, her enthusiasm proved useful as she learned to carry out missions with the squad.<ref name="Replacements" /><ref name="Rampage" /> She felt a sense of duty to help others around them,<ref name="Rescue on Ryloth" /> consistently advocating for the squad to intervene when someone needed help.<ref name="Comprehensive" /> When she was left behind when the rest of the Bad Batch traveled to Raxus, she was visibly disappointed to be left out.<ref name="Common Ground" /> She always spoke up when Hunter wanted to leave her out of missions in an effort to protect her.<ref name="The Return" /><ref name="BT" /> Over time, Hunter came to share Omega's readiness to assist those in need.<ref name="Comprehensive" />

[[File:OmegaWreckerMantellMix-BS.png|thumb|left|300px|Omega and Wrecker snacked together after every mission]]
Omega grew very close to each of her brothers in the squad. Although they were a team of soldiers, they were also Omega's family,<ref name="The Crossing" /> with the ''Marauder'' being their home.<ref name="Retrieval" /> Although she once teased Crosshair about being her "little brother," she looked up to all of them.<ref name="The Return" /> Wrecker's fun-loving personality<ref name="War-Mantle" /> and big heart<ref name="Insider" /> gave her a playful companion. During their time on Ord Mantell, she and Wrecker formed a tradition where they snacked on Mantell Mix after every mission.<ref name="Battle Scars" /> The two also played board games together during down time.<ref name="War-Mantle" /> She had a strong relationship with Hunter, the first member of the squad to really connect with her,<ref name="Replacements" /> and who acted as a parental guardian towards her.<ref name="Reunion" /> She admired Echo and shared a close bond with him as well.<ref name="Comprehensive" /> Omega very sorrowful when he left to join Rex's operation.<ref name="Truth and Consequences" /> She struggled with his departure and was both frustrated and saddened by the changes going on around her, not understanding how the other members of the squad, especially Tech, seemed so unbothered by his absence. She eventually had a conversation with Tech and came to understand that they all felt the weight of their changing circumstances, but processed and expressed that differently.<ref name="The Crossing" /> When Crosshair returned to the squad following his time with the Imperial Army, Omega was intentional about looking out for him. Although she was grateful to be back with Hunter and Wrecker, she took time to try and help Crosshair readjust. Hunter in particular did not fully trust Crosshair upon his return, but Omega was much more trusting and tried to encourage Crosshair to talk to Hunter so they could become on better terms. When Crosshair and Hunter argued, Omega wanted to step in and help, although Echo told her to stay back and let the two clones work it out.<ref name="The Return" /> Her bond and loyalty to her brothers only grew over time.<ref name="Insider" /> As much as each member of her squad were her brothers, they were also parental figures to her.<ref name="Cavalry" /> Additionally, she was close with AZI-3, who was a companion for her on Kamino and remained present after leaving the planet.<ref name="Comprehensive" />

[[File:TruthandConsequences-TBB208.png|thumb|right|275px|Omega was a friendly and positive person]]
During her many adventures with the Bad Batch, Omega enjoyed meeting new people.<ref name="Cut and Run" /> Despite Cid's gruffness and eventual betrayal, the Trandoshan had a soft spot for Omega.<ref name="Common Ground" /> She enjoyed the company of other young people like herself, getting along with Shaeeah and Jek Lawquane,<ref name="Cut and Run" /> bonding with Lyana Hazard,<ref name="Pabu" /> and quickly developing a friendship with the young pilot Hera Syndulla, enjoying her appreciation for flying.<ref name="Devil's Deal" /> She was fascinated by Phee Genoa's stories and tales,<ref name="Entombed" /> being very excited by treasure.<ref name="Ruins" /><ref name="Entombed" /> Upon meeting Benni Baro, Omega trusted him to help the squad even though he had previously stolen their ship. She was also willing to share [[ration bar|rations]] with the boy when she realized that the miners were underfed.<ref name="The Crossing" /> When Omega was detained in Tantiss for a second time, she was quick to care for the fellow child prisoners, Eva, Jax, Sami, and Bayrn. She was supportive, kind, and helped to inspire hope that they could escape together.<ref name="Breach" /> She also enjoyed being around animals, bonding with a [[zardimallo]] [[lizard]] and naming it Ruby.<ref name="Comprehensive" /> On Pabu, she laughed when a [[Moonyo|moon-yo]] jumped onto her shoulder.<ref name="Pabu" /> In general, Omega understood people<ref name="Insider" /> and saw the best in them. She was quick to trust, forming a rapport with Trace and Rafa Martez almost right away<ref name="Decommissioned" /> and trying to see the good in Emerie Karr even though Karr was helping oversee her imprisonment.<ref name="Shadows" /> She was also very forgiving. Even as Crosshair became their enemy, Omega still treated him as her brother and wanted him to come home.<ref name="Kamino Lost" /> Although Crosshair saw her optimism as misguided and Royce Hemlock considered her idealism to be a weakness,<ref name="Confined" /> Omega used her compassionate traits to help wherever she could.<ref name="Databank" />

When Asajj Ventress located Omega on Pabu, she wanted to trust the former Sith apprentice despite her brothers told her about her actions during the Clone Wars. She felt strongly about taking the opportunity to try and discover if she had a high M-count, saying that she had to know what she was. Crosshair thought her trusting Ventress was naive, but Omega convinced the others to give Ventress a chance when she reminded them that people could change, and that she had never given up on Crosshair. She was excited by the notion that she could be a Force-sensitive, but was frustrated by the fact that she did not know how to approach the abstract nature of the tests.<ref name="Harbinger" />

As Omega reached adulthood, she felt the need to join the Rebel Alliance, wanting to do more to help the galaxy. Although the rest of her squad were done fighting, having survived through the Clone Wars and made peace with leaving the life of a soldier behind, Omega wanted to choose her own cause to fight for. Although Hunter did not want her to leave, he ultimately let her go and allowed her to make her own path through life, giving to Omega something he and the clones of the Grand Army of the Republic had never had during the war and still had trouble with even after the end of the conflict.<ref name="Cavalry" />

Omega regarded the ''Marauder'' as home and was upset when Tech insinuated that the ship was merely a mode of transportation after it was stolen on Ipsidon.<ref name="The Crossing" /> When the Batch prepared to leave Pabu, Omega told Lyana that the Pabu had been the first place that felt like home to her.<ref name="Point of No Return" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|I get my own comm device?''"<br />"''Technically, it was Crosshair's, but he doesn't appear to be needing it.|Omega expressed excitement as Tech outfits her with a comlink|<ref name="Rampage" />}}
[[File:OmegaTBBS2-DoRTVG.png|left|thumb|357x357px|Omega practicing with her bow.]]
During her time on Kamino, Omega wore a white tunic with red-and-blue sleeves, black pants, and black [[boot]]s. She had a Kaminoan-style forehead pendant which she wore in her hair,<ref name="Aftermath" /> although she removed it and altered her hairstyle after escaping Saleucami.<ref name="Cut and Run" /> Her overall outfit reflected that of Nala Se. During the mission to Ord Mantell, Tech provided her with a [[Wrist comm|wrist-mounted communicator]], which had formerly been Crosshair's. When the wrist comm was destroyed by Cad Bane on Bora Vio<ref name="Bounty Lost" /> she was provided with a standard [[comlink]].<ref name="Rescue on Ryloth" /> On the same mission she had been given the wrist comm, she acquired a retractable Zygerrian energy bow<ref name="Rampage" /> that she went on to use in combat.<ref name="Bad Batch Trailer" /> However, she was quite ineffective using the weapon at first due to not being practiced or strong enough to shoot straight.<ref name="Decommissioned" /> In time, she became skilled with the weapon.<ref name="Plan 99" /> Echo later gifted her a modified [[energy crossbow]] on Teth, which Omega was thankful to receive.<ref name="Infiltration" />

[[File:Omega-TBBs2.png|thumb|right|200px|Omega's regular outfit during her adventures]]
Omega would eventually leave behind the simple tunic of Kamino and wear a red shirt, a blue jacket, a brown bandolier and belt, gray pants, and brown boots. During missions, she frequently wore a<ref name="Spoils" /> speeder courier helmet<ref name="Dawn Guide" /> and sometimes carried a backpack.<ref name="Spoils" /> As Omega's hair grew out, she wore a small ponytail.<ref name="Confined" /> After being rescued from Tantiss Base and returning to Pabu, Omega was outfitted with a pale green shirt, a knit green sweater vest, and a simple necklace.<ref name="The Return" /> She later wore a white shirt with a brown jacket.<ref name="BT" /> As an adult, Omega had a jacket that was orange and tan denim fabric with slightly reflective yellow shoulders. The jacket included a patch on the right shoulder that depicting the black and red Bad Batch emblem. Her thin blue pants were synthetic spacesuit material. She had black boots and also wore gloves.<ref name="Older Omega">{{Twitter|StarWars|status/1851702254488748177|Star Wars|quote=if you’re still finishing up your #TheBadBatch costume, here are the details you’ve been waiting for! #LucasfilmAnimation}}</ref> Finally, Omega carried a brown bag,<ref name="Cavalry" /> had an orange pendant around her neck, and a red bandana in her hair.<ref name="Older Omega" />

During her time on Pantora, Omega ended up taking a clone trooper doll without paying for it.<ref name="Cornered" /> She considered the toy trooper to be a female like herself, painting its armor black to make the doll a member of the Bad Batch.<ref name="Rampage" /> For Omega, the doll was not only one of her only playthings and a comfort to her when she was scared, but a connection to her past life on Kamino as well as her new life with the Bad Batch.<ref name="Doll DB">{{Databank|clone-trooper-doll|Clone Trooper doll}}</ref> She also co-owned Wrecker's [[tooka doll]], [[Lula]],<ref name="Replacements" /> sleeping with it on occasion.<ref name="The Return" />

By the time she left Pabu to join the Rebellion, Omega had her own [[Omega's ship|ship]], which included several mementos of her squad aboard. Tech's goggles sat in the cockpit, while Lula sat in a seat located in the ship's cabin.<ref name="Cavalry" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Development and early seasons===
{{Quote|The interesting challenge was: How do you challenge a super soldier? And what can you throw at them that's something that they're not equipped to deal with? That's how the idea of Omega came to be. Soldiers can figure things out, but what they've never had to deal with is a young kid. And that completely changes how they relate to one another and changes their perspective on the galaxy... You drop them into a Separatist battlefront and they're going to be fine no matter what. But having to be guardians and be responsible for the upbringing and rearing of a child is something totally different.|Jennifer Corbett, ''The Bad Batch'' head writer|<ref name="Corbett Interview">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-bad-batch-jennifer-corbett-interview|text="How Do You Challenge A Super Soldier?": Jennifer Corbett On Helping The Clones In ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Find Their Way|date=2021-06-23}}</ref>}}
Omega was created for the [[2021]] [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]''. She was first revealed on [[March 30]] of that year in a trailer for the show which gave the character's name in the closed captioning.<ref name="Bad Batch Trailer">{{SWYouTube|BsOmYpP4UDU|Star Wars: The Bad Batch | Official Trailer | Disney+|sw_url=video/trailer-the-bad-batch}}</ref> Her first appearance was in the series premiere, "[[Aftermath (episode)|Aftermath]]." She is voiced by [[Michelle Ang]],<ref name="Aftermath" /> who was delighted to be a part of the Star Wars universe. She had originally auditioned for a role in the [[2017]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars:'' Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']], the second installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[sequel trilogy]]. and was heartbroken when she did not get the part. Admittedly, she did not realize she was auditioning for a ''Star Wars'' project when she tried out, but was delighted when she learned she was finally entering the ''Star Wars'' universe, and felt the satisfaction of having come full circle. When recording her lines, Ang did much of the work from her own home as opposed to being in the recording studio, noting that it was much more comfortable that way and that it allowed her to be more physical in her performance.<ref name="Meet Omega">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-bad-batch-omega-michelle-ang-interview|text=Meet Omega: Michelle Ang on Becoming the Heart of ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch''}}</ref> For the final recording session, Ang joined her co-star [[Dee Bradley Baker]] in the studio at Lucasfilm headquarters. Ang felt lucky to be working alongside Baker, saying she felt that they both agreed on morality being important to their characters and to the show overall. Baker agreed, asserting Omega was the moral compass and the character that powered the story.<ref name="Finale Interview">{{SW|url=news/the-bad-batch-series-finale-dee-bradley-baker-michelle-ang-interview|text=''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Comes to a "Spectacular Finish"}}</ref>

[[File:MichelleAng.jpg|thumb|right|225px|Michelle Ang, who voices Omega.]]
Throughout the series, Ang's approach to Omega evolved. In later seasons, Ang did not pitch her voice up as much to reflect Omega's growing maturity, which she felt was also complemented by thoughtfulness from the writers when constructing her dialogue.<ref name="Soldier and Survivor">{{SW|url=news/michelle-ang-interview-the-bad-batch-season-2|text=Soldier and Survivor: Michelle Ang on Omega's Story in ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch''}}</ref> In season one, she was not shy about suggesting changes to the script during script-readings, wanting to emphasize Omega's child-like perspective whenever possible. Many conversations were had about how to balance Omega's cheeky or sassy sides with her "grown-upness."<ref name="Meet Omega" /> In season two, Ang and director [[Brad Rau]] described the evolution of Omega's personality as growing into "Good Soldier Omega," which entailed more clipped, direct ways of speaking and less of the excessive expressiveness. Ang also noted that as much as she drew on her own life experiences in the recording booth, her son was also a big inspiration to her portrayal of Omega's youthful confidence and newfound audaciousness.<ref name="Soldier and Survivor" /> Although she did not feel like her son was old enough to enjoy or appreciate the show in the beginning, when he was only four years old,<ref name="Meet Omega" /> as he grew, they began to watch the episodes together each week.<ref name="Soldier and Survivor" />

Rau acknowledged Omega's relationship with the other members of the Bad Batch as being both a sibling bond<ref name="Look Back" /> as well as a parental bond, thinking of the other clones as both Omega's brothers in one sense and her dads in another.<ref name="Empire is Everywhere">{{SW|url=news/the-bad-batch-interview-jennifer-corbett-brad-rau|text="The Empire Is Everywhere": The Creators of ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' on The Long Road Ahead in Season 2}}</ref> Baker also acknowledged this complexity in their relationship.<ref name="Buckle Up">{{SW|url=news/dee-bradley-baker-bad-batch-season-2-interview|text="Buckle Up": Dee Bradley Baker on What's to Come in ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' Season 2}}</ref> The creators took care to spend time on Omega's relationship with each of her brothers individually. While the show's [[The Bad Batch Season 1|first season]] spent more time on Omega's connection with Hunter and Wrecker, the [[The Bad Batch Season 2|second season]] delved more into Omega's relationships with Echo and Tech.<ref name="Empire is Everywhere">{{SW|url=news/the-bad-batch-interview-jennifer-corbett-brad-rau|text="The Empire Is Everywhere": The Creators of ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' on The Long Road Ahead in Season 2}}</ref> Finally, the [[The Bad Batch Season 3|third season]] showcased the dynamic between Omega and Crosshair.<ref name="Look Back" />

The music that became [[Omega's Theme]] was originally written by [[Sean Kiner]], who collaborated with [[Kevin Kiner|Kevin]] and [[Deana Kiner]] on the show's score. Kiner noted that he was inspired by the birth of his daughter, a moment that he drew from to create the sense of hope and optimism in the theme. The track's original B section eventually became the main A section.<ref name="Kiners">{{WookYouTube|9xrcKowBNQM|Wookieepedia talks with the Kiner brothers, with a surprise guest!|date=2021-09-01|old=1}} {{C|Begins at 33m33s}}</ref>

Omega's introduction to the [[2015]] [[EA Capital Games]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''<ref name="SWGOH">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref> was teased in a forum post on [[July 13]], 2021, following the release of the show's first season.<ref name="Forum Post">{{EA|subdomain=forums.galaxy-of-heroes.starwars|url=discussion/247069/kit-reveal-omega|text=Kit Reveal: Omega}}</ref> Later, another version of the character inspired by the latter two seasons of ''The Bad Batch'', Omega (Fugitive), was revealed on [[January 15]], [[2025]].<ref name="Kit Reveal">{{EA|url=games/starwars/galaxy-of-heroes/news/kit-reveal-omega|text=Kit Reveal: Omega (Fugitive)}}</ref>

===Season three finale===
{{Quote|We weren't set on exactly how it was going to end. There were sort of some exploration, but as an actor, an emotional moment was the ending we landed on. It was like the culmination of my journey as a performer and Omega's journey as a character all consolidated into, two lines.|Michelle Ang|<ref name="Omega Season 3">{{WebCite|url=https://theholofiles.com/2024/02/13/exclusive-interview-omega-actress-michelle-ang-talks-star-wars-the-bad-batch-season-3-asajj-ventress-the-series-finale|text=EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW: Omega Actress Michelle Ang Talks 'Star Wars: The Bad Batch' Season 3, Asajj Ventress, & the Series Finale|author=George and Josh Bate|archivedate=20240213234307}}</ref>}}
Due to her history with the show and her character, it was difficult for Ang to even open the script for the series finale. Ang promised the series finale would be very sentimental<ref name="Omega Season 3" /> and satisfying.<ref name="Behind the Geeks">{{YouTube|video=92bzWaGUlp8|text=Behind The Geeks | Interview with Michelle Ang voice of Omega from Star Wars: The Bad Batch Season 3|channel=wearegeekcentric|name=Geekcentris|date=2024-01-19}}</ref> She further promised that Omega's final moments on screen had a great gravity to them, thereby culminating "everything" at play in a bittersweet ending. In one interview, she also revealed Omega originally had a different ending, which would have opened the door for her to have a very important future in the overall ''Star Wars'' galaxy, but it was changed "from there" into the bittersweet ending.<ref name="Omega Season 3" /> All the same, she expressed in another interview her hopes that Omega's story would have larger ramifications on the ''Star Wars'' galaxy and even open a door for her to appear in a live action production, which was where she mainly did acting work.<ref name="Behind the Geeks" />

[[File:BadBatchFamily-CharPoster-TBBS3.jpg|thumb|left|180px|The final Bad Batch character poster, released the same day as the series finale]]
Rau noted that Omega's role in the series finale was comparable to Hunter's role in the Bad Batch—explaining that "Hunter-Omega" was forced to lead, be calm, and take charge in order to help the other imprisoned children. Rau felt it was a full-circle moment for the character and was impressed by Ang's ability to portray Omega in these scenes. The show's co-creator and head writer [[Jennifer Corbett]] felt that it was a good parallel to the [[Aftermath (episode)|first episode]] of the show, where the Bad Batch had to rescue Omega themselves. In this episode, Omega, using all her training, was able to break out and help the other children escape without needing help from her squad.<ref name="Look Back">{{SW|url=news/the-bad-batch-series-end-interview|text=Brad Rau and Jennifer Corbett Look Back on ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch''}}</ref>

While the epilogue scene was always in the minds of the show's creators, the actual events of the scene were always in flux. Corbett noted discussions about the epilogue happened as early as Season 1, but the final version of the scene was not nailed down until Season 3. Each member of the team felt they had a certain connection to the scene, with Corbett noting how personal it felt as a parallel to her own choice to join the military and Rau comparing it to the bittersweet emotions of sending two kids off to college.<ref name="Look Back" /> Ang also felt that Omega's journey was a reflection of her own personal journey. She felt it was important for Omega to emerge from the story as resilient and ready to start a new chapter, choosing a life that she felt compelled to live. Ang ultimately used something closer to her normal voice for the epilogue scene.<ref name="Finale Interview" />

===Contradictions===
{{SWKidsYouTube|a8pt85FAJuc|8 of the Best Buddies in Star Wars | Star Wars: List It!}} states that Omega is around the same age as [[Shaeeah Lawquane|Shaeeah]] and [[Jek Lawquane]]. {{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode210.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Deserter}} states that Jek was four and Shaeeah was five [[Standard year|years]] old during the events of "[[The Deserter]]." {{TCWcanondates|210}} However, as the [[2002]] film {{Film|II}}, the second installment of the ''Star Wars'' [[prequel trilogy]], establishes that the [[Cloning|clones]] of [[Jango Fett]] required a [[Standard decade|decade]] of growth to reach adulthood, and ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch'' portrays Omega as being older than the other members of [[Clone Force 99]], who were adults by [[19 BBY]], this seems to be in conflict with previous sources. Moreover, the statement regarding Omega's age may not have been intended literally, and the ''[[Star Wars: List It!]]'' series of videos has since been removed from [[StarWarsKids.com]]. Therefore, this article does not assume the statement to establish an exact [[Standard year|year]] of Omega's birth.
